reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century, perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the scope and seriousness of their arts coverage. It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers. Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews. To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-circulation dailies. We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an ornament to the publications in which it appeared. In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered. Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about. These men believed in journalism as a calling, and were proud to be published in the daily press. "So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism," Newman wrote, "that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are'." Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten. Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket. During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England's foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller. He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored. Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to specialists. Is there any chance that Cardus's criticism will enjoy a revival? The prospect seems remote. Journalistic tastes had changed long before his death, and postmodern readers have little use for the richly upholstered Vicwardian prose in which he specialized. Moreover, the amateur tradition in music criticism has been in headlong retreat.

paragraphs.en: Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century, perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the scope and seriousness of their arts coverage.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去二十五年间英语报纸发生的所有变化中,影响最为深远的或许是其艺术报道范围和严肃性不可阻挡的衰落。

paragraphs.en: It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers. Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews. To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-circulation dailies.
paragraphs.zh: 对于四十岁以下的普通读者来说,很难想象甚至根本无法想象曾经有那么一个时代,在大多数大城市报纸上都能找到高质量的艺术评论。然而,二十世纪出版的最重要的评论文集中,有相当数量在很大程度上都是由报纸评论构成的。今天阅读这些书籍,会惊叹于这样一个事实:它们那些博学的内容曾经被认为适合在面向大众发行的日报上发表。

paragraphs.en: We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an ornament to the publications in which it appeared. In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered. Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about. These men believed in journalism as a calling, and were proud to be published in the daily press. "So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism," Newman wrote, "that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are'."
paragraphs.zh: 我们距离二十世纪之交至第二次世界大战前夕在英国出版的那种不拘一格的报纸评论则更为遥远,那时新闻纸极其廉价,而时髦的艺术评论被视为刊登它的出版物的一种装饰。在那些遥远的日子里,人们理所当然地认为主要报纸的评论家会详尽而长篇地撰写他们所报道的事件。这是一项严肃的事业,即使是那些展现学识时举重若轻的评论家,如George Bernard Shaw和Ernest Newman,也可以信赖他们知道自己在做什么。这些人相信新闻业是一种使命,并为能在日报上发表文章而自豪。Newman写道:"很少有作者拥有足够的头脑或足够的文学天赋来在新闻业中保持自己的水准,以至于我忍不住将'新闻业'定义为'不被人阅读的作家用来贬低被人阅读的作家的一个蔑称'。"

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten. Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket. During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England's foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller. He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored. Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to specialists.
paragraphs.zh: 不幸的是,这些评论家实际上已被遗忘。Neville Cardus从1917年起为曼彻斯特卫报撰稿,直到1975年去世前不久,如今他仅仅作为一位撰写板球运动散文的作家为人所知。然而在他的有生之年,他也是英国最重要的古典音乐评论家之一,其文体广受赞誉,以至于他的《自传》(1947)成为畅销书。他于1967年被授予爵士头衔,是第一位获此殊荣的音乐评论家。然而,他的著作中现在只有一本还在印行,他关于音乐的大量著述除了专业人士外已无人知晓。

paragraphs.en: Is there any chance that Cardus's criticism will enjoy a revival? The prospect seems remote. Journalistic tastes had changed long before his death, and postmodern readers have little use for the richly upholstered Vicwardian prose in which he specialized. Moreover, the amateur tradition in music criticism has been in headlong retreat.
paragraphs.zh: Cardus的评论有可能重获新生吗?这种前景似乎很渺茫。早在他去世之前,新闻业的品味就已经改变,而后现代读者对他所擅长的那种华丽繁复的维多利亚-爱德华时代风格的散文几乎不感兴趣。此外,音乐评论中的业余传统一直在急剧退却。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Over the past decade, thousands of patents have been granted for what are called business methods. Amazon.com received one for its "one-click" online payment system. Merrill Lynch got legal protection for an asset allocation strategy. One inventor patented a technique for lifting a box. Now the nation's top patent court appears completely ready to scale back on business-method patents, which have been controversial ever since they were first authorized 10 years ago. In a move that has intellectual-property lawyers abuzz, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit said it would use a particular case to conduct a broad review of business-method patents. In re Bilski, as the case is known, is "a very big deal," says Dennis D. Crouch of the University of Missouri School of Law. It "has the potential to eliminate an entire class of patents." Curbs on business-method claims would be a dramatic about-face, because it was the Federal Circuit itself that introduced such patents with its 1998 decision in the so-called State Street Bank case, approving a patent on a way of pooling mutual-fund assets. That ruling produced an explosion in business-method patent filings, initially by emerging Internet companies trying to stake out exclusive rights to specific types of online transactions. Later, more established companies raced to add such patents to their files, if only as a defensive move against rivals that might beat them to the punch. In 2005, IBM noted in a court filing that it had been issued more than 300 business-method patents, despite the fact that it questioned the legal basis for granting them. Similarly, some Wall Street investment firms armed themselves with patents for financial products, even as they took positions in court cases opposing the practice. The Bilski case involves a claimed patent on a method for hedging risk in the energy market. The Federal Circuit issued an unusual order stating that the case would be heard by all 12 of the court's judges, rather than a typical panel of three, and that one issue it wants to evaluate is whether it should "reconsider" its State Street Bank ruling. The Federal Circuit's action comes in the wake of a series of recent decisions by the Supreme Court that have narrowed the scope of protections for patent holders. Last April, for example, the justices signaled that too many patents were being upheld for "inventions" that are obvious. The judges on the Federal Circuit are "reacting to the anti-patent trend at the Supreme Court," says Harold C. Wegner, a patent attorney and professor at George Washington University Law School.

paragraphs.zh: 对商业方法专利申请的限制将是一个戏剧性的转变,因为正是联邦巡回法院本身在1998年对所谓的State Street Bank案的判决中引入了此类专利,批准了一项关于共同基金资产汇集方式的专利。该裁决导致商业方法专利申请激增,最初是新兴互联网公司试图为特定类型的在线交易争取独占权。后来,更多老牌公司竞相将此类专利纳入其档案,哪怕只是作为针对可能抢先一步的竞争对手的防御性举措。2005年,IBM在一份法庭文件中指出,尽管它质疑授予此类专利的法律依据,但已获得超过300项商业方法专利。同样,一些华尔街投资公司用金融产品专利武装自己,尽管它们在法庭案件中采取反对这种做法的立场。

The judges on the Federal Circuit are "reacting to the anti-patent trend at the Supreme Court," says Harold C. Wegner, a patent attorney and professor at George Washington University Law School.

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: In his book The Tipping Point, Malcolm Gladwell argues that "social epidemics" are driven in large part by the actions of a tiny minority of special individuals, often called influentials, who are unusually informed, persuasive, or well connected. The idea is intuitively compelling, but it doesn't explain how ideas actually spread. The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the "two-step flow of communication": Information flows from the media to the influentials and from them to everyone else. Marketers have embraced the two-step flow because it suggests that if they can just find and influence the influentials, those select people will do most of the work for them. The theory also seems to explain the sudden and unexpected popularity of certain looks, brands, or neighborhoods. In many such cases, a cursory search for causes finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention. Anecdotal evidence of this kind fits nicely with the idea that only certain special people can drive trends. In their recent work, however, some researchers have come up with the finding that influentials have far less impact on social epidemics than is generally supposed. In fact, they don't seem to be required at all. The researchers' argument stems from a simple observation about social influence: With the exception of a few celebrities like Oprah Winfrey – whose outsize presence is primarily a function of media, not interpersonal, influence – even the most influential members of a population simply don't interact with that many others. Yet it is precisely these non-celebrity influentials who, according to the two-step-flow theory, are supposed to drive social epidemics, by influencing their friends and colleagues directly. For a social epidemic to occur, however, each person so affected must then influence his or her own acquaintances, who must in turn influence theirs, and so on; and just how many others pay attention to each of these people has little to do with the initial influential. If people in the network just two degrees removed from the initial influential prove resistant, for example, the cascade of change won't propagate very far or affect many people. Building on this basic truth about interpersonal influence, the researchers studied the dynamics of social influence by conducting thousands of computer simulations of populations, manipulating a number of variables relating to people's ability to influence others and their tendency to be influenced. They found that the principal requirement for what is called "global cascades" – the widespread propagation of influence through networks – is the presence not of a few influentials but, rather, of a critical mass of easily influenced people.

paragraphs.en: In his book The Tipping Point, Malcolm Gladwell argues that "social epidemics" are driven in large part by the actions of a tiny minority of special individuals, often called influentials, who are unusually informed, persuasive, or well connected. The idea is intuitively compelling, but it doesn't explain how ideas actually spread.
paragraphs.zh: 在《引爆点》一书中，Malcolm Gladwell认为，"社会流行"在很大程度上是由极少数特殊个体的行为所驱动的,这些人通常被称为影响者,他们异常见多识广、极具说服力或人脉广泛。这个观点在直觉上很有说服力,但它并不能解释思想实际上是如何传播的。

paragraphs.en: The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the "two-step flow of communication": Information flows from the media to the influentials and from them to everyone else. Marketers have embraced the two-step flow because it suggests that if they can just find and influence the influentials, those select people will do most of the work for them. The theory also seems to explain the sudden and unexpected popularity of certain looks, brands, or neighborhoods. In many such cases, a cursory search for causes finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention. Anecdotal evidence of this kind fits nicely with the idea that only certain special people can drive trends.
paragraphs.zh: 影响者的所谓重要性源于一个听起来合理但基本未经检验的理论,称为"传播的两级流动":信息从媒体流向影响者,再从他们流向其他所有人。营销人员欣然接受两级流动理论,因为它表明,如果他们能找到并影响这些影响者,那些被选中的人就会为他们完成大部分工作。该理论似乎也解释了某些造型、品牌或街区突然且出人意料的流行。在许多此类情况下,对原因的粗略搜寻会发现,某个小群体在其他任何人关注之前就在穿着、推广或开发这些东西。这类轶事证据很好地契合了只有某些特殊的人才能引领潮流的观点。

paragraphs.en: In their recent work, however, some researchers have come up with the finding that influentials have far less impact on social epidemics than is generally supposed. In fact, they don't seem to be required at all.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,在他们最近的研究中,一些研究人员得出了这样的发现:影响者对社会流行的影响远低于普遍认为的程度。事实上,他们似乎根本不是必需的。

paragraphs.en: The researchers' argument stems from a simple observation about social influence: With the exception of a few celebrities like Oprah Winfrey – whose outsize presence is primarily a function of media, not interpersonal, influence – even the most influential members of a population simply don't interact with that many others. Yet it is precisely these non-celebrity influentials who, according to the two-step-flow theory, are supposed to drive social epidemics, by influencing their friends and colleagues directly. For a social epidemic to occur, however, each person so affected must then influence his or her own acquaintances, who must in turn influence theirs, and so on; and just how many others pay attention to each of these people has little to do with the initial influential. If people in the network just two degrees removed from the initial influential prove resistant, for example, the cascade of change won't propagate very far or affect many people.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员的论点源于对社会影响力的一个简单观察:除了像Oprah Winfrey这样的少数名人——她们超大的影响力主要是媒体的作用,而非人际影响——即使是人群中最有影响力的成员也不会与那么多其他人互动。然而,恰恰是这些非名人影响者,根据两级流动理论,应该通过直接影响他们的朋友和同事来推动社会流行。但是,要发生社会流行,每个受影响的人必须继而影响他或她自己的熟人,而这些熟人又必须影响他们的熟人,如此等等;而这些人中的每一个究竟有多少其他人关注,与最初的影响者关系不大。例如,如果社交网络中与最初影响者相隔两度的人被证明具有抵抗力,那么变化的级联就不会传播很远,也不会影响很多人。

paragraphs.en: Building on this basic truth about interpersonal influence, the researchers studied the dynamics of social influence by conducting thousands of computer simulations of populations, manipulating a number of variables relating to people's ability to influence others and their tendency to be influenced. They found that the principal requirement for what is called "global cascades" – the widespread propagation of influence through networks – is the presence not of a few influentials but, rather, of a critical mass of easily influenced people.
paragraphs.zh: 基于这个关于人际影响的基本事实,研究人员通过对人群进行数千次计算机模拟来研究社会影响的动态,操纵了与人们影响他人的能力和被影响倾向相关的若干变量。他们发现,所谓"全局级联"——影响力通过网络的广泛传播——的主要要求不是少数影响者的存在,而是大量易受影响的人达到临界数量。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Bankers have been blaming themselves for their troubles in public. Behind the scenes, they have been taking aim at someone else: the accounting standard-setters. Their rules, moan the banks, have forced them to report enormous losses, and it's just not fair. These rules say they must value some assets at the price a third party would pay, not the price managers and regulators would like them to fetch. Unfortunately, banks' lobbying now seems to be working. The details may be unknowable, but the independence of standard-setters, essential to the proper functioning of capital markets, is being compromised. And, unless banks carry toxic assets at prices that attract buyers, reviving the banking system will be difficult. After a bruising encounter with Congress, America's Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) rushed through rule changes. These gave banks more freedom to use models to value illiquid assets and more flexibility in recognizing losses on long-term assets in their income statements. Bob Herz, the FASB's chairman, cried out against those who "question our motives." Yet bank shares rose and the changes enhance what one lobbying group politely calls "the use of judgment by management." European ministers instantly demanded that the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) do likewise. The IASB says it does not want to act without overall planning, but the pressure to fold when it completes its reconstruction of rules later this year is strong. Charlie McCreevy, a European commissioner, warned the IASB that it did "not live in a political vacuum" but "in the real world" and that Europe could yet develop different rules. It was banks that were on the wrong planet, with accounts that vastly overvalued assets. Today they argue that market prices overstate losses, because they largely reflect the temporary illiquidity of markets, not the likely extent of bad debts. The truth will not be known for years. But banks' shares trade below their book value, suggesting that investors are skeptical. And dead markets partly reflect the paralysis of banks which will not sell assets for fear of booking losses, yet are reluctant to buy all those supposed bargains. To get the system working again, losses must be recognized and dealt with. America's new plan to buy up toxic assets will not work unless banks mark assets to levels which buyers find attractive. Successful markets require independent and even combative standard-setters. The FASB and IASB have been exactly that, cleaning up rules on stock options and pensions, for example, against hostility from special interests. But by giving in to critics now they are inviting pressure to make more concessions.

Today they argue that market prices overstate losses, because they largely reflect the temporary illiquidity of markets, not the likely extent of bad debts. The truth will not be known for years. But banks' shares trade below their book value, suggesting that investors are skeptical. And dead markets partly reflect the paralysis of banks which will not sell assets for fear of booking losses, yet are reluctant to buy all those supposed bargains.
paragraphs.zh: 是银行处在错误的星球上,它们的账目大大高估了资产价值。如今它们辩称市场价格夸大了损失,因为这些价格主要反映的是市场暂时的非流动性,而不是坏账可能达到的程度。真相要多年后才能知晓。但银行股价低于其账面价值,这表明投资者持怀疑态度。而市场停滞在一定程度上反映了银行的瘫痪状态,它们因害怕账面亏损而不愿出售资产,却又不愿购买所有那些所谓的便宜货。

paragraphs.en: To get the system working again, losses must be recognized and dealt with. America's new plan to buy up toxic assets will not work unless banks mark assets to levels which buyers find attractive. Successful markets require independent and even combative standard-setters. The FASB and IASB have been exactly that, cleaning up rules on stock options and pensions, for example, against hostility from special interests. But by giving in to critics now they are inviting pressure to make more concessions.
paragraphs.zh: 要让这个体系重新运转起来,必须承认并处理损失。美国收购不良资产的新计划不会奏效,除非银行将资产标记到买家认为有吸引力的水平。成功的市场需要独立甚至敢于对抗的准则制定者。FASB和IASB一直正是如此,例如在面对特殊利益集团的敌意时,它们清理了股票期权和养老金方面的规则。但现在向批评者让步,它们是在招致压力做出更多让步。

It did not [6] what was done in the experiment; [7] something was changed, productivity rose. A(n) [8] that they were being experimented upon seemed to be [9] to alter workers' behavior [10] itself.
paragraphs.zh: 这一观点的产生是因为工厂中女工们令人困惑的行为。根据实验记录,当照明增强时她们的小时产量上升,但照明变暗时产量也上升。实验中做什么并不重要;只要有什么东西被改变了,生产率就会上升。意识到自己正在被实验似乎本身就足以改变工人的行为。

When work started again on Monday, output [16] rose compared with the previous Saturday and [17] to rise for the next couple of days. [18] , a comparison with data for weeks when there was no experimentation showed that output always went up on Mondays. Workers [19] to be diligent for the first few days of the week in any case, before [20] a plateau and then slackening off. This suggests that the alleged "Hawthorne effect" is hard to pin down.
paragraphs.zh: 事实证明,进行实验的特殊方式可能导致了对所发生情况的误导性解读。例如,照明总是在星期日改变。当星期一重新开始工作时,与之前的星期六相比产量如期上升,并在接下来的几天里继续上升。然而,与没有进行实验的几周数据比较显示,产量在星期一总是上升。无论如何,工人们往往在一周的头几天勤奋工作,然后达到平稳状态,接着松懈下来。这表明所谓的"霍桑效应"难以确定。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst, Beautiful Inside My Head Forever, at Sotheby's in London on September 15th 2008. All but two pieces sold, fetching more than £70m, a record for a sale by a single artist. It was a last victory. As the auctioneer called out bids, in New York one of the oldest banks on Wall Street, Lehman Brothers, filed for bankruptcy. The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003. At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm – double the figure five years earlier. Since then it may have come down to $50 billion. But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, enormous egos, greed, passion and controversy in a way matched by few other industries. In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst's sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable. In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms. Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008. Within weeks the world's two biggest auction houses, Sotheby's and Christie's, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placed works for sale with them. The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989. This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant. But Edward Dolman, Christie's chief executive, says: "I'm pretty confident we're at the bottom." What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market. Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell. The three Ds – death, debt and divorce – still deliver works of art to the market. But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.

questions.explanation: 第 25 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）Art Market in Decline 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989. ↔ Art Market in Decline）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、B 项属以偏概全、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst, Beautiful Inside My Head Forever, at Sotheby's in London on September 15th 2008. All but two pieces sold, fetching more than £70m, a record for a sale by a single artist. It was a last victory. As the auctioneer called out bids, in New York one of the oldest banks on Wall Street, Lehman Brothers, filed for bankruptcy.
paragraphs.zh: 一个世纪以来艺术市场历史上最长的牛市以戏剧性的方式结束，2008年9月15日，Damien Hirst的56件作品在伦敦苏富比以"Beautiful Inside My Head Forever"为题进行拍卖。除两件作品外全部售出，成交额超过7000万英镑，创下单一艺术家作品拍卖的纪录。这是最后的胜利。就在拍卖师喊出竞价时，华尔街最古老的银行之一雷曼兄弟在纽约申请破产。

paragraphs.en: The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003. At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm – double the figure five years earlier. Since then it may have come down to $50 billion. But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, enormous egos, greed, passion and controversy in a way matched by few other industries.
paragraphs.zh: 全球艺术市场在2003年以来令人眩目的上涨之后,已经失去动力有一段时间了。研究公司Arts Economics的创始人Clare McAndrew估计，艺术市场在2007年达到顶峰时价值约650亿美元——是五年前数字的两倍。此后可能已降至500亿美元。但这个市场引发的关注远超其规模，因为它以少数其他行业难以匹敌的方式汇聚了巨额财富、膨胀的自我、贪婪、激情和争议。

paragraphs.en: In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst's sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable. In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms. Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008. Within weeks the world's two biggest auction houses, Sotheby's and Christie's, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placed works for sale with them.
paragraphs.zh: 在Hirst先生拍卖后的数周和数月里，任何形式的消费都变得极不合时宜。在艺术界，这意味着收藏家远离画廊和拍卖行。当代艺术品销售额下降了三分之二，在最过热的领域，截至2008年11月的一年中销售额下降了近90%。几周之内，全球两大拍卖行苏富比和佳士得不得不向委托他们出售作品的客户支付近2亿美元的担保金。

paragraphs.en: The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989. This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant. But Edward Dolman, Christie's chief executive, says: "I'm pretty confident we're at the bottom."
paragraphs.zh: 艺术市场当前的低迷是自1989年底日本人停止购买印象派作品以来最严重的一次。这次专家估计价格平均比峰值下降了约40%，尽管有些作品的波动要大得多。但佳士得首席执行官Edward Dolman说："我相当确信我们已经触底了。"

paragraphs.en: What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market. Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell. The three Ds – death, debt and divorce – still deliver works of art to the market. But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，这次衰退与上次的不同之处在于市场上仍然有买家。几乎所有接受本特别报道采访的人都表示，目前最大的问题不是需求不足，而是缺乏可供出售的优质作品。三个D——死亡、债务和离婚——仍在向市场输送艺术品。但任何不必出售的人都在观望，等待信心回归。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room – a women's group that had invited men to join them. Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch. Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them. This man quickly nodded in agreement. He gestured toward his wife and said, "She's the talker in our family." The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt. "It's true," he explained. "When I come home from work I have nothing to say. If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the whole evening in silence." This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home. And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage. The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s. Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed – but only a few of the men – gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces. Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United States every year – a virtual epidemic of failed conversation. In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements. Instead, they focused on communication: "He doesn't listen to me." "He doesn't talk to me." I found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives. In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.

paragraphs.en: I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room – a women's group that had invited men to join them. Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch. Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them. This man quickly nodded in agreement. He gestured toward his wife and said, "She's the talker in our family." The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt. "It's true," he explained. "When I come home from work I have nothing to say. If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the whole evening in silence."
paragraphs.zh: 我正在弗吉尼亚州郊区一间起居室里对一小群人发言——一个邀请了男性参加的女性团体。整个晚上,有一位男士特别健谈,频繁地提出想法和讲述轶事,而他的妻子则静静地坐在他旁边的沙发上。临近晚会结束时,我评论说女性经常抱怨她们的丈夫不与她们交谈。这位男士很快点头表示赞同。他朝他妻子做了个手势,说道:"她才是我们家里爱说话的人。"房间里爆发出一阵笑声;那位男士看起来既困惑又受伤。"这是真的,"他解释道,"当我下班回家时我没什么可说的。如果不是她让谈话继续下去,我们整个晚上都会在沉默中度过。"

paragraphs.en: This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home. And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage.
paragraphs.zh: 这一插曲凸显了一个讽刺现象:尽管美国男性在公共场合往往比女性说得更多,但他们在家里却常常说得更少。而这种模式正在对婚姻造成严重破坏。

paragraphs.en: The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s. Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed – but only a few of the men – gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces. Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United States every year – a virtual epidemic of failed conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 这种模式是政治学家Andrew Hacker在20世纪70年代末观察到的。社会学家Catherine Kohler Riessman在她的新书《离婚访谈》中报告说,她采访的大多数女性——但只有少数男性——把缺乏沟通作为离婚的原因。鉴于目前近50%的离婚率,这相当于美国每年有数百万案例——实际上是一场对话失败的流行病。

paragraphs.en: In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements. Instead, they focused on communication: "He doesn't listen to me." "He doesn't talk to me." I found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives.
paragraphs.zh: 在我自己的研究中,女性对丈夫的抱怨最常聚焦的不是有形的不公平,比如为了陪伴丈夫而放弃职业机会,或者承担了远超自己应有份额的日常生活支持工作,如清洁、烹饪和社交安排。相反,她们关注的是沟通:"他不听我说话。""他不和我说话。"正如Hacker多年前观察到的,我发现大多数妻子希望她们的丈夫首先是谈话伙伴,但很少有丈夫对妻子抱有这种期望。

paragraphs.en: In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.
paragraphs.zh: 简而言之,最能代表当前危机的画面是一个老套的卡通场景:一个男人坐在早餐桌旁,面前举着一份报纸挡住脸,而一个女人怒视着报纸的背面,想要说话。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Over the past decade, many companies had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors – habits – among consumers. These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues. "There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits," said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. "We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically." The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to – Procter & Gamble, Colgate-Palmolive and Unilever – had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers' lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines. If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day – chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins – are results of manufactured habits. A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day. Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands. A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal. Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long. Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal. Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup. "Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns," said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year. "Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers' lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable." Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising. As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.

questions.stem: From the text we know that some of consumers' habits are developed due to ________________.
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 C）commercial promotions 定位句在第 4 段：如今，由于精明的广告与公共卫生宣传活动，许多美国人养成了每天刷两次牙的习惯——常常使用高露洁、佳洁士等品牌。正确项与原文构成同义替换（shrewd advertising and public health campaigns ↔ commercial promotions；tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising ↔ commercial promotions）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属答非所问、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。 2010年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇 35. The author's attitude toward the influence of advertisement on people's habits is ________________. 答案是什么？为什么选 B？ 2010年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the influence of advertisement on people's habits is ________________.
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是态度题，正确答案 B）negative 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（ruthless advertising ↔ negative；controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods ↔ negative）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Over the past decade, many companies had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors – habits – among consumers. These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去十年中,许多公司已经完善了在消费者中创造自动行为——习惯——的艺术。当顾客几乎不假思索地吃零食或擦拭台面时,这些习惯帮助公司赚取了数十亿美元,这通常是对一系列精心设计的日常提示的反应。

paragraphs.en: "There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits," said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. "We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically."
paragraphs.zh: 伦敦卫生与热带医学学院卫生中心主任Curtis博士说:"存在一些基本的公共卫生问题,比如脏手而非肥皂习惯,它们之所以仍然是致命因素,仅仅是因为我们无法弄清楚如何改变人们的习惯。我们想向私营企业学习如何创造自动发生的新行为。"

paragraphs.en: The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to – Procter & Gamble, Colgate-Palmolive and Unilever – had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers' lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines.
paragraphs.zh: Curtis博士求助的公司——宝洁、高露洁棕榄和联合利华——已经投资了数亿美元来寻找消费者生活中那些公司可以用来引入新习惯的微妙提示。

paragraphs.en: If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day – chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins – are results of manufactured habits. A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day. Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你仔细观察,你会发现我们每天使用的许多产品——口香糖、皮肤保湿霜、消毒湿巾、空气清新剂、净水器、健康零食、牙齿美白剂、织物柔顺剂、维生素——都是人为制造的习惯的结果。一个世纪前,很少有人每天多次定期刷牙。今天,由于精明的广告和公共健康运动,许多美国人习惯性地每天两次给他们洁白的牙齿进行预防蛀牙的清洁,通常使用高露洁、佳洁士或其他品牌之一。

paragraphs.en: A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal. Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long. Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal. Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年前,许多人在用餐之外不喝水。然后饮料公司开始将遥远泉水的产品装瓶,现在办公室职员整天不假思索地啜饮瓶装水。口香糖曾经主要由青春期男孩购买,现在在广告中被宣传为餐后使用的口气清新剂和牙齿清洁剂。皮肤保湿霜被宣传为晨间美容仪式的一部分,插入在梳头和化妆之间。

paragraphs.en: "Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns," said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year. "Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers' lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable."
paragraphs.zh: 消费心理学家Carol Berning最近从宝洁公司退休,该公司去年销售了760亿美元的汰渍、佳洁士和其他产品,她说:"当我们的产品成为日常或每周模式的一部分时,它们就会成功。创造积极的习惯是改善消费者生活的重要部分,对于使新产品在商业上可行至关重要。"

paragraphs.en: Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising. As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.
paragraphs.zh: 通过实验和观察,像Berning博士这样的社会科学家已经了解到,通过无情的广告将某些行为与习惯性提示联系起来具有力量。随着这种关于习惯的新科学的出现,当这些策略被用来销售可疑的美容霜或不健康食品时,争议就爆发了。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law. The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy. In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them. But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals. In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character. Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws. The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century. Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty. Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list. This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s. In 1968, the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury. This law abolished special educational requirements for federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community. In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level. The Taylor decision also declared sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the same procedures for selecting male and female jurors.

paragraphs.en: Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law. The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy. In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them.
paragraphs.zh: 许多美国人将陪审团制度视为重要民主价值观的具体体现,这些价值观包括以下原则:所有符合年龄和文化程度最低资格的公民都同样有资格担任陪审员;陪审员应从具有代表性的社区横断面中随机选出;任何公民都不应因种族、宗教、性别或民族出身而被剥夺担任陪审员的权利;被告有权由其同辈审判;裁决应代表社区的良知,而不仅仅是法律条文。陪审团也被认为是直接民主而非代议制民主现存的最佳范例。在直接民主中,公民轮流自我治理,而不是选举代表来为他们治理。

paragraphs.en: But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals. In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character. Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws.
paragraphs.zh: 但直到1968年,陪审员选拔程序仍与这些民主理想相冲突。例如,在一些州,陪审义务仅限于被认为具有优越智力、教育程度和道德品质的人。尽管美国最高法院早在1880年Strauder诉West Virginia案中就禁止了陪审员选拔中的蓄意种族歧视,但选拔所谓精英陪审团或蓝带陪审团的做法为规避这项法律和其他反歧视法律提供了便利途径。

paragraphs.en: The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century. Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty. Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list. This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s.
paragraphs.zh: 该制度也未能定期让女性进入陪审团,直到20世纪中叶。虽然女性于1898年首次在Utah州担任州陪审员,但直到20世纪40年代,大多数州才使女性有资格担任陪审义务。即便如此,仍有几个州自动豁免女性的陪审义务,除非她们亲自要求将自己的名字列入陪审员名单。这种做法以女性需要待在家中为由加以辩护,并使陪审团在整个20世纪60年代都不能代表女性。

paragraphs.en: In 1968, the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury. This law abolished special educational requirements for federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community. In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level. The Taylor decision also declared sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the same procedures for selecting male and female jurors.
paragraphs.zh: 1968年,美国国会通过了《陪审员选拔与服务法》,为陪审团开启了民主改革的新时代。该法律废除了对联邦陪审员的特殊教育要求,并要求从整个社区的横断面中随机选拔他们。在1975年具有里程碑意义的Taylor诉Louisiana案判决中,最高法院将陪审团必须代表社区各阶层的要求扩展到州一级。Taylor案判决还宣布陪审员选拔中的性别歧视违宪,并命令各州对男性和女性陪审员使用相同的选拔程序。

paragraphs.en: The outbreak of swine flu that was first detected in Mexico was declared a global epidemic on June 11, 2009. It is the first worldwide epidemic [1] by the World Health Organization in 41 years.

paragraphs.en: But the epidemic is " [4] " in severity, according to Margaret Chan, the organization's director general, [5] the overwhelming majority of patients experiencing only mild symptoms and a full recovery, often in the [6] of any medical treatment.

As much of Mexico City shut down at the height of a panic, cases began to [9] in New York City, the southwestern United States and around the world.

paragraphs.en: In the United States, new cases seemed to fade [10] warmer weather arrived. But in late September 2009, officials reported there was [11] flu activity in almost every state and that virtually all the [12] tested are the new swine flu, also known as (A) H1N1, not seasonal flu. paragraphs.zh: 在美国,随着温暖天气的到来,新增病例似乎有所减少。但在2009年9月下旬,官员报告称几乎每个州都有显著的流感活动,并且几乎所有检测样本都是新型猪流感,也称为甲型H1N1流感,而非季节性流感。在美国,它已感染超过一百万人,造成600多人死亡和6000多人住院。

More than three million doses were to be made available in early October 2009, though most of those [17] doses were of the FluMist nasal spray type, which is not [18] for pregnant women, people over 50 or those with breathing difficulties, heart disease or several other [19] . reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009. For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. "Hooray! At last!" wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic. One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known. Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the Times, calls him "an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him." As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise. For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music. All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes. Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point. For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century. These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today's live performances; moreover, they can be "consumed" at a time and place of the listener's choosing. The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert. One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record. Gilbert's own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into "a markedly different, more vibrant organization." But what will be the nature of that difference? Merely expanding the orchestra's repertoire will not be enough. If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America's oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.

paragraphs.en: The decision of the New York Philharmonic to hire Alan Gilbert as its next music director has been the talk of the classical-music world ever since the sudden announcement of his appointment in 2009. For the most part, the response has been favorable, to say the least. "Hooray! At last!" wrote Anthony Tommasini, a sober-sided classical-music critic.
paragraphs.zh: 纽约爱乐乐团决定聘请Alan Gilbert担任下一任音乐总监，自2009年突然宣布其任命以来，一直是古典音乐界的热门话题。总的来说，反应至少可以说是正面的。"万岁!终于!"Anthony Tommasini写道，他是一位严肃的古典音乐评论家。

paragraphs.en: One of the reasons why the appointment came as such a surprise, however, is that Gilbert is comparatively little known. Even Tommasini, who had advocated Gilbert's appointment in the Times, calls him "an unpretentious musician with no air of the formidable conductor about him." As a description of the next music director of an orchestra that has hitherto been led by musicians like Gustav Mahler and Pierre Boulez, that seems likely to have struck at least some Times readers as faint praise.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这一任命之所以如此令人惊讶的原因之一是，Gilbert相对来说并不知名。即使是在《纽约时报》上支持Gilbert任命的Tommasini也称他为"一位谦逊的音乐家，没有令人敬畏的指挥家气质"。作为对一个迄今为止由Gustav Mahler和Pierre Boulez这样的音乐家领导的乐团的下一任音乐总监的描述，这似乎至少会让一些《纽约时报》读者觉得是一种轻描淡写的赞扬。

paragraphs.en: For my part, I have no idea whether Gilbert is a great conductor or even a good one. To be sure, he performs an impressive variety of interesting compositions, but it is not necessary for me to visit Avery Fisher Hall, or anywhere else, to hear interesting orchestral music. All I have to do is to go to my CD shelf, or boot up my computer and download still more recorded music from iTunes.
paragraphs.zh: 就我而言，我不知道Gilbert是否是一位伟大的指挥家，甚至是否是一位优秀的指挥家。诚然，他演奏各种各样令人印象深刻的有趣作品，但我没有必要去Avery Fisher Hall或任何其他地方听有趣的管弦乐。我所要做的就是去我的CD架，或者启动电脑从iTunes下载更多录制的音乐。

paragraphs.en: Devoted concertgoers who reply that recordings are no substitute for live performance are missing the point. For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century. These recordings are cheap, available everywhere, and very often much higher in artistic quality than today's live performances; moreover, they can be "consumed" at a time and place of the listener's choosing. The widespread availability of such recordings has thus brought about a crisis in the institution of the traditional classical concert.
paragraphs.zh: 那些回应说录音无法替代现场演出的忠实音乐会观众没有抓住要点。为了争夺热爱艺术的公众的时间、注意力和金钱，古典乐器演奏家不仅必须与歌剧院、舞蹈团、剧院公司和博物馆竞争，还必须与20世纪伟大古典音乐家的录音演出竞争。这些录音价格便宜，随处可得，而且在艺术质量上往往远高于今天的现场演出；此外，它们可以在听众选择的时间和地点"消费"。因此，这类录音的广泛传播给传统古典音乐会这一制度带来了危机。

paragraphs.en: One possible response is for classical performers to program attractive new music that is not yet available on record. Gilbert's own interest in new music has been widely noted: Alex Ross, a classical-music critic, has described him as a man who is capable of turning the Philharmonic into "a markedly different, more vibrant organization." But what will be the nature of that difference? Merely expanding the orchestra's repertoire will not be enough. If Gilbert and the Philharmonic are to succeed, they must first change the relationship between America's oldest orchestra and the new audience it hopes to attract.
paragraphs.zh: 一种可能的应对方式是古典表演者演奏尚未录制的有吸引力的新音乐。Gilbert本人对新音乐的兴趣已被广泛关注：古典音乐评论家Alex Ross形容他是一个能够将爱乐乐团变成"一个明显不同、更有活力的组织"的人。但这种不同的本质是什么呢？仅仅扩大乐团的曲目是不够的。如果Gilbert和爱乐乐团要取得成功，他们必须首先改变美国最古老的乐团与它希望吸引的新观众之间的关系。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: When Liam McGee departed as president of Bank of America in August, his explanation was surprisingly straight up. Rather than cloaking his exit in the usual vague excuses, he came right out and said he was leaving "to pursue my goal of running a company." Broadcasting his ambition was "very much my decision," McGee says. Within two weeks, he was talking for the first time with the board of Hartford Financial Services Group, which named him CEO and chairman on September 29. McGee says leaving without a position lined up gave him time to reflect on what kind of company he wanted to run. It also sent a clear message to the outside world about his aspirations. And McGee isn't alone. In recent weeks the No. 2 executives at Avon and American Express quit with the explanation that they were looking for a CEO post. As boards scrutinize succession plans in response to shareholder pressure, executives who don't get the nod also may wish to move on. A turbulent business environment also has senior managers cautious of letting vague pronouncements cloud their reputations. As the first signs of recovery begin to take hold, deputy chiefs may be more willing to make the jump without a net. In the third quarter, CEO turnover was down 23% from a year ago as nervous boards stuck with the leaders they had, according to Liberum Research. As the economy picks up, opportunities will abound for aspiring leaders. The decision to quit a senior position to look for a better one is unconventional. For years executives and headhunters have adhered to the rule that the most attractive CEO candidates are the ones who must be poached. Says Korn/Ferry senior partner Dennis Carey: "I can't think of a single search I've done where a board has not instructed me to look at sitting CEOs first." Those who jumped without a job haven't always landed in top positions quickly. Ellen Marram quit as chief of Tropicana a decade ago, saying she wanted to be a CEO. It was a year before she became head of a tiny Internet-based commodities exchange. Robert Willumstad left Citigroup in 2005 with ambitions to be a CEO. He finally took that post at a major financial institution three years later. Many recruiters say the old disgrace is fading for top performers. The financial crisis has made it more acceptable to be between jobs or to leave a bad one. "The traditional rule was it's safer to stay where you are, but that's been fundamentally inverted," says one headhunter. "The people who've been hurt the worst are those who've stayed too long."

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: The rough guide to marketing success used to be that you got what you paid for. No longer. While traditional "paid" media – such as television commercials and print advertisements – still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media. Consumers passionate about a product may create "earned" media by willingly promoting it to friends, and a company may leverage "owned" media by sending e-mail alerts about products and sales to customers registered with its Web site. The way consumers now approach the process of making purchase decisions means that marketing's impact stems from a broad range of factors beyond conventional paid media. Paid and owned media are controlled by marketers promoting their own products. For earned media, such marketers act as the initiator for users' responses. But in some cases, one marketer's owned media become another marketer's paid media – for instance, when an e-commerce retailer sells ad space on its Web site. We define such sold media as owned media whose traffic is so strong that other organizations place their content or e-commerce engines within that environment. This trend, which we believe is still in its infancy, effectively began with retailers and travel providers such as airlines and hotels and will no doubt go further. Johnson & Johnson, for example, has created BabyCenter, a stand-alone media property that promotes complementary and even competitive products. Besides generating income, the presence of other marketers makes the site seem objective, gives companies opportunities to learn valuable information about the appeal of other companies' marketing, and may help expand user traffic for all companies concerned. The same dramatic technological changes that have provided marketers with more (and more diverse) communications choices have also increased the risk that passionate consumers will voice their opinions in quicker, more visible, and much more damaging ways. Such hijacked media are the opposite of earned media: an asset or campaign becomes hostage to consumers, other stakeholders, or activists who make negative allegations about a brand or product. Members of social networks, for instance, are learning that they can hijack media to apply pressure on the businesses that originally created them. If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products, putting the reputation of the target company at risk. In such a case, the company's response may not be sufficiently quick or thoughtful, and the learning curve has been steep. Toyota Motor, for example, alleviated some of the damage from its recall crisis earlier this year with a relatively quick and well-orchestrated social-media response campaign, which included efforts to engage with consumers directly on sites such as Twitter and the social-news site Digg.

paragraphs.en: The rough guide to marketing success used to be that you got what you paid for. No longer. While traditional "paid" media – such as television commercials and print advertisements – still play a major role, companies today can exploit many alternative forms of media. Consumers passionate about a product may create "earned" media by willingly promoting it to friends, and a company may leverage "owned" media by sending e-mail alerts about products and sales to customers registered with its Web site. The way consumers now approach the process of making purchase decisions means that marketing's impact stems from a broad range of factors beyond conventional paid media.
paragraphs.zh: 过去,营销成功的粗略指南是一分钱一分货。如今不再如此。尽管传统的"付费"媒体——如电视广告和平面广告——仍然发挥着重要作用,但企业现在可以利用许多替代形式的媒体。对产品充满热情的消费者可能会自愿向朋友推广产品,从而创造"赢得"媒体,而企业可以通过向其网站注册客户发送有关产品和促销的电子邮件提醒来利用"自有"媒体。消费者现在做出购买决策的方式意味着,营销的影响源于传统付费媒体之外的广泛因素。

paragraphs.en: Paid and owned media are controlled by marketers promoting their own products. For earned media, such marketers act as the initiator for users' responses. But in some cases, one marketer's owned media become another marketer's paid media – for instance, when an e-commerce retailer sells ad space on its Web site. We define such sold media as owned media whose traffic is so strong that other organizations place their content or e-commerce engines within that environment. This trend, which we believe is still in its infancy, effectively began with retailers and travel providers such as airlines and hotels and will no doubt go further. Johnson & Johnson, for example, has created BabyCenter, a stand-alone media property that promotes complementary and even competitive products. Besides generating income, the presence of other marketers makes the site seem objective, gives companies opportunities to learn valuable information about the appeal of other companies' marketing, and may help expand user traffic for all companies concerned.
paragraphs.zh: 付费媒体和自有媒体由推广自身产品的营销人员控制。对于赢得媒体,这些营销人员充当用户响应的发起者。但在某些情况下,一个营销人员的自有媒体会成为另一个营销人员的付费媒体——例如,当电子商务零售商在其网站上出售广告位时。我们将这种售出媒体定义为流量强大到其他组织在其环境中放置内容或电子商务引擎的自有媒体。我们认为这一趋势仍处于初期阶段,它实际上始于零售商以及航空公司和酒店等旅游服务提供商,并且无疑会进一步发展。例如,Johnson & Johnson创建了BabyCenter,这是一个独立的媒体平台,推广互补甚至竞争性产品。除了创造收入外,其他营销人员的存在使该网站显得客观,为企业提供了了解其他公司营销吸引力的宝贵信息的机会,并可能有助于扩大所有相关公司的用户流量。

paragraphs.en: The same dramatic technological changes that have provided marketers with more (and more diverse) communications choices have also increased the risk that passionate consumers will voice their opinions in quicker, more visible, and much more damaging ways. Such hijacked media are the opposite of earned media: an asset or campaign becomes hostage to consumers, other stakeholders, or activists who make negative allegations about a brand or product. Members of social networks, for instance, are learning that they can hijack media to apply pressure on the businesses that originally created them.
paragraphs.zh: 为营销人员提供更多(且更多样化)传播选择的同样巨大的技术变革,也增加了充满热情的消费者以更快、更明显且更具破坏性的方式表达意见的风险。这种被劫持的媒体与赢得媒体相反:资产或活动成为消费者、其他利益相关者或活动人士的人质,他们对品牌或产品提出负面指控。例如,社交网络成员正在了解到,他们可以劫持媒体,对最初创建这些媒体的企业施加压力。

paragraphs.en: If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products, putting the reputation of the target company at risk. In such a case, the company's response may not be sufficiently quick or thoughtful, and the learning curve has been steep. Toyota Motor, for example, alleviated some of the damage from its recall crisis earlier this year with a relatively quick and well-orchestrated social-media response campaign, which included efforts to engage with consumers directly on sites such as Twitter and the social-news site Digg.
paragraphs.zh: 如果发生这种情况,充满热情的消费者会试图说服他人抵制产品,使目标公司的声誉面临风险。在这种情况下,公司的反应可能不够迅速或周到,而且学习曲线一直很陡峭。例如,Toyota Motor今年早些时候通过相对迅速且精心策划的社交媒体响应活动,减轻了召回危机造成的一些损害,其中包括在Twitter和社交新闻网站Digg等网站上直接与消费者互动的努力。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: It's no surprise that Jennifer Senior's insightful, provocative magazine cover story, "I love My Children, I Hate My Life," is arousing much chatter – nothing gets people talking like the suggestion that child rearing is anything less than a completely fulfilling, life-enriching experience. Rather than concluding that children make parents either happy or miserable, Senior suggests we need to redefine happiness: instead of thinking of it as something that can be measured by moment-to-moment joy, we should consider being happy as a past-tense condition. Even though the day-to-day experience of raising kids can be soul-crushingly hard, Senior writes that "the very things that in the moment dampen our moods can later be sources of intense gratification and delight." The magazine cover showing an attractive mother holding a cute baby is hardly the only Madonna-and-child image on newsstands this week. There are also stories about newly adoptive – and newly single – mom Sandra Bullock, as well as the usual "Jennifer Aniston is pregnant" news. Practically every week features at least one celebrity mom, or mom-to-be, smiling on the newsstands. In a society that so persistently celebrates procreation, is it any wonder that admitting you regret having children is equivalent to admitting you support kitten-killing? It doesn't seem quite fair, then, to compare the regrets of parents to the regrets of the childless. Unhappy parents rarely are provoked to wonder if they shouldn't have had kids, but unhappy childless folks are bothered with the message that children are the single most important thing in the world: obviously their misery must be a direct result of the gaping baby-size holes in their lives. Of course, the image of parenthood that celebrity magazines like Us Weekly and People present is hugely unrealistic, especially when the parents are single mothers like Bullock. According to several studies concluding that parents are less happy than childless couples, single parents are the least happy of all. No shock there, considering how much work it is to raise a kid without a partner to lean on; yet to hear Sandra and Britney tell it, raising a kid on their "own" (read: with round-the-clock help) is a piece of cake. It's hard to imagine that many people are dumb enough to want children just because Reese and Angelina make it look so glamorous: most adults understand that a baby is not a haircut. But it's interesting to wonder if the images we see every week of stress-free, happiness-enhancing parenthood aren't in some small, subconscious way contributing to our own dissatisfactions with the actual experience, in the same way that a small part of us hoped getting "the Rachel" might make us look just a little bit like Jennifer Aniston.

paragraphs.en: It's no surprise that Jennifer Senior's insightful, provocative magazine cover story, "I love My Children, I Hate My Life," is arousing much chatter – nothing gets people talking like the suggestion that child rearing is anything less than a completely fulfilling, life-enriching experience. Rather than concluding that children make parents either happy or miserable, Senior suggests we need to redefine happiness: instead of thinking of it as something that can be measured by moment-to-moment joy, we should consider being happy as a past-tense condition. Even though the day-to-day experience of raising kids can be soul-crushingly hard, Senior writes that "the very things that in the moment dampen our moods can later be sources of intense gratification and delight."
paragraphs.zh: Jennifer Senior那篇富有洞察力、引人深思的杂志封面文章《我爱我的孩子,我恨我的生活》引发了大量讨论,这并不令人意外——没有什么比暗示养育孩子并非一种完全令人满足、丰富人生的体验更能引起人们的热议了。Senior并没有得出孩子让父母要么幸福要么痛苦的结论,而是建议我们需要重新定义幸福:我们不应将其视为可以用每时每刻的快乐来衡量的东西,而应将幸福视为一种过去时态的状态。尽管抚养孩子的日常经历可能会令人精疲力竭,但Senior写道,"那些在当下压抑我们情绪的事情,日后可能成为强烈满足感和愉悦的来源。"

paragraphs.en: The magazine cover showing an attractive mother holding a cute baby is hardly the only Madonna-and-child image on newsstands this week. There are also stories about newly adoptive – and newly single – mom Sandra Bullock, as well as the usual "Jennifer Aniston is pregnant" news. Practically every week features at least one celebrity mom, or mom-to-be, smiling on the newsstands.
paragraphs.zh: 本周报刊上展示一位迷人母亲抱着可爱婴儿的杂志封面,绝非唯一的圣母与圣子形象。还有关于新晋领养妈妈——同时也是新晋单身妈妈——Sandra Bullock的报道,以及惯常的"Jennifer Aniston怀孕了"的新闻。实际上每周至少有一位名人妈妈或准妈妈在报刊上微笑示人。

paragraphs.en: In a society that so persistently celebrates procreation, is it any wonder that admitting you regret having children is equivalent to admitting you support kitten-killing? It doesn't seem quite fair, then, to compare the regrets of parents to the regrets of the childless. Unhappy parents rarely are provoked to wonder if they shouldn't have had kids, but unhappy childless folks are bothered with the message that children are the single most important thing in the world: obviously their misery must be a direct result of the gaping baby-size holes in their lives.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个如此持续不断地颂扬生育的社会里,承认自己后悔生孩子等同于承认自己支持虐杀小猫,这有什么奇怪的吗?那么,将父母的遗憾与无子女者的遗憾相比较似乎并不公平。不幸福的父母很少会被激起思考自己是否不该生孩子,但不幸福的无子女者却被这样的信息所困扰:孩子是世界上最重要的东西,显然他们的痛苦一定是其生活中那个婴儿大小的空缺直接造成的。

paragraphs.en: Of course, the image of parenthood that celebrity magazines like Us Weekly and People present is hugely unrealistic, especially when the parents are single mothers like Bullock. According to several studies concluding that parents are less happy than childless couples, single parents are the least happy of all. No shock there, considering how much work it is to raise a kid without a partner to lean on; yet to hear Sandra and Britney tell it, raising a kid on their "own" (read: with round-the-clock help) is a piece of cake.
paragraphs.zh: 当然,像Us Weekly和People这样的名人杂志所呈现的为人父母形象是极不真实的,尤其是当父母是像Bullock这样的单身母亲时。根据多项研究得出的结论,父母的幸福感低于无子女夫妇,而单亲父母是所有人中最不幸福的。这并不令人震惊,考虑到在没有伴侣可以依靠的情况下抚养孩子需要付出多少努力;然而听Sandra和Britney说来,她们"独自"(意思是:在全天候帮助下)抚养孩子简直是小菜一碟。

paragraphs.en: It's hard to imagine that many people are dumb enough to want children just because Reese and Angelina make it look so glamorous: most adults understand that a baby is not a haircut. But it's interesting to wonder if the images we see every week of stress-free, happiness-enhancing parenthood aren't in some small, subconscious way contributing to our own dissatisfactions with the actual experience, in the same way that a small part of us hoped getting "the Rachel" might make us look just a little bit like Jennifer Aniston.
paragraphs.zh: 很难想象会有很多人愚蠢到仅仅因为Reese和Angelina让养育孩子看起来如此光鲜亮丽就想要孩子:大多数成年人都明白婴儿不是理发。但有趣的是,我们每周看到的那些无压力、增进幸福感的为人父母形象,是否在某种微小的、潜意识的层面上助长了我们对实际经历的不满,就像我们中有一小部分人曾希望剪个"Rachel头"可能会让我们看起来有那么一点像Jennifer Aniston一样。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs's board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University. For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism. But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked? By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board. The position was just taking up too much time, she said. Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board. Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals. If the sky and the share price are falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises. The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004. Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next. The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70. They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms. Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they "trade up," leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms. But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred. Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives. Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.

paragraphs.en: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs's board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University. For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism. But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked? By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board. The position was just taking up too much time, she said.
paragraphs.zh: Ruth Simmons于2000年1月作为外部董事加入Goldman Sachs董事会；一年后她成为Brown University校长。在接下来的十年里，她显然同时管理着这两个职务，并未招致太多批评。但到2009年底，Simmons女士因担任Goldman薪酬委员会成员而受到抨击；她怎么能对那些巨额奖金发放视而不见呢？到次年2月，Simmons女士已离开董事会。她说，这个职位占用了太多时间。

paragraphs.en: Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board. Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals. If the sky and the share price are falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.
paragraphs.zh: 外部董事应当在公司董事会中充当有益但较少偏见的顾问。由于他们的财富和声誉是在其他地方建立的，他们大概有足够的独立性来反对首席执行官的提议。如果股价和天空一起下跌，外部董事应该能够基于自己经历过的危机提供建议。

paragraphs.en: The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004. Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next. The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70. They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms. Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they "trade up," leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.
paragraphs.zh: Ohio University的研究人员使用了一个涵盖1989年至2004年间超过10,000家公司和超过64,000名不同董事的数据库。然后他们只是简单地检查哪些董事从一份委托声明留任到下一份。离开董事会最可能的原因是年龄，因此研究人员将注意力集中在70岁以下董事的那些"意外"离职上。他们发现，在意外离职后，公司随后必须重述收益的概率增加了近20%。被列入联邦集体诉讼的可能性也会增加，股票表现可能会更差。这种影响对于规模更大的公司往往更明显。尽管他们离职与公司随后的糟糕表现之间的相关性具有暗示性，但这并不意味着这些董事总是在弃船逃跑。他们往往是"向上跳槽"，离开风险较高的小公司，转投规模更大、更稳定的公司。

paragraphs.en: But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred. Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives. Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
paragraphs.zh: 但研究人员认为，如果外部董事在坏消息曝光之前离开公司，他们更容易避免声誉受损，即使历史回顾显示在任何不当行为发生时他们就在董事会任职。希望在困难时期留住外部董事的公司可能必须创造激励措施。否则，外部董事将效仿Simmons女士的做法，再次在校园里大受欢迎。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers? A year ago the end seemed near. The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet. Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom. America's Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers. Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them? It will hold another meeting soon. But the discussions now seem out of date. In much of the world there is little sign of crisis. German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession. Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit. Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same. It has not been much fun. Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard. The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007. Readers are paying more for slimmer products. Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further. Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers. American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD). In Japan the proportion is 35%. Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable. The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive. Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters. Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off. Newspapers are less complete as a result. But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.

questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 C）are less dependent on advertising 定位句在第 4 段：美国报纸长期以来在依赖广告这一点上非常不寻常。根据经济合作与发展组织（OECD）数据，2008 年它们 87% 的收入来自广告。在日本这一比例是 35%。不出意外，日本报纸要稳定得多。正确项与原文构成同义替换（In Japan the proportion is 35%. ↔ are less dependent on advertising；American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. ↔ are less dependent on advertising）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。 2011年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 29. questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about the current newspaper business?
options: A) Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.
B) Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspaper.
C) Foreign bureaus play a crucial role in the newspaper business.
D) Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是推断题，正确答案 A）Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers. 定位句在第 5 段：横扫新闻编辑室的风暴伤害了所有人，但大部分伤害集中在报纸最缺乏独特性的领域。汽车和电影评论员走了。科技和综合商业记者也是。驻外机构被狠狠裁掉。结果报纸变得不完整。但在报业里，完整性不再是一种美德。正确项与原文构成同义替换（areas where newspapers are least distinctive ↔ Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.；But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business. ↔ Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。 2011年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 30.
