questions.stem: The most appropriate title for this text would be____.
options: A) American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival
B) American Newspapers: Gone with the Wind
C) American Newspapers: A Thriving Business
D) American Newspapers: A Hopeless Story
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（these desperate measures have proved the right ones ↔ American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival；Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit. ↔ American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival；much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive ↔ American Newspapers: Struggling for Survival）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属过度推断、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers? A year ago the end seemed near. The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet. Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom. America's Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers. Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them? It will hold another meeting soon. But the discussions now seem out of date.
paragraphs.zh: 报纸的消亡究竟怎么样了?一年前,终结似乎近在眼前。经济衰退威胁要夺走尚未逃往互联网的广告和读者。像旧金山纪事报这样的报纸正在记录它们自己的末日。美国联邦贸易委员会发起了一轮关于如何拯救报纸的讨论。它们应该成为慈善公司吗?国家应该补贴它们吗?委员会很快将再举行一次会议。但这些讨论现在似乎已经过时了。

paragraphs.en: In much of the world there is little sign of crisis. German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession. Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit. Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same.
paragraphs.zh: 在世界大部分地区几乎没有危机的迹象。德国和巴西的报纸摆脱了经济衰退的影响。即使是身处全球报业最困难角落的美国报纸,不仅生存了下来,而且往往恢复了盈利。虽然不是几年前常规的20%利润率,但毕竟还是盈利。

paragraphs.en: It has not been much fun. Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard. The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007. Readers are paying more for slimmer products. Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further.
paragraphs.zh: 这个过程并不怎么愉快。许多报纸通过把记者推下船来维持生存。美国新闻编辑协会估计,自2007年以来已经失去了13500个新闻编辑室的工作岗位。读者正在为更薄的产品支付更多费用。一些报纸甚至敢于拒绝向偏远郊区投递。然而这些绝望的措施被证明是正确的,而且令许多记者遗憾的是,这些措施还可以进一步推行。

paragraphs.en: Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers. American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD). In Japan the proportion is 35%. Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.
paragraphs.zh: 报纸正在成为更加平衡的企业,来自读者和广告商的收入组合更加健康。美国报纸长期以来在对广告的依赖方面一直非常不寻常。根据经济合作与发展组织的数据,2008年它们87%的收入来自广告。在日本这一比例是35%。毫不奇怪,日本报纸要稳定得多。

paragraphs.en: The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive. Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters. Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off. Newspapers are less complete as a result. But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.
paragraphs.zh: 席卷新闻编辑室的旋风伤害了所有人,但大部分损害集中在报纸最不具特色的领域。汽车和电影评论员已经消失了。科学和综合商业记者也是如此。驻外记者站被大幅削减。报纸因此变得不那么完整了。但完整性在报业中不再是一种美德。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus. But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more. During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish. Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase "less is more" was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools. These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies. Mies's signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot. Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood – materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future. Mies's sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty. The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller – two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet – than those in their older neighbors along the city's Gold Coast. But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings' details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time. The trend toward "less" was not entirely foreign. In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses – usually around 1,200 square feet – than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century. The "Case Study Houses" commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the "less is more" trend. Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.

paragraphs.en: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.
paragraphs.zh: 我们倾向于认为二战后的几十年是一个繁荣和增长的时期，数百万士兵返回家园，依靠《退伍军人权利法案》上大学，并在婚姻登记处排队。

paragraphs.en: But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more. During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.
paragraphs.zh: 但就住房而言,那是一个崇尚常识、相信少即是多的时代。在大萧条和战争期间,美国人学会了简朴生活,这种克制与战后对未来的信心相结合,使小型高效住宅成为一种时尚。

paragraphs.en: Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase "less is more" was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools. These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.
paragraphs.zh: 经济状况只是高效生活趋势的一个刺激因素。"少即是多"这句话实际上最早是由一位德国人、建筑师Ludwig Mies van der Rohe推广的,他像其他与包豪斯设计学院有关的人一样,在二战前移民到美国并在美国建筑学院任职。这些设计师对美国建筑的发展产生了巨大影响,但没有人比Mies的影响更大。

paragraphs.en: Mies's signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot. Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood – materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future. Mies's sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.
paragraphs.zh: Mies的标志性语句意味着,适当组织的少量装饰比大量装饰更有冲击力。他认为,优雅并非源于丰富。像其他现代建筑师一样,他使用金属、玻璃和层压木材——这些材料在今天我们认为理所当然,但在20世纪40年代却象征着未来。Mies精致的呈现掩盖了一个事实,即他设计的空间是小而高效的,而非大而常常空荡的。

paragraphs.en: The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller – two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet – than those in their older neighbors along the city's Gold Coast. But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings' details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time.
paragraphs.zh: 例如,Mies在芝加哥Lake Shore Drive建造的优雅高层公寓——面积不足1000平方英尺的两居室单元——比沿城市Gold Coast的老建筑更小。但它们很受欢迎,因为有通透的玻璃墙、所提供的景观,以及建筑细节和比例的优雅,这是当时流行的抽象艺术在建筑上的对应物。

paragraphs.en: The trend toward "less" was not entirely foreign. In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses – usually around 1,200 square feet – than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century.
paragraphs.zh: "少"的趋势并非完全来自国外。20世纪30年代,Frank Lloyd Wright开始建造更简朴高效的住宅——通常在1200平方英尺左右——比他在19世纪90年代和20世纪初设计的开阔的两层住宅要小。

paragraphs.en: The "Case Study Houses" commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the "less is more" trend. Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.
paragraphs.zh: 1945年至1962年间由加州《艺术与建筑》杂志委托才华横溢的现代建筑师设计的"案例研究住宅"是"少即是多"趋势的另一个本土影响因素。美学效果来自景观、新材料和直白的细节处理。在他的案例研究住宅中,Ralph Rapson可能错误预测了机械革命将如何影响日常生活——很少有美国家庭拥有直升机,尽管大多数家庭最终都有了干衣机——但他认为自给自足既可取又不可避免的信念得到了广泛认同。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a "Bermuda triangle" of debt, population decline and lower growth. As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency. Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation. Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise. Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey. These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference. A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers. Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs. It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world's largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area. It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.

questions.stem: Regarding the future of the EU, the author seems to feel____.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是态度题，正确答案 D）hopeful 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（It is too soon to write off the EU ↔ hopeful；It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign ↔ hopeful）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a "Bermuda triangle" of debt, population decline and lower growth.
paragraphs.zh: 欧盟能否挺过去？这个问题在不久前听起来还很奇怪。如今，即便是该计划最热情的支持者也在谈论一个面临债务、人口下降和增长放缓这一"百慕大三角"的大陆。

paragraphs.en: As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency. Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 除了这些长期问题，欧盟在其经济核心——使用单一货币的16个国家——还面临着一场严重危机。市场已不再相信欧元区经济体，无论强弱，会因共享单一货币的约束而终有一天趋于一致，而单一货币使缺乏竞争力的成员国无法采取货币贬值这一权宜之计。

paragraphs.en: Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，关于如何拯救欧洲单一货币免于分崩离析的辩论陷入了僵局。之所以陷入僵局,是因为欧元区的主导力量法国和德国在欧元区内需要加强协调一致方面意见相同，但在协调什么方面存在分歧。

paragraphs.en: Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey. These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.
paragraphs.zh: 德国认为必须通过更严格的借贷、支出和竞争力规则来拯救欧元，并对不遵守的政府实施准自动制裁。这些制裁可能包括威胁冻结面向贫困地区的欧盟基金和欧盟大型项目，甚至暂停一国在欧盟部长理事会中的投票权。德国坚持认为经济协调应涉及欧盟俱乐部的全部27个成员国，其中支持自由市场自由主义和经济严谨的占微弱多数；德国担心，仅在核心圈内，支持法国式干预的会占微弱多数。

paragraphs.en: A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers. Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.
paragraphs.zh: 以法国为首的"南方"阵营想要的是不同的东西：在欧元区成员国核心圈内建立"欧洲经济政府"。换句话说，这意味着政治家干预货币政策，以及通过共同欧洲债券或完全的财政转移支付来降低政府借贷成本，从而建立一个从富裕成员国向贫困成员国再分配的体系。最后，接近法国政府的人士私下表示，欧元区成员国应就某些财政和社会协调达成一致：例如，限制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的竞争。

paragraphs.en: It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world's largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area. It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
paragraphs.zh: 现在就对欧盟下定论还为时过早。它仍然是世界上最大的贸易集团。在最好的状态下，欧洲计划是非常自由的：围绕一个由27个富国和穷国组成的单一市场建立，其内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度远超任何可比的贸易区。这是一次雄心勃勃的尝试，旨在削弱全球化最尖锐的锋芒，使资本主义变得温和。

reading.passage: Come on – Everybody's doing it. That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good—drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world. Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. In South Africa, an HIV-prevention initiative known as loveLife recruits young people to promote safe sex among their peers. The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the lameness of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. "Dare to be different, please don't smoke!" pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers—teenagers, who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues convincingly that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure. But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological factors that make peer pressure so powerful. The most glaring flaw of the social cure as it's presented here is that it doesn't work very well for very long. Rage Against the Haze failed once state funding was cut. Evidence that the loveLife program produces lasting changes is limited and mixed. There's no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits—as well as negative ones—spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we unconsciously imitate the behavior we see every day. Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It's like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that's the problem with a social cure engineered from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, peer pressure often emerges as____
options: A) a supplement to the social cure.
B) a stimulus to group dynamics.

paragraphs.en: Come on – Everybody's doing it. That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure. It usually leads to no good—drinking, drugs and casual sex. But in her new book Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure, in which organizations and officials use the power of group dynamics to help individuals improve their lives and possibly the world.
paragraphs.zh: 来吧——大家都在这么做。这句半是邀请半是强迫的耳语,正是我们大多数人听到"同辈压力"这个词时想到的东西。它通常不会带来什么好结果——酗酒、吸毒和随意的性行为。但在她的新书《加入俱乐部》中,Tina Rosenberg认为同辈压力也可以成为一种积极的力量,她称之为社会治愈,即组织和官员利用群体动力学的力量来帮助个人改善生活,甚至可能改善世界。

paragraphs.en: Rosenberg, the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize, offers a host of examples of the social cure in action: In South Carolina, a state-sponsored antismoking program called Rage Against the Haze sets out to make cigarettes uncool. In South Africa, an HIV-prevention initiative known as loveLife recruits young people to promote safe sex among their peers.
paragraphs.zh: 普利策奖获得者Rosenberg列举了大量社会治愈实践的例子:在South Carolina,一个由州政府资助的反吸烟项目叫做Rage Against the Haze,旨在让香烟变得不酷。在South Africa,一个名为loveLife的艾滋病预防倡议招募年轻人在同龄人中推广安全性行为。

paragraphs.en: The idea seems promising, and Rosenberg is a perceptive observer. Her critique of the lameness of many public-health campaigns is spot-on: they fail to mobilize peer pressure for healthy habits, and they demonstrate a seriously flawed understanding of psychology. "Dare to be different, please don't smoke!" pleads one billboard campaign aimed at reducing smoking among teenagers—teenagers, who desire nothing more than fitting in. Rosenberg argues convincingly that public-health advocates ought to take a page from advertisers, so skilled at applying peer pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 这个想法似乎很有前景,而Rosenberg是一位敏锐的观察者。她对许多公共卫生运动的无力的批评切中要害:它们未能调动同辈压力来促进健康习惯,并且表现出对心理学严重缺陷的理解。"勇于与众不同,请不要吸烟!"一个旨在减少青少年吸烟的广告牌运动如此恳求——而青少年最渴望的就是融入群体。Rosenberg令人信服地论证,公共卫生倡导者应该向广告商学习,因为他们在运用同辈压力方面如此娴熟。

paragraphs.en: But on the general effectiveness of the social cure, Rosenberg is less persuasive. Join the Club is filled with too much irrelevant detail and not enough exploration of the social and biological factors that make peer pressure so powerful. The most glaring flaw of the social cure as it's presented here is that it doesn't work very well for very long. Rage Against the Haze failed once state funding was cut. Evidence that the loveLife program produces lasting changes is limited and mixed.
paragraphs.zh: 但在社会治愈的总体有效性方面,Rosenberg的说服力较弱。《加入俱乐部》充斥着太多无关的细节,而对使同辈压力如此强大的社会和生物因素探索不足。此处呈现的社会治愈最明显的缺陷是,它在很长时间内效果并不理想。Rage Against the Haze在州政府资金削减后就失败了。loveLife项目产生持久改变的证据有限且结果不一。

paragraphs.en: There's no doubt that our peer groups exert enormous influence on our behavior. An emerging body of research shows that positive health habits—as well as negative ones—spread through networks of friends via social communication. This is a subtle form of peer pressure: we unconsciously imitate the behavior we see every day.
paragraphs.zh: 毫无疑问,我们的同辈群体对我们的行为施加着巨大的影响。一个新兴的研究领域表明,积极的健康习惯——以及消极的习惯——通过社交传播在朋友网络中传播。这是一种微妙的同辈压力形式:我们无意识地模仿每天看到的行为。

paragraphs.en: Far less certain, however, is how successfully experts and bureaucrats can select our peer groups and steer their activities in virtuous directions. It's like the teacher who breaks up the troublemakers in the back row by pairing them with better-behaved classmates. The tactic never really works. And that's the problem with a social cure engineered from the outside: in the real world, as in school, we insist on choosing our own friends.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,远不那么确定的是,专家和官僚能在多大程度上成功地选择我们的同辈群体并将他们的活动引向良性方向。这就像老师通过将后排的捣蛋学生与表现更好的同学配对来拆散他们。这种策略从来没有真正奏效过。这就是从外部设计的社会治愈的问题所在:在现实世界中,就像在学校里一样,我们坚持选择自己的朋友。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: A deal is a deal—except, apparently, when Entergy is involved. The company, a major energy supplier in New England, provoked justified outrage in Vermont last week when it announced it was reneging on a longstanding commitment to abide by the state's strict nuclear regulations. Instead, the company has done precisely what it had long promised it would not: challenge the constitutionality of Vermont's rules in the federal court, as part of a desperate effort to keep its Vermont Yankee nuclear power plant running. It's a stunning move. The conflict has been surfacing since 2002, when the corporation bought Vermont's only nuclear power plant, an aging reactor in Vernon. As a condition of receiving state approval for the sale, the company agreed to seek permission from state regulators to operate past 2012. In 2006, the state went a step further, requiring that any extension of the plant's license be subject to the Vermont legislature's approval. Then, too, the company went along. Either Entergy never really intended to live by those commitments, or it simply didn't foresee what would happen next. A string of accidents, including the partial collapse of a cooling tower in 2007 and the discovery of an underground pipe system leakage, raised serious questions about both Vermont Yankee's safety and Entergy's management – especially after the company made misleading statements about the pipe. Enraged by Entergy's behavior, the Vermont Senate voted 26 to 4 last year against allowing an extension. Now the company is suddenly claiming that the 2002 agreement is invalid because of the 2006 legislation, and that only the federal government has regulatory power over nuclear issues. The legal issues in the case are obscure: whereas the Supreme Court has ruled that states do have some regulatory authority over nuclear power, legal scholars say that Vermont case will offer a precedent-setting test of how far those powers extend. Certainly, there are valid concerns about the patchwork regulations that could result if every state sets its own rules. But had Entergy kept its word, that debate would be beside the point. The company seems to have concluded that its reputation in Vermont is already so damaged that it has nothing left to lose by going to war with the state. But there should be consequences. Permission to run a nuclear plant is a public trust. Entergy runs 11 other reactors in the United States, including Pilgrim Nuclear station in Plymouth. Pledging to run Pilgrim safely, the company has applied for federal permission to keep it open for another 20 years. But as the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reviews the company's application, it should keep in mind what promises from Entergy are worth.

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by objective researchers who use the scientific method to carry out their work. But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route. We aim to be objective, but we cannot escape the context of our unique life experiences. Prior knowledge and interests influence what we experience, what we think our experiences mean, and the subsequent actions we take. Opportunities for misinterpretation, error, and self-deception abound. Consequently, discovery claims should be thought of as protoscience. Similar to newly staked mining claims, they are full of potential. But it takes collective scrutiny and acceptance to transform a discovery claim into a mature discovery. This is the credibility process, through which the individual researcher's me, here, now becomes the community's anyone, anywhere, anytime. Objective knowledge is the goal, not the starting point. Once a discovery claim becomes public, the discoverer receives intellectual credit. But, unlike with mining claims, the community takes control of what happens next. Within the complex social structure of the scientific community, researchers make discoveries; editors and reviewers act as gatekeepers by controlling the publication process; other scientists use the new finding to suit their own purposes; and finally, the public (including other scientists) receives the new discovery and possibly accompanying technology. As a discovery claim works its way through the community, the interaction and confrontation between shared and competing beliefs about the science and the technology involved transforms an individual's discovery claim into the community's credible discovery. Two paradoxes exist throughout this credibility process. First, scientific work tends to focus on some aspect of prevailing knowledge that is viewed as incomplete or incorrect. Little reward accompanies duplication and confirmation of what is already known and believed. The goal is new-search, not re-search. Not surprisingly, newly published discovery claims and credible discoveries that appear to be important and convincing will always be open to challenge and potential modification or refutation by future researchers. Second, novelty itself frequently provokes disbelief. Nobel Laureate and physiologist Albert Szent-Györgyi once described discovery as "seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought." But thinking what nobody else has thought and telling others what they have missed may not change their views. Sometimes years are required for truly novel discovery claims to be accepted and appreciated. In the end, credibility "happens" to a discovery claim—a process that corresponds to what philosopher Annette Baier has described as the commons of the mind. "We reason together, challenge, revise, and complete each other's reasoning and each other's conceptions of reason."

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title of the text?
options: A) Novelty as an Engine of Scientific Development.

C) Evolution of Credibility in Doing Science.

paragraphs.en: In the idealized version of how science is done, facts about the world are waiting to be observed and collected by objective researchers who use the scientific method to carry out their work. But in the everyday practice of science, discovery frequently follows an ambiguous and complicated route. We aim to be objective, but we cannot escape the context of our unique life experiences. Prior knowledge and interests influence what we experience, what we think our experiences mean, and the subsequent actions we take. Opportunities for misinterpretation, error, and self-deception abound.
paragraphs.zh: 在科学研究的理想化版本中，关于世界的事实正等待着客观的研究者去观察和收集,这些研究者使用科学方法来开展工作。但在科学的日常实践中,发现往往遵循一条模糊而复杂的路径。我们力求客观,但我们无法摆脱各自独特生活经历的背景。先前的知识和兴趣影响着我们的经历、我们对经历意义的理解,以及我们随后采取的行动。误解、错误和自欺的机会比比皆是。

paragraphs.en: Consequently, discovery claims should be thought of as protoscience. Similar to newly staked mining claims, they are full of potential. But it takes collective scrutiny and acceptance to transform a discovery claim into a mature discovery. This is the credibility process, through which the individual researcher's me, here, now becomes the community's anyone, anywhere, anytime. Objective knowledge is the goal, not the starting point.
paragraphs.zh: 因此,发现声明应被视为原科学。类似于新立的采矿权,它们充满潜力。但需要集体审查和认可才能将一项发现声明转化为成熟的发现。这就是可信度过程,通过这一过程,个体研究者的"我、此地、此刻"变成了共同体的"任何人、任何地方、任何时候"。客观知识是目标,而非起点。

paragraphs.en: Once a discovery claim becomes public, the discoverer receives intellectual credit. But, unlike with mining claims, the community takes control of what happens next. Within the complex social structure of the scientific community, researchers make discoveries; editors and reviewers act as gatekeepers by controlling the publication process; other scientists use the new finding to suit their own purposes; and finally, the public (including other scientists) receives the new discovery and possibly accompanying technology. As a discovery claim works its way through the community, the interaction and confrontation between shared and competing beliefs about the science and the technology involved transforms an individual's discovery claim into the community's credible discovery.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦发现声明公之于众,发现者就会获得智力荣誉。但与采矿权不同,共同体掌控着接下来发生的事情。在科学共同体复杂的社会结构中,研究者做出发现;编辑和审稿人通过控制出版过程充当守门人;其他科学家利用新发现来服务于他们自己的目的;最后,公众(包括其他科学家)接收新发现以及可能伴随的技术。随着发现声明在共同体中推进,关于所涉及的科学和技术的共享信念与相互竞争信念之间的互动和对抗,将个人的发现声明转化为共同体的可信发现。

paragraphs.en: Two paradoxes exist throughout this credibility process. First, scientific work tends to focus on some aspect of prevailing knowledge that is viewed as incomplete or incorrect. Little reward accompanies duplication and confirmation of what is already known and believed. The goal is new-search, not re-search. Not surprisingly, newly published discovery claims and credible discoveries that appear to be important and convincing will always be open to challenge and potential modification or refutation by future researchers. Second, novelty itself frequently provokes disbelief. Nobel Laureate and physiologist Albert Szent-Györgyi once described discovery as "seeing what everybody has seen and thinking what nobody has thought." But thinking what nobody else has thought and telling others what they have missed may not change their views. Sometimes years are required for truly novel discovery claims to be accepted and appreciated.
paragraphs.zh: 在整个可信度过程中存在两个悖论。首先,科学工作往往聚焦于现有知识中被视为不完整或不正确的某个方面。对已知和已被相信的内容进行重复和确认几乎没有回报。目标是新研究,而非再研究。毫不奇怪,新发表的发现声明和看似重要且令人信服的可信发现,总是会面临未来研究者的质疑以及潜在的修正或反驳。其次,新颖性本身常常引发怀疑。诺贝尔奖得主、生理学家Albert Szent-Györgyi曾将发现描述为"看到了每个人都看到的东西,却想到了没有人想到的东西"。但想到别人没想到的东西并告诉他人他们所遗漏的,可能不会改变他们的观点。有时需要数年时间,真正新颖的发现声明才能被接受和认可。

paragraphs.en: In the end, credibility "happens" to a discovery claim—a process that corresponds to what philosopher Annette Baier has described as the commons of the mind. "We reason together, challenge, revise, and complete each other's reasoning and each other's conceptions of reason."
paragraphs.zh: 最终,可信度"发生"在一项发现声明身上——这一过程对应于哲学家Annette Baier所描述的心灵共同体。"我们共同推理、质疑、修正并完善彼此的推理和彼此对理性的理解。"

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: If the trade unionist Jimmy Hoffa were alive today, he would probably represent civil servants. When Hoffa's Teamsters were in their prime in 1960, only one in ten American government workers belonged to a union; now 36% do. In 2009 the number of unionists in America's public sector passed that of their fellow members in the private sector. In Britain, more than half of public-sector workers but only about 15% of private-sector ones are unionized. There are three reasons for the public-sector unions' thriving. First, they can shut things down without suffering much in the way of consequences. Second, they are mostly bright and well-educated. A quarter of America's public-sector workers have a university degree. Third, they now dominate left-of-centre politics. Some of their ties go back a long way. Britain's Labor Party, as its name implies, has long been associated with trade unionism. Its current leader, Ed Miliband, owes his position to votes from public-sector unions. At the state level their influence can be even more fearsome. Mark Baldassare of the Public Policy Institute of California points out that much of the state's budget is patrolled by unions. The teachers' unions keep an eye on schools, the CCPOA on prisons and a variety of labor groups on health care. In many rich countries average wages in the state sector are higher than in the private one. But the real gains come in benefits and work practices. Politicians have repeatedly "backloaded" public-sector pay deals, keeping the pay increases modest but adding to holidays and especially pensions that are already generous. Reform has been vigorously opposed, perhaps most notoriously in education, where charter schools, academies and merit pay all faced drawn-out battles. Even though there is plenty of evidence that the quality of the teachers is the most important variable, teachers' unions have fought against getting rid of bad ones and promoting good ones. As the cost to everyone else has become clearer, politicians have begun to clamp down. In Wisconsin the unions have rallied thousands of supporters against Scott Walker, the hardline Republican governor. But many within the public sector suffer under the current system, too. John Donahue at Harvard's Kennedy School points out that the norms of culture in Western civil services suit those who want to stay put but are bad for high achievers. The only American public-sector workers who earn well above $250,000 a year are university sports coaches and the president of the United States. Bankers' fat pay packets have attracted much criticism, but a public-sector system that does not reward high achievers may be a much bigger problem for America.

When Hoffa's Teamsters were in their prime in 1960, only one in ten American government workers belonged to a union; now 36% do. In 2009 the number of unionists in America's public sector passed that of their fellow members in the private sector. In Britain, more than half of public-sector workers but only about 15% of private-sector ones are unionized.

paragraphs.en: There are three reasons for the public-sector unions' thriving. First, they can shut things down without suffering much in the way of consequences. Second, they are mostly bright and well-educated. A quarter of America's public-sector workers have a university degree. Third, they now dominate left-of-centre politics. Some of their ties go back a long way. Britain's Labor Party, as its name implies, has long been associated with trade unionism. Its current leader, Ed Miliband, owes his position to votes from public-sector unions.

paragraphs.zh: 在许多富裕国家,公共部门的平均工资高于私营部门。但真正的收益体现在福利和工作制度上。政客们反复对公共部门的薪酬协议采取"后置"做法,将加薪幅度控制得较为适度,但增加了假期,尤其是增加了本已十分慷慨的养老金。

paragraphs.en: Reform has been vigorously opposed, perhaps most notoriously in education, where charter schools, academies and merit pay all faced drawn-out battles. The court cannot [1] its legitimacy as guardian of the rule of law [2] justices behave like politicians. paragraphs.en: The framers of the Constitution envisioned law [10] having authority apart from politics. They gave justices permanent positions [11] they would be free to [12] those in power and have no need to [13] political support. Our legal system was designed to set law apart from politics precisely because they are so closely [14] .
paragraphs.zh: 宪法的制定者们设想法律拥有独立于政治的权威。他们赋予大法官终身职位,使他们能够自由地对抗当权者,而无需培植政治支持。我们的法律体系旨在将法律与政治分开,正是因为二者联系如此紧密。

paragraphs.en: Constitutional law is political because it results from choices rooted in fundamental social [15] like liberty and property. When the court deals with social policy decisions, the law it [16] is inescapably political – which is why decisions split along ideological lines are so easily [17] as unjust.
paragraphs.zh: 宪法法律具有政治性,因为它源于植根于自由和财产等基本社会概念的选择。当法院处理社会政策决定时,它所塑造的法律不可避免地具有政治性——这就是为什么沿意识形态路线分裂的裁决如此容易被斥为不公正。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned. School districts across the country, most recently Los Angeles Unified, are revising their thinking on this educational ritual. Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student's academic grade. This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework. But the policy is unclear and contradictory. Certainly, no homework should be assigned that students cannot complete on their own or that they cannot do without expensive equipment. But if the district is essentially giving a pass to students who do not do their homework because of complicated family lives, it is going riskily close to the implication that standards need to be lowered for poor children. District administrators say that homework will still be a part of schooling; teachers are allowed to assign as much of it as they want. But with homework counting for no more than 10% of their grades, students can easily skip half their homework and see very little difference on their report cards. Some students might do well on state tests without completing their homework, but what about the students who performed well on the tests and did their homework? It is quite possible that the homework helped. Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule. At the same time, the policy addresses none of the truly thorny questions about homework. If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students' academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing. Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade. Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct. The homework rules should be put on hold while the school board, which is responsible for setting educational policy, looks into the matter and conducts public hearings. It is not too late for L.A. Unified to do homework right.

Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade. Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时,该政策没有解决任何关于家庭作业的真正棘手问题。如果学区认为家庭作业对学生的学业成就不重要,就应该采取措施减少或取消作业,而不是让它们几乎不计分。相反,如果家庭作业很重要,它就应该占成绩的很大一部分。同时,该政策没有采取任何措施来确保学生收到的家庭作业是有意义的或适合他们的年龄和科目的,也没有确保教师布置的作业不超过他们愿意批改和纠正的数量。

paragraphs.en: The homework rules should be put on hold while the school board, which is responsible for setting educational policy, looks into the matter and conducts public hearings. It is not too late for L.A. Unified to do homework right.
paragraphs.zh: 家庭作业规定应该暂停执行,由负责制定教育政策的学校董事会调查此事并举行公开听证会。洛杉矶联合学区现在纠正家庭作业政策还为时不晚。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls' lives. It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls' identity to appearance. Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence. Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls' lives and interests. Girls' attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not. Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them. What's more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses. When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength. Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity. It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children's marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years. I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s. Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a "third stepping stone" between infant wear and older kids' clothes. It was only after "toddler" became a common shoppers' term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage. Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits. And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.

paragraphs.en: Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls' lives. It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls' identity to appearance. Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence. Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls' lives and interests.
paragraphs.zh: 粉红色真美：成年女性并不记得自己曾如此痴迷于这种颜色，然而它却充斥在我们年幼女孩的生活中。粉红色本身并非坏事，但它只是彩虹中极小的一部分，尽管它可能在某种程度上赞颂女孩特质，但它也反复而坚定地将女孩的身份与外表融合在一起。然后它呈现出这种联系，甚至在两岁大的孩子中间，将女孩们之间的这种联系不仅视为纯真的表现，而且视为纯真本身的证据。环顾四周，我对女孩生活和兴趣方面想象力的极度匮乏感到绝望。

paragraphs.en: Girls' attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not. Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them. What's more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses. When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength. Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity. It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children's marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩对粉红色的喜爱似乎不可避免，仿佛编码在她们的DNA中，但根据美国研究副教授Jo Paoletti的说法，事实并非如此。直到20世纪初，儿童才开始按颜色区分：在家用洗衣机出现之前的时代，出于实际考虑，所有婴儿都穿白色衣服,因为清洗衣物的唯一方法是煮沸它们。而且，男孩和女孩都穿被认为是中性的连衣裙。当育儿室颜色被引入时，粉红色实际上被认为是更具男性气质的颜色，是红色的柔和版本，与力量相关联。蓝色则因其让人联想到圣母玛利亚、坚定和忠诚，象征着女性气质。直到20世纪80年代中期，当放大年龄和性别差异成为儿童市场营销的主导策略时，粉红色才真正确立了自己的地位，它开始似乎天然地吸引女孩，成为定义她们作为女性的一部分，至少在最初几年的关键时期是如此。

paragraphs.en: I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.
paragraphs.zh: 我没有意识到市场营销趋势如此深刻地影响了我们对儿童天性的认知，包括我们关于他们心理发展的核心信念。以学步儿童为例。我原以为这个阶段是专家们经过多年研究儿童行为后提出的：错了。事实证明,根据儿童消费主义历史学家Daniel Cook的说法，它是在20世纪30年代作为服装制造商的营销手段而流行起来的。

paragraphs.en: Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a "third stepping stone" between infant wear and older kids' clothes. It was only after "toddler" became a common shoppers' term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage. Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits. And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
paragraphs.zh: 行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，它们应该在婴儿装和大龄儿童服装之间创造一个"第三个阶梯"。只有在"学步儿童"成为购物者的常用术语之后，它才演变成一个被广泛接受的发展阶段。将儿童或成人划分为越来越细小的类别已被证明是提高利润的可靠方法。而细分市场最简单的方法之一就是放大性别差异——或者在以前不存在差异的地方创造出差异。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: In 2010, a federal judge shook America's biotech industry to its core. Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades – by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented. But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable. Executives were violently agitated. The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a "preliminary step" in a longer battle. On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily. A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman's risk of breast cancer. The chief executive of Myriad, a company in Utah, said the ruling was a blessing to firms and patients alike. But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy. The Myriad case itself is probably not over. Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's. A growing number seem to agree. Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests. In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule "is no less a product of nature…than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds." Despite the appeals court's decision, big questions remain unanswered. For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it. The case may yet reach the Supreme Court. As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact. Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules – most are already patented or in the public domain. Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy. Companies are eager to win patents for "connecting the dots," explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO. Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term. The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents. Each meeting was packed.

paragraphs.en: In 2010, a federal judge shook America's biotech industry to its core. Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades – by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented. But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable. Executives were violently agitated. The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a "preliminary step" in a longer battle.

paragraphs.zh: 7月29日,他们松了一口气,至少是暂时的。一家联邦上诉法院推翻了之前的裁决,裁定Myriad Genetics公司确实可以持有两个有助于预测女性乳腺癌风险的基因的专利。这家位于犹他州的公司的首席执行官表示,这一裁决对企业和患者都是一件幸事。

paragraphs.en: But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy. The Myriad case itself is probably not over. Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's. paragraphs.zh: 但随着各公司继续尝试个性化医疗,法院将依然相当繁忙。Myriad案件本身很可能尚未结束。批评者提出了反对基因专利的三个主要论点:基因是自然产物,因此不可授予专利;基因专利抑制创新而非奖励创新;专利的垄断限制了人们获得诸如Myriad的基因检测的机会。越来越多的人似乎表示赞同。去年,一个联邦工作组敦促改革与基因检测相关的专利。10月,司法部在Myriad案件中提交了一份简报,论证称分离的DNA分子"与从棉籽中分离出来的棉纤维一样,都是自然产物"。

paragraphs.en: As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact. Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules – most are already patented or in the public domain. Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy. Companies are eager to win patents for "connecting the dots," explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,随着该行业的发展,其他诉讼可能会产生更大的影响。各公司不太可能再为人类DNA分子申请更多专利——大多数已经获得专利或进入公共领域。企业现在正在研究基因如何相互作用,寻找可能用于确定疾病原因或预测药物疗效的相关性。BIO的律师Hans Sauer解释说,各公司渴望赢得"连接各点"的专利。

paragraphs.en: Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term. The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents. Each meeting was packed.
paragraphs.zh: 它们的成功可能取决于与此问题相关的一起诉讼,该诉讼由Mayo Clinic提起,最高法院将在下一任期审理此案。BIO最近举办了一次会议,其中包括指导律师应对专利格局变化的研讨会。每场会议都座无虚席。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning. Before it ends, it will likely change the life course and character of a generation of young adults. And ultimately, it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years. No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster. Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others. In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off. At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending. But for the most part, these benefits seem thin, uncertain, and far off. In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms. Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes. Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one. Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them – especially for young people. The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind. In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society. More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society's character. In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results. We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric. But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend.

questions.stem: By saying "to find silver linings" (Line 1, Para. 2) the author suggests that the jobless try to____.
options: A) seek subsidies from the government
B) make profits from the troubled economy
C) explore reasons for the unemployment
D) look on the bright side of the recession
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是词义句意题，正确答案 D）look on the bright side of the recession 定位句在第 2 段：没有谁比失业者更卖力地想在这场全国性经济灾难里找到一丝光亮。许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，但在某些方面让自己变得更好：变得不那么物质主义、更懂得理财，也更体恤他人的不易。正确项与原文构成同义替换（to find silver linings in this national economic disaster ↔ look on the bright side of the recession）。其余三项中，A 项属选项含原文未出现的实体即无中生有、B 项属把抽象益处偷换成物质收益即偷换概念、C 项属回答的不是题目要解释的对象即答非所问，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇 37. According to Paragraph 2, the recession has made people ____. 答案是什么？为什么选 D？ 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the recession has made people ____.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 D）reconsider their lifestyle 定位句在第 2 段：至少，它把我们从 "轻易致富、住更大房子" 的全民狂热美梦中惊醒，给一个肆意消费的时代画上了必要的句点。正确项与原文构成同义替换（awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses ↔ reconsider their lifestyle；put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending ↔ reconsider their lifestyle）。其余三项中，A 项属把别段信息塞进本段即张冠李戴、B 项属选项与原文方向相反即反向干扰、C 项属拿原文关键词反向加工即反向干扰，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇 38. Benjamin Friedman believes that economic recessions may ____. 答案是什么？为什么选 B？ 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇

questions.stem: Benjamin Friedman believes that economic recessions may ____.
options: A) impose a heavier burden on immigrants
B) bring out more evils of human nature
C) promote the advance of rights and freedoms
D) ease conflicts between races and classes
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）bring out more evils of human nature 定位句在第 3 段：经济史学家本杰明·弗里德曼在《经济增长的道德后果》一书中指出，无论美国国内还是国外，经济长期停滞或衰退几乎总让社会变得更刻薄、更排他，通常也会让权利与自由的进步停滞甚至倒退。正确项与原文构成同义替换（lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive ↔ bring out more evils of human nature；have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms ↔ bring out more evils of human nature）。其余三项中，A 项属用次级具体例当主论点即以偏概全、C 项属拿原文短语反向粘动词即反向干扰、D 项属原词照搬+反义动词替换即反向干扰，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇 39. The research of Till Von Wachter suggests that in the recession graduates from elite universities tend to____. 答案是什么？为什么选 D？ 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇

questions.stem: The research of Till Von Wachter suggests that in the recession graduates from elite universities tend to____.
options: A) lag behind the others due to decreased opportunities
B) catch up quickly with experienced employees
C) see their life chances as dimmed as the others'
D) recover more quickly than the others
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 D）recover more quickly than the others 定位句在第 4 段：哥伦比亚大学经济学家蒂尔·冯·瓦赫特的研究表明，并非所有进入衰退期就业的人前景都被削弱：精英大学毕业生能较快追平自己若在景气年份毕业时本应达到的位置；落在后面的是他们之下的大众。正确项与原文构成同义替换（those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times ↔ recover more quickly than the others）。其余三项中，A 项属把对比的两组身份对调即张冠李戴、B 项属改写比较对象即偷换概念、C 项属忽略 not all 的范围限定即反向干扰，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇 40. The author thinks that the influence of hard times on society is ____. 答案是什么？为什么选 C？ 2012年考研英语二 阅读理解（四选一） 第 4 篇

questions.stem: The author thinks that the influence of hard times on society is ____.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是态度题，正确答案 C）certain 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend ↔ certain；it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years ↔ certain）。其余三项中，A 项属全文严肃话题选 "无关紧要" 即反向干扰、B 项属把 "保留判断" 误读为 "乐观" 即推过头、D 项属拿中段负面论据外推全文态度即推过头，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning. Before it ends, it will likely change the life course and character of a generation of young adults. And ultimately, it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years.
paragraphs.zh: 大衰退或许已经结束，但这个高失业率的时代可能才刚刚开始。在它结束之前，它很可能会改变一代年轻人的人生轨迹和性格特征。而且最终，它很可能在未来数年重塑我们的政治、我们的文化以及我们社会的特征。

paragraphs.en: No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster. Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others. In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off. At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending.
paragraphs.zh: 没有人比失业者更努力地试图在这场全国性经济灾难中寻找一线希望。许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，但在某些方面改善了他们：他们变得不那么物质主义，在财务上更加审慎；他们更能意识到他人的挣扎。在有限的方面，也许这场衰退会让社会变得更好。至少，它把我们从轻松致富和更大房子的全民狂热梦想中唤醒，并给一个鲁莽的个人消费时代画上了必要的句号。

paragraphs.en: But for the most part, these benefits seem thin, uncertain, and far off. In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms. Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes.
paragraphs.zh: 但在大多数情况下，这些好处似乎微薄、不确定且遥远。在《经济增长的道德后果》一书中，经济史学家Benjamin Friedman认为，无论在美国国内还是国外，漫长的经济停滞或衰退期几乎总是让社会变得更加刻薄、包容性更差，并且通常会阻止或逆转权利和自由的进步。反移民情绪通常会增加，种族和阶级之间的冲突也会增加。

paragraphs.en: Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one. Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them – especially for young people. The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind.
paragraphs.zh: 收入不平等通常在经济衰退期间会下降，但在这次衰退中并未缩小。事实上，这段经济疲软时期可能会强化阶级分化，并减少跨越阶级的机会——尤其是对年轻人而言。Columbia University经济学家Till Von Wachter的研究表明，并非所有在经济衰退期毕业的人都会看到自己的人生机会变暗：那些拥有精英大学学位的人能相当快地赶上他们在较好时期毕业本应达到的位置；而被抛在后面的是他们之下的大众。

paragraphs.en: In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society. More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society's character. In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results. We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric. But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend.
paragraphs.zh: 在互联网时代，特别容易看到一直隐藏在美国社会内部的怨恨。更困难的是，在当下准确辨别这些艰难时期如何影响社会性格。在许多方面，美国进入这次衰退时比其历史上任何时期都更具社会包容性，而此后关于社会冲突的各种全国性民调显示了好坏参半的结果。我们必须等待并观察这些艰难时期将如何重塑我们的社会结构。但它们肯定会重塑社会结构，而且持续时间越长，影响就越大。

blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 A）served。后文紧接 "the people they liberated"，说明这些人是参战并解放他人的盟军士兵。其余三项：B）performed 搭配偏义：perform in 多指"演出/表演"，与战争语境违和、C）rebelled 逻辑反向：rebel = 反叛，与盟军"解放他人"完全冲突、D）betrayed 色彩反向：betray = 背叛，是贬义，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 2 空（词义辨析）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 2 空正确答案 B）common。下文用 "穷苦农家娃""普通人" 一连串同位语为这个形容词作注脚。其余三项：A）actual 义偏：actual 强调"实际/真实"，不指"普通"、C）special 反向：special 与下文"穷苦平凡"完全冲突、D）normal 近义但搭配弱：normal man 不是表达"普通老百姓"的地道说法，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 3 空（固定搭配）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 3 空正确答案 D）bore。本句平行结构 "slept in cold foxholes... went without food and shelter... stuck it out" 全是"扛下苦难"。其余三项：A）loaded 搭配反向：load 是"装载（到某人身上）"，主语通常是施加方、B）eased 义反：ease the burdens = 减轻负担，与坚守苦难矛盾、C）removed 义反：remove the burdens = 卸下负担，方向相反，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 4 空（词义辨析）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 4 空正确答案 A）necessities。went without 直接点明"连最基本的都没"，定位"必需品"。其余三项：B）facilities 义偏：facilities 是"设施/设备"，不指"食物住所本身"、C）commodities 义偏：commodities = 商品（经济学语境）、D）properties 义偏：property 是财产/地产或属性，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 5 空（逻辑关系）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 5 空正确答案 C）but。本句构成 "not X, not Y, but Z" 的经典对比结构。其余三项：A）and 义弱：and 表并列，不能精准呈现"反差/纠正"、B）nor 继续否定方向错：nor 等于 and not，会让 C 也变否定、D）hence 逻辑错：hence = 因此，表因果，不是对比，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 6 空（固定搭配）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 6 空正确答案 D）against。短语 be up against = 面对/对抗（强敌）。其余三项：A）for 搭配错：up for 多表"愿意做"或"轮到"、B）into 搭配错：up into 不是固定短语、C）from 搭配错：up from 多表"从……起来"，无对抗义，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 7 空（词义辨析）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 7 空正确答案 B）meaning。主语是 abbreviation（缩写），缩写=A 代表 B 的对应关系。其余三项：A）implying 义偏：imply = 暗含、不明说地表达、C）symbolizing 义偏：symbolize = 象征，含抽象比喻色彩、D）claiming 义偏：claim = 宣称、声称，主语通常是人，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 8 空（词义辨析）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 8 空正确答案 A）handed out。前文说 Government Issue（政府配发），物品的去向是"发给士兵"。其余三项：B）turned over 义偏：turn over = 移交（权力/物品所有权）、C）brought back 义反：bring back = 带回，方向反向、D）passed down 义偏：pass down = 代代相传，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 9 空（固定搭配）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 9 空正确答案 C）made。下句"美国从没有 Joe 当总统"反向印证"没爬上去"。其余三项：A）pushed 搭配错：push it to the top 不是固定表达、B）got 搭配错：get to the top 不带 it，且 got it to the top 不通顺、D）managed 搭配错：manage 不带 it 加 to the top，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 10 空（逻辑关系）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 10 空正确答案 B）never。上句 never 已定否定基调。其余三项：A）ever 极性反：ever 在肯定句中="曾经"，与全文走向冲突、C）either 句法错：either 不能直接修饰动词作"也不"用、D）neither 句法错：neither 不与单一句的动词组合成否定，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 11 空（词义辨析）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 18 空正确答案 C）fragments。冒号后只列"咖啡、烟、威士忌、住处、睡眠"等零碎日常。其余三项：A）stages 义偏：stages of civilization = 文明的（发展）阶段、B）illusions 义偏：illusions = 幻觉/错觉，与实物清单不符、D）advances 义偏：advances of civilization = 文明的进步，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 19 空（固定搭配）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 19 空正确答案 B）To。末句 "the most important person in their lives" 中 their 指这些国家的人。其余三项：A）With 义偏：with 表伴随/同……，无法直接表"在他们眼里"、C）Among 义偏：Among 表"在……之间"，宾语应是同类成员、D）Beyond 义偏：Beyond = 超越/在……之外，均可排除。 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一） 第 20 空（逻辑关系）填 A/B/C/D 哪个？为什么？ 2012年考研英语二 完形填空（四选一）

第 20 空正确答案 D）at that point。全文反复对比 "现在 vs 当年"，本句要锁定"当年那时"。其余三项：A）on the contrary 义偏：on the contrary 表"恰恰相反"，前后必须对立、B）by this means 义偏：by this means 表"以此方式"，需有方法可指、C）from the outset 义偏：from the outset = 从一开始就，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Millions of Americans and foreigners see G.I. Joe as a mindless war toy, the symbol of American military adventurism, but that's not how it used to be. To the men and women who [1] in World War II and the people they liberated, the G.I. was the [2] man grown into hero, the poor farm kid torn away from his home, the guy who [3] all the burdens of battle, who slept in cold foxholes, who went without the [4] of food and shelter, who stuck it out and drove back the Nazi reign of murder. This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, [5] an average guy, up [6] the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.
paragraphs.zh: 数百万美国人和外国人将G.I. Joe视为一个无思想的战争玩具,是美国军事冒险主义的象征,但它过去并非如此。对于在二战中服役的男女军人以及他们解放的人民而言,G.I.是成长为英雄的普通人,是被迫离开家园的贫苦农家子弟,是承受战斗所有重负的人,是睡在冰冷散兵坑里的人,是缺少食物和住所等生活必需品的人,是坚持到底并击退纳粹杀戮统治的人。这不是志愿兵,不是报酬丰厚的人,而是普通人,面对的却是几个世纪以来训练最精良、装备最精良、最凶猛、最残暴的敌人。

paragraphs.en: His name isn't much. G.I. is just a military abbreviation [7] Government Issue, and it was on all of the articles [8] to soldiers. And Joe? A common name for a guy who never [9] it to the top. Joe Blow, Joe Palooka, Joe Magrac…a working class name. The United States has [10] had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe.
paragraphs.zh: 他的名字并不起眼。G.I.只是一个军事缩写,意思是Government Issue(政府配发),它出现在发给士兵的所有物品上。那Joe呢?一个从未出人头地的普通人的常见名字。Joe Blow、Joe Palooka、Joe Magrac……一个工人阶级的名字。美国从未有过一位名叫Joe的总统、副总统或国务卿。

paragraphs.en: G.I. Joe had a [11] career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops. He appears as a character, or a [12] of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle. Some of the soldiers Pyle [13] portrayed themselves in the film. Pyle was famous for covering the [14] side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers, not how many miles were [15] or what towns were captured or liberated. His reports [16] the "Willie" cartoons of famed Stars and Stripes artist Bill Mauldin. Both men [17] the dirt and exhaustion of war, the [18] of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep. [19] Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, [20] the most important person in their lives.
paragraphs.zh: G.I. Joe在与德国、日本和朝鲜军队的作战中有着卓越的战绩。他作为一个角色,或者说一组美国人的性格集合,出现在1945年的电影《G.I. Joe的故事》中,该片基于战地记者Ernie Pyle的最后战地岁月。Pyle采访过的一些士兵在影片中扮演他们自己。Pyle以报道战争的人性面而闻名,他书写的是那些满身尘土、冰雪和泥泞的士兵,而不是推进了多少英里或占领或解放了哪些城镇。他的报道与著名《星条旗报》艺术家Bill Mauldin的"Willie"漫画相呼应。两人都强调战争的肮脏和疲惫,强调士兵们彼此之间以及与平民分享的文明碎片:咖啡、烟草、威士忌、住所、睡眠。对于埃及、法国和其他十几个国家来说,G.I. Joe就是任何一名美国士兵,在那个时刻是他们生命中最重要的人。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: In the 2006 film version of The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, scolds her unattractive assistant for imagining that high fashion doesn't affect her. Priestly explains how the deep blue color of the assistant's sweater descended over the years from fashion shows to department stores and to the bargain bin in which the poor girl doubtless found her garment. This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn't be more out of date or at odds with the feverish world described in Overdressed, Elizabeth Cline's three-year indictment of "fast fashion". In the last decade or so, advances in technology have allowed mass-market labels such as Zara, H&M, and Uniqlo to react to trends more quickly and anticipate demand more precisely. Quicker turnarounds mean less wasted inventory, more frequent releases, and more profit. These labels encourage style-conscious consumers to see clothes as disposable – meant to last only a wash or two, although they don't advertise that – and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks. By offering on-trend items at dirt-cheap prices, Cline argues, these brands have hijacked fashion cycles, shaking an industry long accustomed to a seasonal pace. The victims of this revolution, of course, are not limited to designers. For H&M to offer a $5.95 knit miniskirt in all its 2,300-plus stores around the world, it must rely on low-wage overseas labor, order in volumes that strain natural resources, and use massive amounts of harmful chemicals. Overdressed is the fashion world's answer to consumer-activist bestsellers like Michael Pollan's The Omnivore's Dilemma. "Mass-produced clothing, like fast food, fills a hunger and need, yet is non-durable and wasteful," Cline argues. Americans, she finds, buy roughly 20 billion garments a year – about 64 items per person – and no matter how much they give away, this excess leads to waste. Towards the end of Overdressed, Cline introduced her ideal, a Brooklyn woman named Sarah Kate Beaumont, who since 2008 has made all of her own clothes – and beautifully. But as Cline is the first to note, it took Beaumont decades to perfect her craft; her example can't be knocked off. Though several fast-fashion companies have made efforts to curb their impact on labor and the environment – including H&M, with its green Conscious Collection line – Cline believes lasting change can only be effected by the customer. She exhibits the idealism common to many advocates of sustainability, be it in food or in energy. Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can't afford not to.

paragraphs.en: In the 2006 film version of The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, scolds her unattractive assistant for imagining that high fashion doesn't affect her. Priestly explains how the deep blue color of the assistant's sweater descended over the years from fashion shows to department stores and to the bargain bin in which the poor girl doubtless found her garment.
paragraphs.zh: 在2006年的电影版《穿普拉达的女王》中,由梅丽尔·斯特里普饰演的米兰达·普里斯特利斥责她那位缺乏时尚感的助理,因为后者认为高级时装与自己无关。普里斯特利解释了助理毛衣的深蓝色是如何经年累月地从时装秀流向百货商店,再流向廉价货区,而这个可怜的女孩无疑是在那里找到她的衣服的。

paragraphs.en: This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn't be more out of date or at odds with the feverish world described in Overdressed, Elizabeth Cline's three-year indictment of "fast fashion". In the last decade or so, advances in technology have allowed mass-market labels such as Zara, H&M, and Uniqlo to react to trends more quickly and anticipate demand more precisely. Quicker turnarounds mean less wasted inventory, more frequent releases, and more profit. These labels encourage style-conscious consumers to see clothes as disposable – meant to last only a wash or two, although they don't advertise that – and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks. By offering on-trend items at dirt-cheap prices, Cline argues, these brands have hijacked fashion cycles, shaking an industry long accustomed to a seasonal pace.
paragraphs.zh: 这种自上而下的时装业构想已经完全过时,与伊丽莎白·克莱因在《过度着装》中描述的那个狂热世界格格不入。《过度着装》是她对"快时尚"长达三年的控诉。在过去十年左右的时间里,技术进步使得Zara、H&M和Uniqlo等大众市场品牌能够更快地对潮流做出反应,更精准地预测需求。更快的周转意味着更少的库存浪费、更频繁的新品发布和更多的利润。这些品牌鼓励注重风格的消费者将衣服视为一次性用品——只能洗一两次就不能穿了,尽管它们不会宣传这一点——并且每隔几周就更新一次衣橱。克莱因认为,通过以极低的价格提供时尚单品,这些品牌劫持了时尚周期,撼动了一个长期习惯于季节性节奏的行业。

paragraphs.en: The victims of this revolution, of course, are not limited to designers. For H&M to offer a $5.95 knit miniskirt in all its 2,300-plus stores around the world, it must rely on low-wage overseas labor, order in volumes that strain natural resources, and use massive amounts of harmful chemicals.
paragraphs.zh: 当然,这场革命的受害者不仅限于设计师。为了让H&M能够在其全球2300多家门店提供5.95美元的针织迷你裙,它必须依赖低工资的海外劳工,订购量大到损耗自然资源,并使用大量有害化学品。

paragraphs.en: Overdressed is the fashion world's answer to consumer-activist bestsellers like Michael Pollan's The Omnivore's Dilemma. "Mass-produced clothing, like fast food, fills a hunger and need, yet is non-durable and wasteful," Cline argues. Americans, she finds, buy roughly 20 billion garments a year – about 64 items per person – and no matter how much they give away, this excess leads to waste.
paragraphs.zh: 《过度着装》是时装界对迈克尔·波伦的《杂食者的困境》等消费者维权类畅销书的回应。克莱因认为:"大规模生产的服装就像快餐一样,满足了饥饿和需求,但却不耐用且浪费。"她发现,美国人每年购买约200亿件服装——人均约64件——无论他们捐赠多少,这种过量都会导致浪费。

paragraphs.en: Towards the end of Overdressed, Cline introduced her ideal, a Brooklyn woman named Sarah Kate Beaumont, who since 2008 has made all of her own clothes – and beautifully. But as Cline is the first to note, it took Beaumont decades to perfect her craft; her example can't be knocked off.
paragraphs.zh: 在《过度着装》接近尾声时,克莱因介绍了她的理想典范,一位名叫莎拉·凯特·博蒙特的布鲁克林女性,她从2008年起就自己制作所有衣服——而且做得很漂亮。但正如克莱因首先指出的那样,博蒙特花了几十年时间才完善她的手艺;她的榜样无法被复制。

paragraphs.en: Though several fast-fashion companies have made efforts to curb their impact on labor and the environment – including H&M, with its green Conscious Collection line – Cline believes lasting change can only be effected by the customer. She exhibits the idealism common to many advocates of sustainability, be it in food or in energy. Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can't afford not to.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管几家快时尚公司已经努力遏制它们对劳工和环境的影响——包括H&M及其环保的Conscious Collection系列——但克莱因认为,持久的变革只能由消费者来实现。她展现了许多可持续发展倡导者所共有的理想主义,无论是在食品还是能源领域。虚荣心是永恒的;只有当人们负担不起不可持续的消费时,他们才会开始更可持续地购物。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: An old saying has it that half of all advertising budgets are wasted – the trouble is, no one knows which half. In the internet age, at least in theory, this fraction can be much reduced. By watching what people search for, click on and say online, companies can aim "behavioural" ads at those most likely to buy. In the past couple of weeks a quarrel has illustrated the value to advertisers of such fine-grained information: Should advertisers assume that people are happy to be tracked and sent behavioural ads? Or should they have explicit permission? In December 2010 America's Federal Trade Commission (FTC) proposed adding a "do not track" (DNT) option to internet browsers, so that users could tell advertisers that they did not want to be followed. Microsoft's Internet Explorer and Apple's Safari both offer DNT; Google's Chrome is due to do so this year. In February the FTC and the Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) agreed that the industry would get cracking on responding to DNT requests. On May 31st Microsoft set off the row. It said that Internet Explorer 10, the version due to appear with Windows 8, would have DNT as a default. Advertisers are horrified. Human nature being what it is, most people stick with default settings. Few switch DNT on now, but if tracking is off it will stay off. Bob Liodice, the chief executive of the Association of National Advertisers, says consumers will be worse off if the industry cannot collect information about their preferences. People will not get fewer ads, he says. "They'll get less meaningful, less targeted ads." It is not yet clear how advertisers will respond. Getting a DNT signal does not oblige anyone to stop tracking, although some companies have promised to do so. Unable to tell whether someone really objects to behavioural ads or whether they are sticking with Microsoft's default, some may ignore a DNT signal and press on anyway. Also unclear is why Microsoft has gone it alone. After all, it has an ad business too, which it says will comply with DNT requests, though it is still working out how. If it is trying to upset Google, which relies almost wholly on advertising, it has chosen an indirect method: there is no guarantee that DNT by default will become the norm. DNT does not seem an obviously huge selling point for windows 8 – though the firm has compared some of its other products favourably with Google's on that count before. Brendon Lynch, Microsoft's chief privacy officer, blogged: "We believe consumers should have more control." Could it really be that simple?
