The Parkrun phenomenon began with a dozen friends and has inspired 400 events in the UK and more abroad. Events are free, staffed by thousands of volunteers. Runners range from four years old to grandparents; their times range from Andrew Baddeley's world record 13 minutes 48 seconds up to an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 每周六上午9点,超过5万名跑步者出发在当地公园跑5公里。Parkrun现象始于十几个朋友,如今已在英国催生了400场活动,国外还有更多。活动免费,由数千名志愿者提供服务。跑步者从4岁儿童到祖父母辈不等;他们的成绩从Andrew Baddeley创造的13分48秒世界纪录到1小时不等。

paragraphs.en: Parkrun is succeeding where London's Olympic "legacy" is failing. Ten years ago on Monday, it was announced that the Games of the 30th Olympiad would be in London. Planning documents pledged that the great legacy of the Games would be to lever a nation of sport lovers away from their couches. The population would be fitter, healthier and produce more winners. It has not happened. The number of adults doing weekly sport did rise, by nearly 2 million in the run-up to 2012 – but the general population was growing faster. Worse, the numbers are now falling at an accelerating rate. The opposition claims primary school pupils doing at least two hours of sport a week have nearly halved. Obesity has risen among adults and children. Official retrospections continue as to why London 2012 failed to "inspire a generation." The success of Parkrun offers answers.
paragraphs.zh: Parkrun在伦敦奥运会"遗产"失败的地方取得了成功。十年前的周一,第30届奥林匹克运动会宣布将在伦敦举办。规划文件承诺,奥运会的伟大遗产将是撬动一个热爱运动的国家离开沙发。人口将更健康,产生更多赢家。但这并未发生。在2012年前夕,每周参加体育运动的成年人数量确实增加了近200万,但总人口增长更快。更糟的是,现在这些数字正在加速下降。反对派声称每周至少参加两小时体育运动的小学生几乎减半。成人和儿童的肥胖率都上升了。关于伦敦2012年为何未能"激励一代人"的官方反思仍在继续。Parkrun的成功提供了答案。

paragraphs.en: Parkun is not a race but a time trial: Your only competitor is the clock. The ethos welcomes anybody. There is as much joy over a puffed-out first-timer being clapped over the line as there is about top talent shining. The Olympic bidders, by contrast, wanted to get more people doing sport and to produce more elite athletes. The dual aim was mixed up: The stress on success over taking part was intimidating for newcomers.
paragraphs.zh: Parkrun不是一场比赛而是计时赛:你唯一的竞争对手是时钟。其理念欢迎任何人。当气喘吁吁的初次参加者在掌声中冲过终点线时的欢乐,与顶尖人才闪耀时的欢乐一样多。相比之下,奥运申办者想让更多人参加体育运动并培养更多精英运动员。这一双重目标混淆了:强调成功而非参与对新人来说令人生畏。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, there is something a little absurd in the state getting involved in the planning of such a fundamentally "grassroots" concept as community sports associations. If there is a role for government, it should really be getting involved in providing common goods – making sure there is space for playing fields and the money to pave tennis and netball courts, and encouraging the provision of all these activities in schools. But successive governments have presided over selling green spaces, squeezing money from local authorities and declining attention on sport in education. Instead of wordy, worthy strategies, future governments need to do more to provide the conditions for sport to thrive. Or at least not make them worse.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上,政府参与规划社区体育协会这样一个根本上属于"草根"的概念,确实有些荒谬。如果政府有作用,它真正应该做的是参与提供公共产品——确保有运动场地的空间和铺设网球场和无挡板篮球场的资金,并鼓励学校提供所有这些活动。但历届政府却主持出售绿地,挤压地方当局的资金,减少对教育中体育的关注。未来的政府需要做更多工作来提供体育繁荣的条件,而不是空洞的、冠冕堂皇的战略。或者至少不要让情况变得更糟。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: With so much focus on children's use of screens, it's easy for parents to forget about their own screen use. "Tech is designed to really suck you in," says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, "and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement. It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine." Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise. She found that mothers who used devices during the exercise started 20 per cent fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children. During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family. Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention. Infants are wired to look at parents' faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive – as they often are when absorbed in a device – it can be extremely disconcerting for the children. Radesky cites the "still face experiment" devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s. In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother's attention. "Parents don't have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need," says Radesky. On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids' use of screens are born out of an "oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting" with their children: "It's based on a somewhat fantasised, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you're failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them." Tronick believes that just because a child isn't learning from the screen doesn't mean there's no value to it – particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child. Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way. This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.

questions.stem: According to Jenny Radesky, digital products are designed to____.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）absorb user attention 定位句在第 1 段：Jenny Radesky 在其数字游戏研究中说：科技被设计得真的会把你吸进去，数字产品的存在就是为了促进最大化的用户投入。正确项与原文构成同义替换（suck you in ↔ absorb user attention；promote maximal engagement ↔ absorb user attention）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Radesky's food-testing exercise shows that mothers' use of devices____.
options: C) slows down babies' verbal development
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 D）reduces mother-child communication 定位句在第 2 段：她发现实验中使用设备的母亲与孩子发起的言语互动减少了 20%、非言语互动减少了 39%。正确项与原文构成同义替换（fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children ↔ reduces mother-child communication）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Radesky cites the "still face experiment" to show that____.
options: A) it is easy for children to get used to blank expressions
B) verbal expressions are unnecessary for emotional exchange
C) children are insensitive to changes in their parents' mood
D) parents need to respond to children's emotional needs
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是例证目的题，正确答案 D）parents need to respond to children's emotional needs 定位句在第 3 段：Radesky 说：父母不必时时刻刻精致地陪伴，但需要有平衡，父母需要对孩子言语或非言语的情感需求保持回应与敏感。正确项与原文构成同义替换（parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need ↔ parents need to respond to children's emotional needs）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The oppressive ideology mentioned by Tronick requires parents to____.
options: A) protect kids from exposure to wild fantasies
B) teach their kids at least 30,000 words a year
C) ensure constant interaction with their children
D) remain concerned about kids' use of screens
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）ensure constant interaction with their children 定位句在第 4 段：另一方面，Tronick 本人担心，对孩子使用屏幕的种种担忧源自一种压迫性的意识形态，这种意识形态要求父母必须始终与孩子互动。正确项与原文构成同义替换（parents should always be interacting ↔ ensure constant interaction with their children）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Tronick, kids' use of screens may____.
options: A) give their parents some free time
B) make their parents more creative
C) help them with their homework
D) help them become more attentive
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是细节题，正确答案 A）give their parents some free time 定位句在第 4 段：Tronick 认为，孩子没有从屏幕里学到东西并不意味着屏幕没有价值——尤其当它给父母腾出时间洗澡、做家务或干脆从孩子身边喘口气时。正确项与原文构成同义替换（gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child ↔ give their parents some free time）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属答非所问、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: With so much focus on children's use of screens, it's easy for parents to forget about their own screen use. "Tech is designed to really suck you in," says Jenny Radesky in her study of digital play, "and digital products are there to promote maximal engagement. It makes it hard to disengage, and leads to a lot of bleed-over into the family routine."
paragraphs.zh: 由于过多关注儿童使用屏幕的问题,家长很容易忘记自己对屏幕的使用。Jenny Radesky在她关于数字化游戏的研究中说:"科技的设计就是要真正吸引你,数字产品的存在是为了促进最大程度的参与。这使人难以脱离,并导致大量渗透到家庭日常生活中。"

paragraphs.en: Radesky has studied the use of mobile phones and tablets at mealtimes by giving mother-child pairs a food-testing exercise. She found that mothers who used devices during the exercise started 20 per cent fewer verbal and 39 per cent fewer nonverbal interactions with their children. During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family. Parents would be looking at their emails while the children would be making excited bids for their attention.
paragraphs.zh: Radesky研究了用餐时使用手机和平板电脑的情况,她让母子配对进行食物测试练习。她发现,在练习过程中使用设备的母亲与孩子进行的语言互动减少了百分之二十,非语言互动减少了百分之三十九。在另一次观察中,她看到手机成为家庭中紧张关系的来源。父母会查看电子邮件,而孩子们则会兴奋地争取他们的注意力。

paragraphs.en: Infants are wired to look at parents' faces to try to understand their world, and if those faces are blank and unresponsive – as they often are when absorbed in a device – it can be extremely disconcerting for the children. Radesky cites the "still face experiment" devised by developmental psychologist Ed Tronick in the 1970s. In it, a mother is asked to interact with her child in a normal way before putting on a blank expression and not giving them any visual social feedback: The child becomes increasingly distressed as she tries to capture her mother's attention. "Parents don't have to be exquisitely present at all times, but there needs to be a balance and parents need to be responsive and sensitive to a child's verbal or nonverbal expressions of an emotional need," says Radesky.
paragraphs.zh: 婴儿天生会看着父母的脸来试图理解他们的世界,如果这些脸是空白和无反应的——就像沉浸在设备中时经常出现的那样——这对孩子来说可能会非常令人不安。Radesky引用了发展心理学家Ed Tronick在二十世纪七十年代设计的"静止面孔实验"。在实验中,要求一位母亲先以正常方式与孩子互动,然后面无表情,不给孩子任何视觉社交反馈:随着孩子试图吸引母亲的注意力,她变得越来越焦虑。Radesky说:"父母不必时刻都极度专注,但需要有一个平衡,父母需要对孩子的语言或非语言情感需求表达做出回应和敏感。"

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, Tronick himself is concerned that the worries about kids' use of screens are born out of an "oppressive ideology that demands that parents should always be interacting" with their children: "It's based on a somewhat fantasised, very white, very upper-middle-class ideology that says if you're failing to expose your child to 30,000 words you are neglecting them." Tronick believes that just because a child isn't learning from the screen doesn't mean there's no value to it – particularly if it gives parents time to have a shower, do housework or simply have a break from their child. Parents, he says, can get a lot out of using their devices to speak to a friend or get some work out of the way. This can make them feel happier, which lets them be more available to their child the rest of the time.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面,Tronick本人担心对孩子使用屏幕的忧虑源于一种"压迫性的意识形态,要求父母应该始终与孩子互动":"这基于一种有些理想化的、非常白人的、非常中上阶层的意识形态,认为如果你没有让孩子接触三万个单词,你就是在忽视他们。"Tronick认为,仅仅因为孩子没有从屏幕中学习并不意味着它没有价值——特别是如果它能让父母有时间洗澡、做家务或只是从孩子那里休息一下。他说,父母可以通过使用设备与朋友交谈或完成一些工作而获得很多好处。这可以让他们感到更快乐,从而让他们在其余时间更能陪伴孩子。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year. After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn't it? And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn't feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn't academic. But while this may be true, it's not a good enough reason to condemn gap years. There's always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated "race to the finish line," whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career. But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits – in fact, it probably enhances it. Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not. Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes – all things that first-year students often struggle with the most. Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders. If you're not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once. This isn't surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college. Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game. At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department. Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.

questions.stem: One of the reasons for high-school graduates not taking a gap year is that____.
options: A) they think it academically misleading
B) they have a lot of fun to expect in college
C) it feels strange to do differently from others
D) it seems worthless to take off-campus courses
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 C）it feels strange to do differently from others 定位句在第 1 段：毕竟，要是你认识的所有人秋天都要去上大学，单单自己留一年看上去就很傻，不是吗？而且上了 12 年学之后，再花一年时间去做非学业的事，本就不太自然。正确项与原文构成同义替换（if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year ↔ it feels strange to do differently from others）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Studies from the US and Australia imply that taking a gap year helps____.
options: A) keep students from being unrealistic
B) lower risks in choosing careers
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是推断题，正确答案 D）relieve freshmen of pressures 定位句在第 3 段：美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，相比不休 gap year 的学生，休过 gap year 的学生进大学时通常准备得更充分、表现也更好。gap year 非但不会让学生落后，反而推他们一把——让他们提前准备好独立、新责任和环境变化，而这些恰恰是大一新生最易吃力的方面。正确项与原文构成同义替换（all things that first-year students often struggle with the most ↔ relieve freshmen of pressures）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属过度推断、C 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The word "acclimation" (Para. 3) is closest in meaning to____.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是词义句意题，正确答案 A）adaptation 定位句在第 3 段：gap year 的经历能在适应大学、被抛进全新环境时减轻冲击，让学生更容易把心思放在学业和活动上，而非花在适应不良的失误上。正确项与原文构成同义替换（adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment ↔ adaptation）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: A gap year may save money for students by helping them____.
options: D) decide on the right major
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 D）decide on the right major 定位句在第 4 段：许多学生申请大学时填一个专业，上了课之后又换另一个。这本身不一定是坏事，但要看学校，换得太晚要补学分，可能很费钱。例如在波士顿学院，要从别的院系转去护理学院得多读一年。一开始就用 gap year 把事情想清楚，能减少日后压力、省下日后的开销。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on ↔ decide on the right major）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属过度推断、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The most suitable title for this text would be____.
options: A) In Favor of the Gap Year
B) The ABCs of the Gap Year
C) The Gap Year Comes Back
D) The Gap Year: A Dilemma
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）In Favor of the Gap Year 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits – in fact, it probably enhances it ↔ In Favor of the Gap Year；Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not ↔ In Favor of the Gap Year；Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on ↔ In Favor of the Gap Year）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Today, widespread social pressure to immediately go to college in conjunction with increasingly high expectations in a fast-moving world often causes students to completely overlook the possibility of taking a gap year. After all, if everyone you know is going to college in the fall, it seems silly to stay back a year, doesn't it? And after going to school for 12 years, it doesn't feel natural to spend a year doing something that isn't academic.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，普遍存在的立即上大学的社会压力，加上快速发展的世界中日益增高的期望，常常导致学生完全忽视间隔年的可能性。毕竟，如果你认识的每个人都在秋季上大学，那么推迟一年似乎很愚蠢，不是吗？而且在上了12年学之后，花一年时间做一些非学术性的事情感觉并不自然。

paragraphs.en: But while this may be true, it's not a good enough reason to condemn gap years. There's always a constant fear of falling behind everyone else on the socially perpetuated "race to the finish line," whether that be toward graduate school, medical school or a lucrative career. But despite common misconceptions, a gap year does not hinder the success of academic pursuits – in fact, it probably enhances it.
paragraphs.zh: 但尽管这可能是事实，却不足以成为谴责间隔年的充分理由。人们总是不断担心在社会延续的"冲向终点线的竞赛"中落后于其他所有人，无论那是通向研究生院、医学院还是一份高薪职业。但尽管存在普遍的误解，间隔年并不会阻碍学业追求的成功——事实上，它可能会增强成功。

paragraphs.en: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not. Rather than pulling students back, a gap year pushes them ahead by preparing them for independence, new responsibilities and environmental changes – all things that first-year students often struggle with the most. Gap year experiences can lessen the blow when it comes to adjusting to college and being thrown into a brand new environment, making it easier to focus on academics and activities rather than acclimation blunders.
paragraphs.zh: 来自美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，经历间隔年的学生通常比没有经历间隔年的学生为大学做了更好的准备，并且在大学中表现更好。间隔年不是把学生拉回来，而是通过让他们为独立、新责任和环境变化做好准备来推动他们前进——这些都是大一新生往往最难应对的事情。间隔年经历可以减轻适应大学和被投入全新环境时的冲击，使人更容易专注于学业和活动，而不是适应过程中的失误。

paragraphs.en: If you're not convinced of the inherent value in taking a year off to explore interests, then consider its financial impact on future academic choices. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, nearly 80 percent of college students end up changing their majors at least once. This isn't surprising, considering the basic mandatory high school curriculum leaves students with a poor understanding of the vast academic possibilities that await them in college. Many students find themselves listing one major on their college applications, but switching to another after taking college classes. It's not necessarily a bad thing, but depending on the school, it can be costly to make up credits after switching too late in the game. At Boston College, for example, you would have to complete an extra year were you to switch to the nursing school from another department. Taking a gap year to figure things out initially can help prevent stress and save money later on.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你不相信用一年时间探索兴趣的内在价值，那么请考虑它对未来学业选择的财务影响。根据美国国家教育统计中心的数据，近80%的大学生最终至少换过一次专业。这并不令人惊讶，因为高中基础必修课程使学生对大学中等待他们的广阔学术可能性了解甚少。许多学生发现自己在大学申请中列出一个专业，但在上了大学课程后换到另一个专业。这不一定是坏事，但取决于学校，如果换专业太晚，补学分可能代价高昂。例如在Boston College，如果你从其他院系转到护理学院，就必须额外完成一年学业。最初花一年间隔年来弄清楚这些事情，可以帮助防止压力并在以后节省金钱。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Though often viewed as a problem for western states, the growing frequency of wildfires is a national concern because of its impact on federal tax dollars, says Professor Max Moritz, a specialist in fire ecology and management. In 2015, the US Forest Service for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget fighting fires – nearly double the percentage it spent on such efforts 20 years ago. In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency's other work – such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep – that affect the lives of all Americans. Another nationwide concern is whether public funds from other agencies are going into construction in fire-prone districts. As Moritz puts it, how often are federal dollars building homes that are likely to be lost to a wildfire? "It's already a huge problem from a public expenditure perspective for the whole country," he says. "We need to take a magnifying glass to that. Like, 'Wait a minute, is this OK?' Do we want instead to redirect those funds to concentrate on lower-hazard parts of the landscape?" Such a view would require a corresponding shift in the way US society today views fire, researchers say. For one thing, conversations about wildfires need to be more inclusive. Over the past decade, the focus has been on climate change – how the warming of the Earth from greenhouse gases is leading to conditions that worsen fires. While climate is a key element, Moritz says, it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation. "The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked, and the interactions go both ways," he says. Failing to recognize that, he notes, leads to "an overly simplified view of what the solutions might be. Our perception of the problem and of what the solution is becomes very limited." At the same time, people continue to treat fire as an event that needs to be wholly controlled and unleashed only out of necessity, says Professor Balch at the University of Colorado. But acknowledging fire's inevitable presence in human life is an attitude crucial to developing the laws, policies, and practices that make it as safe as possible, she says. "We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire," Balch says. "It is really important to understand and try and tease out what is the human connection with fire today."

questions.stem: More frequent wildfires have become a national concern because in 2015 they____.
options: B) consumed a record-high percentage of budget
C) severely damaged the ecology of western states
D) caused a huge rise of infrastructure expenditure
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 B）consumed a record-high percentage of budget 定位句在第 2 段：2015年，美国林务局有史以来首次把其55亿美元年度预算的过半用于救火——几乎是它20年前同类支出占比的两倍。正确项与原文构成同义替换（for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget ↔ consumed a record-high percentage of budget）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Moritz calls for the use of "a magnifying glass" to____.
options: A) raise more funds for fire-prone areas
B) avoid the redirection of federal money
C) find wildfire-free parts of the landscape
D) guarantee safer spending of public funds
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 D）guarantee safer spending of public funds 定位句在第 4 段：我们得拿放大镜审视这件事。就好像"等等，这样真的OK吗？"——我们是不是该把那些钱转去用在风险更低的地段？正确项与原文构成同义替换（redirect those funds to concentrate on lower-hazard parts of the landscape ↔ guarantee safer spending of public funds；Wait a minute, is this OK? ↔ guarantee safer spending of public funds）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属范围程度偷改，均可排除。

questions.stem: While admitting that climate is a key element, Moritz notes that____.
options: A) public debates have not settled yet
C) other factors should not be overlooked
D) a shift in the view of fire has taken place
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 C）other factors should not be overlooked 定位句在第 7 段：Moritz说，虽然气候是一个关键因素，但它不应以牺牲方程式其余部分为代价。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation ↔ other factors should not be overlooked）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属答非所问、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The overly simplified view Moritz mentions is a result of failing to____.
options: A) discover the fundamental makeup of nature
B) explore the mechanism of the human systems
C) maximize the role of landscape in human life
D) understand the interrelations of man and nature
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 D）understand the interrelations of man and nature 定位句在第 8 段：他说，人类系统与我们栖居的景观是相互关联的，相互作用是双向的。他指出，没认清这一点，就会导致"对解决方案视野的过度简化"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The human systems and the landscapes we live on are linked ↔ understand the interrelations of man and nature；Failing to recognize that ↔ failing to ... understand）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属以偏概全、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Professor Balch points out that fire is something man should____.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是细节题，正确答案 B）come to terms with 定位句在第 9 段：但她说，承认火在人类生活中不可避免的存在，是制定使其尽可能安全的法律、政策与实践所必须的一种态度。正确项与原文构成同义替换（acknowledging fire's inevitable presence in human life ↔ come to terms with；We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire ↔ come to terms with）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: In 2015, the US Forest Service for the first time spent more than half of its $5.5 billion annual budget fighting fires – nearly double the percentage it spent on such efforts 20 years ago. In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency's other work – such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep – that affect the lives of all Americans.

paragraphs.zh: 另一个全国性的关切是,来自其他机构的公共资金是否正流向火灾高发地区的建设。正如Moritz所说,联邦资金有多少次在建造可能毁于野火的房屋?

paragraphs.en: Such a view would require a corresponding shift in the way US society today views fire, researchers say.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,这种观点需要美国社会对火灾的看法发生相应的转变。

paragraphs.en: For one thing, conversations about wildfires need to be more inclusive. Over the past decade, the focus has been on climate change – how the warming of the Earth from greenhouse gases is leading to conditions that worsen fires.
paragraphs.zh: 首先,关于野火的讨论需要更具包容性。过去十年,焦点一直集中在气候变化上,即温室气体导致的地球变暖如何造成恶化火灾的条件。

paragraphs.en: While climate is a key element, Moritz says, it shouldn't come at the expense of the rest of the equation.
paragraphs.zh: Moritz表示,虽然气候是一个关键因素,但不应以牺牲等式中的其他部分为代价。

Failing to recognize that, he notes, leads to "an overly simplified view of what the solutions might be. Our perception of the problem and of what the solution is becomes very limited."
paragraphs.zh: 他说:"人类系统和我们生活的地貌是相互关联的,这种相互作用是双向的。"他指出,未能认识到这一点,会导致"对解决方案可能是什么产生过于简化的看法。我们对问题的认知和对解决方案的认知变得非常有限。"

paragraphs.en: At the same time, people continue to treat fire as an event that needs to be wholly controlled and unleashed only out of necessity, says Professor Balch at the University of Colorado. But acknowledging fire's inevitable presence in human life is an attitude crucial to developing the laws, policies, and practices that make it as safe as possible, she says.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时,Colorado大学的Balch教授表示,人们继续将火灾视为需要完全控制、仅在必要时才释放的事件。但她说,承认火灾在人类生活中不可避免的存在,是制定使其尽可能安全的法律、政策和实践的关键态度。

paragraphs.en: "We've disconnected ourselves from living with fire," Balch says. "It is really important to understand and try and tease out what is the human connection with fire today."
paragraphs.zh: Balch说:"我们已经将自己与火共生的状态割裂开来。理解并努力梳理出当今人类与火灾的联系是什么,这一点非常重要。"

[6] , today's unemployed don't seem to be having a great time. One Gallup poll found that 20 percent of Americans who have been unemployed for at least a year report having depression, double the rate for [7] Americans. Also, some research suggests that the [8] for rising rates of mortality, mental-health problems, and addiction [9] poorly-educated, middle-aged people is a shortage of well-paid jobs. "When I come home from a hard day's work, I often feel [18] ," Danaher says, adding, "In a world in which I don't have to work, I might feel rather different" – perhaps different enough to throw himself [19] a hobby or a passion project with the intensity usually reserved for [20] matters.

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs? Don't dismiss that possibility entirely. About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed. Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don't appeal to robots. But many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest, or soon will. The rich own the robots, so they will be fine. This isn't to be alarmist. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. The Industrial Revolution didn't go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting. The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. Curriculums – from grammar school to college – should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication. Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots. Online education can supplement the traditional kind. It could make extra training and instruction affordable. Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt. The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier. In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines. The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven't been invented yet. The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them. Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality. Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts. But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

questions.stem: Who will be most threatened by automation?
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 D）Middle-class workers. 定位句在第 2 段：据牛津大学一项研究，约半数美国岗位有被自动化取代的高风险，而中产阶级被不成比例地挤压。园艺、日托这类低收入工作机器人看不上；但卡车驾驶、理财顾问、软件工程等许多中产职业已经吸引了它们的兴趣，或很快会。富人拥有机器人，所以富人没事。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the middle class disproportionately squeezed ↔ Middle-class workers；many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest ↔ Middle-class workers）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents the author's view?
options: A) Worries about automation are in fact groundless.
B) Optimists' opinions on new tech find little support.
C) Issues arising from automation need to be tackled.
D) Negative consequences of new tech can be avoided.
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）Issues arising from automation need to be tackled. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting ↔ Issues arising from automation need to be tackled；But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable ↔ Issues arising from automation need to be tackled）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属过度推断、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Education in the age of automation should put more emphasis on____
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 A）creative potential. 定位句在第 4 段：从小学到大学的课程应当演变为少记忆事实、多侧重创造力和复杂沟通。正确项与原文构成同义替换（creativity and complex communication ↔ creative potential）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author suggests that tax policies be aimed at____
options: A) encouraging the development of automation.
B) increasing the return on capital investment.
C) easing the hostility between rich and poor.
D) preventing the income gap from widening.
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 D）preventing the income gap from widening. 定位句在第 6 段：最后，由于自动化有扩大资本收入与劳动收入差距的危险，税收和社会保障必须被重新思考。正确项与原文构成同义替换（because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income ↔ preventing the income gap from widening）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: In this text, the author presents a problem with____
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是主旨题，正确答案 B）possible solutions to it. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training ↔ possible solutions to it；Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought ↔ possible solutions to it）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs?
paragraphs.zh: 中产阶级面临的诸多恼人挑战中,有一个在下届总统竞选中可能不会被提及:当机器人来抢他们的工作时会发生什么?

paragraphs.en: Don't dismiss that possibility entirely. About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed. Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don't appeal to robots. But many middle-class occupations – trucking, financial advice, software engineering – have aroused their interest, or soon will. The rich own the robots, so they will be fine.
paragraphs.zh: 不要完全忽视这种可能性。根据牛津大学的一项研究,美国约有一半的工作面临被自动化取代的高风险,而中产阶级受到的挤压尤为严重。园艺或日托等低收入工作对机器人没有吸引力。但许多中产阶级职业——卡车运输、金融咨询、软件工程——已经引起了它们的兴趣,或很快就会引起。富人拥有机器人,所以他们不会有事。

paragraphs.en: This isn't to be alarmist. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. The Industrial Revolution didn't go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting.
paragraphs.zh: 这并非危言耸听。乐观主义者指出,技术变革在过去曾使工人受益。工业革命对那些工作被机械织布机取代的卢德分子来说并不顺利,但它最终提高了生活水平,创造的就业岗位多于摧毁的岗位。同样,自动化最终应该会提高生产率,通过降低价格来刺激需求,并将工人从艰苦、枯燥的工作中解放出来。但在中期内,中产阶级工人可能需要大量帮助来适应。

paragraphs.en: The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. Curriculums – from grammar school to college – should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication. Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots. Online education can supplement the traditional kind. It could make extra training and instruction affordable. Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.
paragraphs.zh: 正如Erik Brynjolfsson和Andrew McAfee在《第二次机器时代》中所论述的,第一步应该是重新思考教育和职业培训。从小学到大学的课程设置应该演变为更少地关注记忆事实,更多地关注创造力和复杂沟通。职业学校应该更好地培养解决问题的能力,并帮助学生与机器人协同工作。在线教育可以补充传统教育。它可以使额外的培训和指导变得负担得起。试图获得新技能的专业人士将能够在不负债的情况下做到这一点。

paragraphs.en: The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier. In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines. The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven't been invented yet. The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.
paragraphs.zh: 应对自动化挑战凸显了美国重振其日渐衰退的商业活力的必要性:必须让创办新公司变得更容易。在以往技术剧变的时代,企业家通过构想将劳动力和机器相结合的方式来平滑过渡。3D打印机和虚拟现实的最佳用途尚未被发明出来。美国需要将发明这些用途的新公司。

paragraphs.en: Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.
paragraphs.zh: 最后,由于自动化有可能扩大资本收入和劳动收入之间的差距,税收和社会保障网必须重新考虑。需要削减对低工资劳动的税收,并应扩大工资补贴,如劳动所得税抵免:这将提高收入,鼓励工作,奖励创造就业机会的公司,并减少不平等。

paragraphs.en: Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts. But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.
paragraphs.zh: 技术将在未来几年以或大或小的方式改善社会,但这对于那些生活和职业被自动化颠覆的人来说将无济于事。摧毁那些来抢我们工作的机器是愚蠢的。但帮助工人适应的政策将是不可或缺的。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump's use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform. Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant. Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded. Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement. Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group. So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 1 and 2, many young Americans cast doubts on____
options: A) the justification of the news-filtering practice.
B) people's preference for social media platforms.
C) the administration's ability to handle information.
D) social media as a reliable source of news.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 D）social media as a reliable source of news. 定位句在第 1 段：其言下之意是：千禧一代更愿意白宫的新闻经由其他渠道过滤呈现，而不是来自总统的社交媒体平台。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform ↔ social media as a reliable source of news；as distrust has risen toward all media ↔ social media as a reliable source of news）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The phrase "beef up" (Line 2, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to____

questions.stem: According to the Knight Foundation survey, young people____
options: A) tend to voice their opinions in cyberspace.
B) verify news by referring to diverse sources.

questions.stem: The Barna survey found that a main cause for the fake news problem is____
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）readers' misinterpretation. 定位句在第 5 段：Barna 调查机构的一项调查发现，美国人为"假新闻现象"列出的首要原因是"读者错误"，其权重高于编造的新闻和报道中的事实错误。约三分之一的人认为，假新闻的问题在于通过社交媒体对真实新闻进行"误读或夸大"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," ↔ readers' misinterpretation；misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news ↔ readers' misinterpretation）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: A) A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online.
B) A Counteraction Against the Over-tweeting Trend.
C) The Accumulation of Mutual Trust on Social Media.

questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media ↔ A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online；beef up their media literacy skills ↔ A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online）。其余三项中，B 项属以偏概全、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

paragraphs.zh: Harvard大学的一项新调查发现,超过三分之二的美国年轻人不赞成特朗普总统使用Twitter。这意味着千禧一代更希望来自白宫的新闻经过其他渠道过滤,而不是通过总统的社交媒体平台。

Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.

A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded.
paragraphs.zh: 作为数字原住民的年轻人确实在网络空间中越来越善于区分事实与虚构。Knight Foundation对14至24岁年轻人进行的焦点小组调查发现,他们使用"分布式信任"来核实报道。他们交叉核对信息源,并偏好来自不同视角的新闻——尤其是那些公开表明任何偏见的新闻。该调查总结道:"许多年轻人承担了大量个人责任来教育自己,并积极寻求对立的观点。"

paragraphs.en: Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.
paragraphs.zh: 这种主动研究可能产生另一种效果。University of Wisconsin-Madison在澳大利亚、英国和美国进行的一项2014年调查发现,年轻人对社交媒体的依赖导致了更高的政治参与度。

paragraphs.en: Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体让用户能够更亲密、更即时地体验新闻事件,同时也允许他们将新闻作为其价值观和兴趣的投射进行再次分享。这迫使用户更加意识到自己在传递信息中的角色。Barna研究小组的一项调查发现,美国人对假新闻现象给出的首要原因是"读者错误",而不是编造的故事或报道中的事实错误。大约三分之一的人表示假新闻问题在于通过社交媒体对"实际新闻的误读或夸大"。换句话说,在社交媒体上分享新闻的选择可能是问题的核心。Barna Group主编Roxanne Stone说:"这表明在应对这一问题上存在真正的个人责任。"

paragraphs.en: So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.
paragraphs.zh: 因此,当年轻人批评一位过度发推特的总统时,他们展现出思维技能上的心智自律——以及在何时于社交媒体上分享内容的选择上的自律。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy. DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value. The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more. The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?
options: A) It caused conflicts among tech giants.
B) It failed to pay due attention to patients' rights.
C) It fell short of the latter's expectations.
D) It put both sides into a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 B）It failed to pay due attention to patients' rights. 定位句在第 1 段：正是在这一背景下，信息专员 Elizabeth Denham 对 NHS 旗下的 Royal Free 医院信托基金做出了严厉的裁决——该信托在 2015 年依据一份措辞含糊的协议，把 160 万患者的记录交给了 DeepMind，而这份协议远远没有充分顾及患者的权利及其对隐私的期待。正确项与原文构成同义替换（took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy ↔ failed to pay due attention to patients' rights）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham's verdict with____
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 C）necessary adjustments. 定位句在第 2 段：DeepMind 已经近乎道歉，NHS 信托基金则已经改正了自己的做法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The NHS trust has mended its ways ↔ necessary adjustments）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that____
options: A) privacy protection must be secured at all costs.
B) leaking patients' data is worse than selling it.
C) making profits from patients' data is illegal.
D) the value of data comes from the processing of it.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是主旨题，正确答案 D）the value of data comes from the processing of it. 定位句在第 2 段：但这种区分忽略了一个要点：让数据产生价值的是处理与聚合，而不是仅仅占有这些数据。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value ↔ the value of data comes from the processing of it）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is____
options: A) the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
B) the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
C) the uncontrolled use of new software.
D) the monopoly of big data by tech giants.
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是细节题，正确答案 D）the monopoly of big data by tech giants. 定位句在第 4 段：这种做法（仅用隐私法约束）并没有应对真正的担忧。仅仅说 DeepMind 开发的算法将造福患者、挽救生命还不够；真正要紧的是，这些算法将归属于一家用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources ↔ the monopoly of big data by tech giants）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is____
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是态度题，正确答案 B）cautious. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. ↔ cautious.；small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. ↔ cautious.）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.
paragraphs.zh: 任何对英国国家医疗服务体系(NHS)与DeepMind之间交易所带来危险的公正评估,都必须首先承认双方的出发点是好的。DeepMind是世界领先的人工智能(AI)公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗保健的潜力非常巨大,但它也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。正是在这样的背景下,信息专员Elizabeth Denham对NHS下属的Royal Free医院信托发出了严厉的裁决,该信托在2015年基于一项含糊的协议将160万患者的记录移交给了DeepMind,而该协议对患者的权利和他们对隐私的期望考虑得太少。

paragraphs.en: DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.
paragraphs.zh: DeepMind几乎已经道歉。NHS信托已经改正了做法。未来NHS与DeepMind之间的安排——可能会有很多——将受到仔细审查,以确保已向患者征求所有必要的许可,并且所有不必要的数据已被清除。关于患者知情同意方面有一些教训需要汲取。但隐私并不是本案中唯一的角度,甚至不是最重要的角度。Denham女士选择将责任集中在NHS信托身上,因为根据现行法律,它"控制"着数据,而DeepMind仅仅是"处理"数据。但这种区分忽略了一个要点,即赋予数据价值的是处理和汇总,而不是仅仅拥有数据片段。

paragraphs.en: The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
paragraphs.zh: 重大问题是谁应该从我们生活现在产生的所有数据的分析中受益。隐私法建立在可识别的个人信息对个人造成损害这一概念之上。这忽视了监控经济的运作方式。个人数据只有在与无数百万人的数据进行比较时才能获得其价值。

paragraphs.en: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.
paragraphs.zh: 在这个案例中使用隐私法来遏制科技巨头感觉有些不太适应。这种做法并未解决真正的担忧。仅仅说DeepMind开发的算法将使患者受益并挽救生命是不够的。重要的是,这些算法将属于一家使用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。如果软件承诺能够像现在的药物一样大规模挽救生命,那么可以预期大数据会像大型制药公司那样行事。我们仍处于这场革命的开端,现在的小选择以后可能会产生巨大的后果。要避免数字封建主义的未来,需要进行长期的斗争。Denham女士的报告是一个值得欢迎的开端。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality. And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization. Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions. If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they're getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21st century.

Scientists have found that exposure [8] this hormone puts us in a trusting [9] : In a Swiss study, researchers sprayed oxytocin into the noses of half the subjects; those subjects were ready to lend significantly higher amounts of money to strangers than were their [10] who inhaled something else.

The tester would ask, "What's in here?" before looking into the container, smiling, and exclaiming, "Wow!" Each subject was then invited to look [15] . reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future. Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain? As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle. But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype…that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says. On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so. But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all – and the subtle devaluing of anything less – misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained. In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap. Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.

questions.stem: A broken bike chain is mentioned to show students' lack of____.
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 A）practical ability 定位句在第 2 段：什么时候开始大家就接受了这样一种想法：学生应该能说出美国第 13 任总统的名字，但面对一根坏掉的自行车链子就完全束手无策？正确项与原文构成同义替换（be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain ↔ practical ability）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: There exists the prejudice that vocational education is for kids who____.

questions.stem: The headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all____.

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward Koziatek's school can be described as____.
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是态度题，正确答案 A）supportive 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. ↔ supportive；Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap. ↔ supportive）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future.
paragraphs.zh: 令人好奇的是,Stephen Koziatek几乎感到自己必须为努力给学生创造更好未来的行为进行辩护。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain?

paragraphs.en: As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle.

paragraphs.en: But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype…that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says.

paragraphs.en: On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.
paragraphs.zh: 一方面,这种观点是美国演变的逻辑产物。制造业不再是曾经的经济引擎。美国经济曾经为高中毕业生提供的工作保障已在很大程度上消失了。接受更多教育成为新的原则。我们为孩子们想要更多,这理所应当。

paragraphs.en: But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all – and the subtle devaluing of anything less – misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.
paragraphs.zh: 但不顾一切地推动所有人获得学士学位——以及对任何更低学历的微妙贬低——忽略了重要的一点:这并非美国经济需要的唯一东西。是的,学士学位能打开更多大门。但即使现在,全国54%的工作是中等技能工作,如建筑业和高技能制造业。但只有44%的工人接受了充分培训。

There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.
paragraphs.zh: 换句话说,在工人阶级已让这个国家在政治上发生剧变的时刻,他们对曾经定义美国的机会正在消失感到沮丧,一个显而易见的解决方案正摆在我们面前。工人阶级岗位存在缺口,但最需要这些工作的工人却不具备胜任能力。Koziatek的Manchester School of Technology High School正试图填补这一缺口。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: While fossil fuels – coal, oil, gas – still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line. Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years. In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration. President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers. The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely. The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years. While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up – perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.

questions.stem: The word "plummeting" (Line 3, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to____.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是词义句意题，正确答案 C）falling 定位句在第 2 段：但越来越多的故事是关于可再生能源（尤其是风能与太阳能）价格的暴跌：过去八年里太阳能板成本下降了 80%，风电机组成本下降了近三分之一。正确项与原文构成同义替换（dropped by 80 percent ↔ falling）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, the use of renewable energy in America____.
options: B) is as extensive as in Europe
D) has proved to be impractical
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是细节题，正确答案 A）is progressing notably 定位句在第 3 段：在世界其他地方（尤其是中国和欧洲）领先的同时，美国也在经历一场显著变革：据美国能源信息署报道，今年 3 月，风能和太阳能首次占到美国发电总量的 10% 以上。正确项与原文构成同义替换（seeing a remarkable shift ↔ is progressing notably；for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent ↔ is progressing notably）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned that in Iowa, ____.
options: A) wind is a widely used energy source
B) wind energy has replaced fossil fuels
C) tech giants are investing in clean energy
