paragraphs.zh: 马德里在清洁空气问题上的反复提醒人们,欧洲各地(英国也深陷其中)针对空气污染所做努力的零散的、逐个城市推进的方式存在局限性。

paragraphs.en: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically controversial, and therefore vulnerable. That's because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers—who must pay fees or buy better vehicles—rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution. It's not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London. The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year's mayoral election. And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
paragraphs.zh: 在其他弱点之中,当城市被迫独自应对污浊空气时必须采用的措施在政治上具有争议性,因此容易受到攻击。这是因为这些措施不可避免地将清洁空气的成本转嫁到个人驾驶者身上——他们必须支付费用或购买更好的车辆——而不是转嫁到汽车制造商身上,而制造商的作弊行为才是我们有毒污染的真正原因。不难想象伦敦也会发生类似的逆转。新的超低排放区(Ulez)很可能成为明年市长选举的一个重大议题。如果Sadiq Khan获胜并按照他的计划在2021年将其扩展到北环路和南环路,这必将引发数量多得多的驾车者的强烈反对,因为届时他们将受到影响。

paragraphs.en: It's not that measures such as London's Ulez are useless. Far from it. Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents' health in the face of a serious threat. The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是说像伦敦的Ulez这样的措施毫无用处。恰恰相反。地方官员正在使用他们可用的手段,在面对严重威胁时保护居民的健康。这些区域确实在一定程度上改善了空气质量,科学告诉我们这意味着真正的健康益处。

paragraphs.en: But mayors and councilors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town. They are acting because national governments—Britain's and others across Europe—have failed to do so.
paragraphs.zh: 但市长和市议员对于这个远大于任何一个城市或城镇的问题所能做的十分有限。他们之所以采取行动,是因为国家政府——英国和欧洲其他国家——未能做到这一点。

paragraphs.en: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas—city centres, "school streets", even individual roads—are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance. Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution. We're doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
paragraphs.zh: 将高污染车辆限制在特定区域之外——市中心、"学校街道",甚至单独的道路——是对缺乏更大努力来适当执行现有法规并要求汽车公司使其车辆符合规定的一种回应。威尔士引入了特殊的低速限制以减少污染。我们正在做一切事情,却没有坚持要求制造商清理他们的汽车。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring—the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year—the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks. Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades. And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them. If "entitled" is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious. According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists. Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like. They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both. They aren't interested in taking any chances. The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt. College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve. One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind. In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose). Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good. That's a big change from the previous generation. "Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives," notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth. "Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy. They have trouble seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse."

questions.stem: Generation Zs graduating college this spring ____.
options: A) are recognized for their abilities
B) are optimistic about the labor market
C) are in favor of office job offers
D) are drawing growing public attention
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 D）are drawing growing public attention 定位句在第 1 段：既然 Z 世代成员（最普遍的定义是 1995 年之后出生的人，前后一两年误差）今春就要大学毕业，最近几周对他们的关注一直在稳步上升。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks ↔ are drawing growing public attention）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Generation Zs are keenly aware ____.
options: A) what their parents expect of them
B) how valuable a counselor's advice is
C) what a tough economic situation is like
D) how they differ from past generations
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 C）what a tough economic situation is like 定位句在第 2 段：Z 世代清楚地知道经济崩盘是什么样子。2008 年大崩盘时，他们正是易受影响的孩子，许多人的父母在那时丢了工作、积蓄，或两者皆失。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like ↔ what a tough economic situation is like）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The word "assuage"(line 9, para. 2) is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是词义句意题，正确答案 D）relieve 定位句在第 2 段：蓬勃发展的经济似乎几乎没能缓解这一代人内心隐隐的焦灼急迫感，对有大学贷款的人尤其如此。正确项与原文构成同义替换（done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency ↔ relieve）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属答非所问、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that Generation Zs ____.
options: A) give top priority to professional training
B) have a clear idea about their future job
C) care little about their job performance
D) think it hard to achieve work-life balance
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是推断题，正确答案 B）have a clear idea about their future job 定位句在第 3 段：Accenture 的一项调查发现，今年 88% 的应届毕业生在选专业时心里已经想好了一份工作。正确项与原文构成同义替换（chose their major with a job in mind ↔ have a clear idea about their future job）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Michelsen thinks that compared with millennials, Generation Zs are ____.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是细节题，正确答案 B）less adventurous 定位句在第 4 段："Z 世代正寻求更多的确定性和稳定性，原因是零工经济的兴起。他们看不清财务未来，且非常厌恶冒险。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（they are quite risk averse ↔ less adventurous；Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability ↔ less adventurous）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring—the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year—the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks. Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that's tighter than it's been in decades. And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
paragraphs.zh: 随着Z世代成员在今春大学毕业——最普遍接受的定义认为这一代人出生于1995年之后，上下浮动一年——近几周来关注度一直在稳步上升。Z世代即将走上街头,在一个数十年来最为紧俏的劳动力市场中寻找工作。根据美国大学与雇主协会进行的一项调查,雇主们计划今年在美国为应届毕业生提供的工作岗位比去年多约17%。每个人都想知道那些即将入驻空置办公隔间的人将与他们的前辈有何不同。

paragraphs.en: If "entitled" is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious. According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists. Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like. They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both. They aren't interested in taking any chances. The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt. College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
paragraphs.zh: 如果说"有权利意识"是最常用来形容千禧一代(出生于1981年至1995年间的人)的形容词,无论公平与否,那么Z世代的关键词则是务实和谨慎。根据研究他们的职业顾问和专家所言,Z世代是目光清醒的经济实用主义者。尽管毕业时正值过去50年来最好的经济形势,Z世代却清楚经济崩溃是什么样子。2008年金融危机时他们正处于易受影响的孩童时期,当时他们的许多父母失去了工作或毕生积蓄,或两者皆失。他们不想冒任何风险。蓬勃发展的经济似乎并未缓解这一代人潜在的焦虑紧迫感,尤其是对那些背负大学债务的人而言。根据美国联邦储备委员会的数据,美国大学贷款余额目前已达创纪录的1.5万亿美元。

paragraphs.en: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind. In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose). Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
paragraphs.zh: 埃森哲的一项调查发现,今年88%的应届毕业生在选择专业时就考虑到了工作。与此同时,在2019年对乔治亚大学学生的一项调查中,就业办公室发现未来雇主最令人向往的特质是能够提供稳定的就业机会(其次是职业发展和培训,然后是鼓舞人心的目标)。工作保障或稳定性是第二重要的职业目标(工作与生活的平衡排名第一),其次是致力于某项事业的使命感或为更大利益服务的良好感觉。

paragraphs.en: That's a big change from the previous generation. "Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives," notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth. "Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy. They have trouble seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse."
paragraphs.zh: 这与上一代人相比是一个巨大的变化。"千禧一代希望生活更加灵活,"英国品牌管理公司YouthSight的副主任Tanya Michelsen指出,该公司定期对英国青年进行60天调查,其研究结果同样适用于美国青年。"Z世代正在寻求更多的确定性和稳定性,因为零工经济的兴起。他们难以看到财务前景,而且相当规避风险。

第 4 空正确答案 C）describe。上段'难下定义'反衬本段'更易描述'。其余三项：A）amuse 义偏'逗乐'，离题、B）assist 动作对象错位、D）train 义偏'训练'，不接段际逻辑，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 A）while。想做耐心父母 vs 做起来不容易。其余三项：B）because 因果倒置、C）unless 条件指向错、D）once 时间条件不合理，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 B）task。前文已把'保持耐心'定性为一件'事'。其余三项：A）answer 搭配冷且指代不通、C）choice 改变所指、D）access 搭配不通，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 A）tolerant。composed 给出'平和沉稳'的方向。其余三项：B）formal 侧重'正式'，方向偏、C）rigid 色彩相反、D）critical 情绪倾向相反，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 C）push。下句'失去耐心、对孩子大喊'是结果。其余三项：A）move 搭配不熟，方向偏感情、B）drag 义偏'拖拽'，无情绪极限义、D）send 缺补足成分，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 D）inevitable。上句'被逼过头'为本句铺垫'必然发生'。其余三项：A）mysterious '神秘'与上下文不接、B）illogical 与因果链冲突、C）suspicious '可疑'语义错位，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 C）harsh。'and does nobody any good'暗示这话有伤害性。其余三项：A）boring 无伤害维度、B）naive 评价'幼稚'，与情绪失控无关、D）vague '含糊'与情境不合，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 A）turn back。'start over'明示'重新来过'。其余三项：B）take apart '拆开'语义不通、C）set aside '搁置'语义反向、D）cover up '掩盖'对象错配，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 C）However。上段宽慰 vs 本段警示。其余三项：A）Overall 总括副词，位置不对、B）Instead 替代关系不存在、D）Otherwise '否则'无前置条件，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 D）regret。上段 turn back the clock 与下文'伤害'双重指向悔意。其余三项：A）like 色彩相反、B）miss 对象错配、C）believe 义偏'相信'，与悔意无关，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 B）affect。'do damage'已给同向方向。其余三项：A）raise 方向相反、C）justify '证明…合理'对象错配、D）reflect '反映'非动作影响，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 D）cool。下文'emotional control'反证'失控'。其余三项：A）time lose your time 不表'失控'、B）bond 义偏'关系断裂'，搭配冷、C）race 义偏'赛跑'，离题，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 C）importance。下文'a skill that will help them all throughout life'凸显重要。其余三项：A）nature 未讲'本质'，方向偏、B）secret 无'隐藏机制'意味、D）context '语境'对象错位，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 D）confronted。情绪调节的对象是'压力情境'。其余三项：A）cheated 搭配不通、语义偏、B）defeated 结果义已'被打败'，与'维持控制'矛盾、C）confused 搭配冷、方向偏，均可排除。
第 18 空正确答案 B）hard。下句'A more practical goal'反衬'全天耐心难'。其余三项：A）terrible 色彩太负面、C）strange 义偏'奇怪'，离题、D）wrong 立场相悖，均可排除。
第 19 空正确答案 A）trying。'tolerant and composed'反推情境性质。其余三项：B）changing 义偏'在变化的'，与忍耐无关、C）exciting 色彩反向、D）surprising 义偏'出乎意料'，与忍耐无对应，均可排除。
第 20 空正确答案 B）emerge。'feeling better physically and emotionally'明示积极结果。其余三项：A）hide '躲藏'色彩与 benefit 相悖、C）withdraw '退缩/撤离'，方向消极、D）escape '逃避'与'努力面对'立场冲突，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Being a good parent is, of course, what every parent would like to be. But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very [1] , particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting. A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, [2] , a younger sibling.
paragraphs.zh: 成为一个好家长当然是每位家长都想做到的。但要定义好家长意味着什么无疑是非常棘手的,尤其是因为孩子们对同样的教养方式会有不同的反应。一个性格平和、遵守规则的孩子可能对某种教养方式反应更好,而不同于比如说一个年幼的弟弟妹妹。

paragraphs.en: [3] , there's another sort of parent that's a bit easier to [4] : a patient parent. Children of every age benefit from patient parenting. Still, [5] every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy [6] . Sometimes parents get exhausted and frustrated and are unable to maintain a [7] and composed style with their kids. I understand this.
paragraphs.zh: 幸运的是,还有另一种家长更容易描述:有耐心的家长。各个年龄段的孩子都能从有耐心的教养中受益。然而,尽管每位家长都想有耐心,但这并非易事。有时家长会感到筋疲力尽和沮丧,无法对孩子保持宽容和镇定的态度。我理解这一点。

paragraphs.en: You're only human, and sometimes your kids can [8] you just a little too far. And then the [9] happens: You lose your patience and either scream at your kids or say something that was a bit too [10] and does nobody any good. You wish that you could [11] the clock and start over. We've all been there.
paragraphs.zh: 你也是人,有时你的孩子可能会把你逼得有点过头。然后不可避免的事情就发生了:你失去了耐心,要么对孩子大喊大叫,要么说了一些过于严厉且对谁都没有好处的话。你希望能让时光倒流,重新开始。我们都经历过这种情况。

paragraphs.en: [12] , even though it's common, it's important to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may [13] for a long time. This may not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also [14] your child's self-esteem.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,尽管这很常见,但重要的是要记住,在疲惫的某个瞬间,你可能会对孩子说出让你长期后悔的话。这不仅可能损害你与孩子的关系,还可能影响孩子的自尊心。

paragraphs.en: If you consistently lose your [15] with your kids, then you are inadvertently modeling a lack of emotional control for your kids. We are all becoming increasingly aware of the [16] of modeling tolerance and patience for the younger generation. This is a skill that will help them all throughout life. In fact, the ability to emotionally regulate or maintain emotional control when [17] by stress is one of the most important of all life's skills.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你经常对孩子发脾气,那么你就在无意中为孩子树立了缺乏情绪控制的榜样。我们都越来越意识到为年轻一代树立宽容和耐心榜样的重要性。这是一项将使他们终身受益的技能。事实上,在面对压力时进行情绪调节或保持情绪控制的能力是人生最重要的技能之一。

paragraphs.en: Certainly, it's incredibly [18] to maintain patience at all times with your children. A more practical goal is to try, to the best of your ability, to be as tolerant and composed as you can when faced with [19] situations involving your children. I can promise you this: As a result of working toward this goal, you and your children will benefit and [20] from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally.
paragraphs.zh: 当然,始终对孩子保持耐心是极其困难的。一个更实际的目标是,在面对涉及孩子的棘手情况时,尽你所能地尽量保持宽容和镇定。我可以向你保证:朝着这个目标努力,你和你的孩子都将受益,并在度过压力时刻后感觉身心都更好。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise. This year's rise, an average of 2.7 per cent, may be a fraction lower than last year's, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation. Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer. Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey? Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North. However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years. It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel. The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions. However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered. The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate. This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain's railways. Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, punctuated by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently. The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.

questions.stem: The author holds that this year's increase in rail passenger fares____
options: A) has kept pace with inflation.
B) is a big surprise to commuters.
D) will ease train operators' burden.
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 C）remains an unreasonable measure. 定位句在第 1 段：今年涨幅平均 2.7%，可能比去年略低，但仍远高于官方消费者物价指数（CPI）所衡量的通胀水平。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation ↔ remains an unreasonable measure；How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? ↔ remains an unreasonable measure）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The stockbroker in Paragraph 2 is used to stand for____
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是例证目的题，正确答案 B）rail travelers. 定位句在第 2 段：（这种论调说）凭什么让一个来自林肯郡、自己开车的退休老人，去补贴一个来自萨里郡的股票经纪人的日常通勤？正确项与原文构成同义替换（the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey ↔ rail travelers）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: It is indicated in Paragraph 3 that train operators____
options: A) are offering compensation to commuters.
B) are trying to repair relations with the unions.
C) have failed to provide an adequate service.
D) have suffered huge losses owing to the strikes.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 C）have failed to provide an adequate service. 定位句在第 3 段：运营商大肆宣扬他们对铁路网做的改进，这固然不错，但乘客花了如此高的费用出行，理应能期待一个最基本的服务水准。正确项与原文构成同义替换（passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel ↔ have failed to provide an adequate service；the worst rail strikes in years ↔ have failed to provide an adequate service）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: If unable to calm down passengers, the railways may have to face____
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 D）a change of ownership. 定位句在第 4 段：国有化的威胁眼下也许已被击退，但若不尽快回应乘客那合情合理的愤怒，它将卷土重来。正确项与原文构成同义替换（The threat of nationalisation ... will return with a vengeance ↔ a change of ownership）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、B 项属过度推断、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: A) Who Are to Blame for the Strikes?
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是主旨题，正确答案 D）Ever-rising Fares Aren't Sustainable 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? ↔ Ever-rising Fares Aren't Sustainable；passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely ↔ Ever-rising Fares Aren't Sustainable；The threat of nationalisation ... will return with a vengeance ↔ Ever-rising Fares Aren't Sustainable）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、B 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: How can the train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares? It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise. This year's rise, an average of 2.7 per cent, may be a fraction lower than last year's, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.
paragraphs.zh: 铁路运营商究竟如何能为又一次提高铁路客运票价辩护？这已成为一个令人沮丧的年度惯例：每年一月，火车出行的费用都会上涨，给那些别无选择只能使用铁路网络上班或出行的人带来重大额外负担。今年的涨幅平均为2.7%，可能比去年略低一点，但仍远高于官方消费者价格指数通胀衡量标准。

paragraphs.en: Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer. Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey? Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.
paragraphs.zh: 历届政府允许这种涨价，理由是投资和运营铁路网络的成本应由使用者承担,而非普通纳税人。论点是，为什么来自林肯郡的开车退休人员要补贴来自萨里郡的股票经纪人的日常通勤？同样，人们也认为，与那些必须忍受中部和北部地区相对落后基础设施的人相比，东南部通勤者的困境受到了过多关注，而他们中许多人将面临最大的涨幅。

paragraphs.en: However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years. It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel. The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions. However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在过去12个月里，这些通勤者也经历了多年来最严重的一些铁路罢工。铁路运营商大肆宣扬他们正在对铁路网络进行的改进固然不错，但乘客应该能够期待获得与他们现在为出行支付的大笔费用相匹配的基本服务水平。最近一波罢工的责任在于工会。然而，有充分理由认为那些受劳资纠纷影响最严重的人应该为他们遭受的干扰获得赔偿。

paragraphs.en: The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate. This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain's railways. Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, punctuated by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently. The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.
paragraphs.zh: 政府已承诺修改法律以引入最低服务要求，使得即使发生罢工，服务也能继续运营。这应成为解决英国铁路长期问题的一揽子措施的一部分。是的，需要更多投资，但如果乘客还必须忍受拥挤、不可靠的服务，以及在时刻表变更或计划维护管理不善时定期出现的混乱，他们将不愿意无限期地支付更多费用。国有化的威胁目前可能已被化解，但如果不立即解决乘客的正当愤怒，它将会卷土重来。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Last year marked the third year in a row that Indonesia's bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace. One reason for the turnaround may be the country's antipoverty program. In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care. Called conditional cash transfers or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty. They're already used in dozens of countries worldwide. In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children. But CCT programs don't generally consider effects on the environment. In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro, an economist at Johns Hopkins University. That's because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty. However, those correlations don't prove cause and effect. The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view. There, as people got more money, some of them may have more cleared land for cattle to raise for meat, Ferraro says. Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though. Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation. Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates. Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012—including during Indonesia's phase-in of the antipoverty program—in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces. "We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation," Ferraro says. That's likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says. Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests. Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody's guess. Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access. And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what's good for people may also be good for the environment. Even if this program didn't reduce poverty, Ferraro says, "the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs."

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, CCT programs aim to____
options: B) help poor families get better off.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）help poor families get better off. 定位句在第 2 段：这些被称为有条件现金转移支付（CCT）的社会援助项目，旨在减少不平等、打破贫困循环。正确项与原文构成同义替换（break the cycle of poverty ↔ help poor families get better off；reduce inequality ↔ help poor families）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: The study based on an area in Mexico is cited to show that____
options: A) cattle raising has been a major means of livelihood for the poor.
B) CCT programs have helped preserve traditional lifestyles.
C) antipoverty efforts require the participation of local farmers.
D) economic growth tends to cause environmental degradation.
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是例证目的题，正确答案 D）economic growth tends to cause environmental degradation. 定位句在第 4 段：此前唯一一项分析因果关系的研究——基于墨西哥某地区已实施的 CCT 项目——支持了传统观点。正确项与原文构成同义替换（economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation ↔ economic growth tends to cause environmental degradation；supported the traditional view ↔ economic growth tends to cause environmental degradation）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、B 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: In his study about Indonesia, Ferraro intends to find out____
options: A) its acceptance level of CCTs.
B) its annual rate of poverty alleviation.
C) the relation of CCTs to its forest loss.
D) the role of its forests in climate change.
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 C）the relation of CCTs to its forest loss. 定位句在第 5 段：Ferraro 想看看印尼的扶贫项目是否在影响森林砍伐。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program ↔ CCTs；was affecting deforestation ↔ the relation of CCTs to its forest loss）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Ferraro, the CCT program in Indonesia is most valuable in that____
options: A) it will benefit other Asian countries.
B) it will reduce regional inequality.
C) it can protect the environment.
D) it can benefit grain production.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）it can protect the environment. 定位句在第 8 段：Ferraro 说，即便这个项目没能减贫，仅就避免森林砍伐带来的二氧化碳减排价值而言，就已经超过了项目本身的成本。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs ↔ it can protect the environment；what's good for people may also be good for the environment ↔ it can protect the environment）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What is the text centered on?
options: A) The effects of a program.
B) The debates over a program.
C) The process of a study.
D) The transferability of a study.
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）The effects of a program. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation ↔ The effects of a program；Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation ↔ The effects of a program；the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs ↔ The effects of a program）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Last year marked the third year in a row that Indonesia's bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace. One reason for the turnaround may be the country's antipoverty program.
paragraphs.zh: 去年标志着印度尼西亚严峻的森林砍伐率连续第三年放缓。出现这种转变的一个原因可能是该国的扶贫计划。

paragraphs.en: In 2007, Indonesia started phasing in a program that gives money to its poorest residents under certain conditions, such as requiring people to keep kids in school or get regular medical care. Called conditional cash transfers or CCTs, these social assistance programs are designed to reduce inequality and break the cycle of poverty. They're already used in dozens of countries worldwide. In Indonesia, the program has provided enough food and medicine to substantially reduce severe growth problems among children.
paragraphs.zh: 2007年,印度尼西亚开始逐步实施一项计划,在某些条件下向最贫困的居民提供资金,例如要求人们让孩子留在学校或定期接受医疗保健。这些社会援助计划被称为有条件现金转移支付或CCT,旨在减少不平等并打破贫困循环。它们已经在全球数十个国家使用。在印度尼西亚,该计划提供了足够的食物和药品,大幅减少了儿童的严重发育问题。

paragraphs.en: But CCT programs don't generally consider effects on the environment. In fact, poverty alleviation and environmental protection are often viewed as conflicting goals, says Paul Ferraro, an economist at Johns Hopkins University.
paragraphs.zh: 但CCT计划通常不考虑对环境的影响。Johns Hopkins大学经济学家Paul Ferraro说,事实上,扶贫和环境保护常常被视为相互冲突的目标。

paragraphs.en: That's because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes correlated with greater poverty. However, those correlations don't prove cause and effect. The only previous study analyzing causality, based on an area in Mexico that had instituted CCTs, supported the traditional view. There, as people got more money, some of them may have more cleared land for cattle to raise for meat, Ferraro says.
paragraphs.zh: 这是因为经济增长可能与环境退化相关,而保护环境有时与更严重的贫困相关。然而,这些相关性并不能证明因果关系。唯一一项分析因果关系的先前研究,基于墨西哥一个实施了CCT的地区,支持了传统观点。Ferraro说,在那里,随着人们获得更多的钱,其中一些人可能清理了更多土地来饲养肉牛。

paragraphs.en: Such programs do not have to negatively affect the environment, though. Ferraro wanted to see if Indonesia's poverty-alleviation program was affecting deforestation. Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.
paragraphs.zh: 不过,此类计划不一定要对环境产生负面影响。Ferraro想看看印度尼西亚的扶贫计划是否正在影响森林砍伐。印度尼西亚拥有世界上第三大热带森林面积和最高的森林砍伐率之一。

paragraphs.en: Ferraro analyzed satellite data showing annual forest loss from 2008 to 2012—including during Indonesia's phase-in of the antipoverty program—in 7,468 forested villages across 15 provinces. "We see that the program is associated with a 30 percent reduction in deforestation," Ferraro says.
paragraphs.zh: Ferraro分析了卫星数据,显示了2008年至2012年期间的年度森林损失——包括印度尼西亚扶贫计划逐步实施期间——涵盖15个省的7468个森林村庄。Ferraro说:"我们看到该计划与森林砍伐减少30%相关。"

paragraphs.en: That's likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says. Typically, if rains are delayed, people may clear land to plant more rice to supplement their harvests.
paragraphs.zh: Ferraro说,这可能是因为农村贫困人口正在将这笔钱用作应对恶劣天气的临时保险政策。通常情况下,如果降雨推迟,人们可能会清理土地种植更多水稻来补充收成。

paragraphs.en: Whether this research translates elsewhere is anybody's guess. Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice and market access. And regardless of transferability, the study shows that what's good for people may also be good for the environment. Even if this program didn't reduce poverty, Ferraro says, "the value of the avoided deforestation just for carbon dioxide emissions alone is more than the program costs."
paragraphs.zh: 这项研究是否适用于其他地方,谁也说不准。Ferraro认为,由于种植水稻的重要性和市场准入等共性,研究结果可能适用于亚洲其他地区。无论可迁移性如何,该研究表明,对人有益的事情也可能对环境有益。Ferraro说,即使该计划没有减少贫困,"仅就二氧化碳排放而言,避免森林砍伐的价值就超过了该计划的成本。"

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter. Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend? During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm. But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile. One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed). A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, the author's posts on Twitter ____
options: A) changed people's impression of the Victorians.
B) highlighted social media's role in Victorian studies.
C) re-evaluated the Victorian's notion of public image.
D) illustrated the development of Victorian photography.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 A）changed people's impression of the Victorians. 定位句在第 1 段：人们惊讶地看到证据，原来维多利亚人也会享受、会笑、确实笑过。他们注意到，维多利亚人突然变得更像 "人" 了——相隔我们一百多年的时空，在共同的笑声体验中消融。正确项与原文构成同义替换（People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun ↔ changed people's impression of the Victorians；the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human ↔ changed people's impression of the Victorians）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author say about the Victorian portraits he has collected?
options: A) They are in popular use among historians.
B) They are rare among photographs of that age.
D) They show effects of different exposure times.
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 B）They are rare among photographs of that age. 定位句在第 2 段：当然，我必须承认，我的 "微笑的维多利亚人" 收藏只占 1840 至 1900 年间产出的庞大肖像目录的极小比例，其中绝大多数都呈现拍摄者僵硬呆板地站在彩绘背景前、或茫然地凝视远处的中景。正确项与原文构成同义替换（my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue ↔ They are rare among photographs of that age）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属答非所问、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s?
options: B) Their tension before the camera.
C) Their distrust of new inventions.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 D）Their unhealthy dental condition. 定位句在第 5 段：一种解释可能是：露齿傻笑会失体面。当时流行的一句格言说 "造物给我们嘴唇是为遮住牙齿"，暗指在正规牙科诞生之前，人们的口腔卫生状况骇人。正确项与原文构成同义替换（mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene ↔ Their unhealthy dental condition；before the birth of proper dentistry ↔ Their unhealthy dental condition）。其余三项中，A 项属过度推断、B 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）a deep-root belief. 定位句在第 6 段：露齿笑（尤其有牙缝或黑牙时）很掉档次：醉汉、流浪汉、音乐厅艺人也许会咧嘴大笑，笑得像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下露牙龈的柴郡猫一样宽，但这对于教养良好之人并非得体之相。甚至连爱开怀大笑的马克·吐温也说，谈到肖像照，"再没有什么比一个永远定格的傻里傻气的笑容更糟的了"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that ... "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever" ↔ a deep-root belief；it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons ↔ a deep-root belief）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following questions does the text answer?
options: A) Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?
B) Why did the Victorians start to view photographs?
C) What made photography develop in the Victorian period?
D) How did smiling in photographs become a post-Victorian norm?
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs? 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（How do we explain this trend? ↔ Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?；the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly ↔ Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?；One explanation might be the loss of dignity ↔ Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?). I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir. People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh. They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名总在寻找那些让我们重新评价过去的文字或图像的历史学家，我开始专注于寻找维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片(还有什么比这更能打破19世纪古板拘谨的形象呢?)。我找到了不少这样的照片，而且自从我开始在Twitter上发布它们以来，它们引起了相当大的轰动。人们惊讶地看到证据表明维多利亚时代的人也有乐趣，能够而且确实会笑。他们注意到，随着我们对笑声的共同体验消除了横亘在我们之间的百年左右的时光，维多利亚时代的人突然显得更加人性化了。

paragraphs.en: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance. How do we explain this trend?
paragraphs.zh: 当然，我需要承认，我收藏的"微笑的维多利亚时代人"照片只占1840年至1900年间创作的大量摄影肖像目录中的极小一部分，其中大多数照片显示的是被拍摄者在彩绘背景前痛苦而僵硬地摆姿势，或茫然地凝视着中距离处。我们如何解释这一趋势？

paragraphs.en: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs. The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
paragraphs.zh: 在19世纪40年代和50年代摄影的早期，曝光时间出了名地长：银版摄影法(在镀银铜板上成像)可能需要几分钟才能完成，导致图像模糊，因为被拍摄者移动了位置或调整了肢体。想到在相机执行其神奇职责时保持固定的笑容实在难以想象，因此不置可否的茫然凝视成为常态。

paragraphs.en: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous. Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
paragraphs.zh: 但到了19世纪80年代，曝光时间已经快得多了，Box Brownie和其他便携式相机的引入意味着，尽管按今天的数字标准来说仍然缓慢，但曝光几乎是瞬时的。到19世纪90年代，捕捉自然的微笑相对容易了，因此我们必须到别处寻找维多利亚时代的人为何仍然犹豫微笑的解释。

paragraphs.en: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. "Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
paragraphs.zh: 一个解释可能是通过俗气的露齿笑所展现出的尊严丧失。"大自然给了我们嘴唇来遮住牙齿，"一句流行的维多利亚时代格言如是说，暗指在正规牙科诞生之前，口腔的卫生状况往往令人震惊。在维多利亚时代社会，一口健康、干净、整齐的"珍珠白"牙齿是罕见的景象，是超级富豪的专属(即便如此，牙齿卫生也不能得到保证)。

paragraphs.en: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".
paragraphs.zh: 露齿的笑容(尤其是当牙齿有缺口或发黑时)缺乏品味：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅表演者可能会像Lewis Carroll笔下露出牙龈的Cheshire Cat那样做鬼脸和咧嘴大笑，但这对于教养良好的人来说不是得体的样子。即使是Mark Twain这样一个喜欢开怀大笑的人也说，在摄影肖像方面，"没有什么比永远定格的愚蠢、傻气的微笑更糟糕的了"。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet. Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either. The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own. On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move. But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism." In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication. The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.

questions.stem: There has long been concern that broadband providers would____
options: A) bring web-based firms under control.
B) slow down the traffic on their network.
C) show partiality in treating clients.
D) intensify competition with their rivals.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 C）show partiality in treating clients. 定位句在第 1 段：从宽带发展早期起，消费者权益倡导者和互联网公司就担心：销售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司，有权力也有动机偏袒与自己关联的网站，而冷落对手的网站。正确项与原文构成同义替换（favor affiliated websites over their rivals' ↔ show partiality in treating clients）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属无中生有、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: Faced with the demand for net neutrality rules, the FCC____
options: A) sticks to an out-of-date order.
C) has issued a special resolution.
D) has allowed the states to intervene.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 B）takes an anti-regulatory stance. 定位句在第 2 段：由共和党主笔的这份命令不仅废除了 FCC 在 2015 年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则，还否定了 FCC 自身要求宽带商做任何事的监管权。该命令还宣布州和地方政府也不能监管宽带商。正确项与原文构成同义替换（eliminated the strict net neutrality rules ↔ takes an anti-regulatory stance；rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything ↔ takes an anti-regulatory stance）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be learned about AT&T from Paragraph 3?
options: A) It protects against unfair competition.
B) It engages in anti-competitive practices.
C) It is under the FCC's investigation.
D) It is in pursuit of quality service.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）It engages in anti-competitive practices. 定位句在第 3 段：FCC 辩称，会有别的机构防止反竞争行为，比如像 AT&T 这种宽带集团偏袒自家流媒体服务、损害 Netflix 和 Apple TV 的利益。正确项与原文构成同义替换（anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV ↔ engages in anti-competitive practices）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Judge Patricia Millett argues that the appeals court's decision____
options: C) is at odds with its earlier rulings.
D) is out of touch with reality.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 D）is out of touch with reality. 定位句在第 4 段：但 Millett 法官在协同意见中说得对："这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实"，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，"以免把互联网监管困在技术时代错置之中"。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service ↔ is out of touch with reality）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What does the author argue in the last paragraph?
options: A) Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality.
B) The FCC should be put under strict supervision.
C) Rules need to be set to diversify online services.
D) Broadband providers' rights should be protected.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（cry out for Congress to act ↔ Congress needs to take action to ensure net neutrality；create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online ↔ to ensure net neutrality）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'. That's why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet.
paragraphs.zh: 从宽带发展早期开始,消费者权益倡导者和网络公司就担心,销售宽带连接的有线电视和电话公司有能力也有动机偏袒关联网站而非竞争对手。这就是为什么人们强烈要求制定规则,防止宽带提供商在网上挑选赢家和输家,保护一直是互联网命脉的自由和创新。

paragraphs.en: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission's authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn't regulate broadband providers either.
paragraphs.zh: 然而,这一要求几乎不可能实现——部分原因是来自宽带提供商、反监管保守派和法院的阻力。联邦上诉法院周二再次介入,但它非但没有提供急需的解决方案,反而延长了这场斗争。美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院审理的是联邦通信委员会在2017年以党派立场投票通过的关于网络中立的最新立场。这项由共和党撰写的命令不仅废除了联邦通信委员会在2015年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立规则,还否认了该委员会要求宽带提供商做任何事情的权力。该命令还宣布州和地方政府也不能监管宽带提供商。

paragraphs.en: The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV. Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals' streaming services but not their own.
paragraphs.zh: 该委员会辩称,其他机构将防范反竞争行为,比如像AT&T这样的宽带提供商集团以牺牲Netflix和Apple TV为代价偏袒自己的视频流媒体服务。然而,联邦通信委员会也终止了对那些对竞争对手的流媒体服务设置数据上限而对自己的服务不设上限的宽带提供商的调查。

paragraphs.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move. But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that "the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service," and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to "avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism."
paragraphs.zh: 周二,上诉法院一致维持了2017年放松对宽带提供商监管的命令,援引了最高法院2005年支持类似放松监管举措的裁决。但法官Patricia Millett在协同意见中正确地指出,'这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实',并表示国会或最高法院可以介入以'避免将互联网监管困在技术过时主义中'。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC's attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission's power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC's abdication.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时,法院推翻了联邦通信委员会试图阻止所有州网络中立规则的做法,同时保留了该委员会优先否决破坏其命令的个别州法律的权力。这意味着会有更多像司法部与加利福尼亚州之间正在进行的这类战斗,该州在联邦通信委员会放弃职责后颁布了一项严格的网络中立法。

paragraphs.en: The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
paragraphs.zh: 联邦通信委员会无休止的法律战和反复无常迫切需要国会采取行动。国会需要一劳永逸地赋予该委员会明确权力,禁止宽带提供商干预其网络上的流量,并制定明确规则保护网络的开放性和创新。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline. The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high. With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel. Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it. But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.

questions.stem: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests____.
options: A) an increase in full-time employment
B) an urgent demand for new job skills
C) a steady growth of job opportunities
D) a controversy about the "core skills"
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 B）an urgent demand for new job skills 定位句在第 1 段：世界经济论坛的研究发现，到 2022 年，岗位中约 42% 的"核心技能"将发生变化。正确项与原文构成同义替换（42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022 ↔ an urgent demand for new job skills；That is a very short timeline. ↔ urgent）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: AT&T is cited to show____.
options: A) an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy
B) an immediate need for government support
C) the importance of staff appraisal standards
D) the characteristics of reskilling programs
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy 定位句在第 2 段：AT&T 常被誉为典范——这家公司选择大规模再培训计划，而不是采取"先解雇再招新"的策略。正确项与原文构成同义替换（decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy ↔ an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada____.
options: A) have driven up labour costs
B) have proved to be inconsistent
C) have met with fierce opposition
D) have appeared to be insufficient
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 D）have appeared to be insufficient 定位句在第 2 段：加拿大及其他地方的努力充其量也只能说是"懒散"，由此造成的局面是：我们常听到雇主求人难，哪怕在失业率本就高的时段和地区也是如此。正确项与原文构成同义替换（languid at best ↔ have appeared to be insufficient；we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high ↔ insufficient）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was____.
options: A) a call for policy adjustment
B) a change in hiring practices
C) a lack of medical workers
D) a sign of economic recovery
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 C）a lack of medical workers 定位句在第 3 段：举一个明显的例子：在医疗领域，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医护人员仍然明显短缺。正确项与原文构成同义替换（clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel ↔ a lack of medical workers）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Scandinavian Airlines decided to____.
options: A) create job vacancies for the unemployed
B) prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs
C) retrain their cabin staff for better services
D) finance their staff's college education
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是细节题，正确答案 B）prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs 定位句在第 4 段：在被迫让 90% 的乘务员停工时，北欧航空决定启动一个短期再培训项目，把被解雇的员工再培训以支援医院员工。正确项与原文构成同义替换（reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff ↔ prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline.
paragraphs.zh: "再培训"听起来像是一个流行词，但如果我们计划拥有一个不让大量潜在劳动者掉队的未来，它实际上是一项必需。我们知道我们正在进入一个需求岗位将快速变化的时期，现有岗位的要求也会随之变化。世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，平均42%的岗位角色"核心技能"将发生变化。这是一个非常短的时间线。

paragraphs.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
paragraphs.zh: 谁应该为再培训买单是一个棘手的问题。对于单个公司而言，诱惑总是解雇技能不再有需求的员工，并用那些拥有所需技能的人取而代之。但情况并非总是如此。AT&T常被视为决定实施大规模再培训计划而非采取解雇再招聘策略的公司的黄金标准。包括亚马逊和迪士尼在内的其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。然而,当技能不匹配出现在更广泛的经济领域时,焦点通常转向政府来处理。加拿大和其他地方的努力可以说充其量是疲软的,并给我们带来了这样一种局面:我们经常听到雇主恳求招工,即使是在失业率很高的时期和地区。

paragraphs.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
paragraphs.zh: 随着疫情的到来,失业率确实非常高。2月份,加拿大和美国的失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%,处于几代人以来的最低水平,各地都出现了劳动力短缺。到5月份,这些比率已飙升至13.3%和13.7%,尽管许多劳动力短缺已经消失,但并非所有短缺都消失了。以医疗领域为例,疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医务人员仍然明显短缺。

paragraphs.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it. But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
paragraphs.zh: 当然,你不可能在几周内把一个失业的服务员培训成医生,无论由谁买单。但即使你无法弥合那种差距,也许你可以弥合其他差距,而这样做将使所有相关方受益。瑞典的情况似乎就是如此:当被迫让90%的机舱乘务员休假时,斯堪的纳维亚航空公司决定启动一个短期再培训项目,对下岗员工进行再培训以支援医院工作人员。这项努力是集体性的,涉及其他公司以及一所瑞典大学。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines. In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit. Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food. The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s. A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health. Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision? According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs. There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave. To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production. But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help. There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields. Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production. Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs. That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley. Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world. Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products. Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many "acqui-hires" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent. To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path. "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors. Microsoft declined to comment. Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on. But are they good for the American economy? I don't know." The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question. This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade. Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach. Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point. Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year. However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a "buy and kill" tactic to simply close them down.

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive. In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness. Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings. Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory. Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing. Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating. Accuracy dropped dramatically. Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression. She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners. Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection. "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing. But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine. Much of our social life is like that." Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences. College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale. And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process. Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances. In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech). Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart"). Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest. Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.

questions.stem: Nalini Ambady's study deals with____.
options: A) the power of people's memory
B) the reliability of first impressions
D) people's ability to influence others
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 B）the reliability of first impressions 定位句在第 1 段：我们仅凭第一印象——从瞥一眼照片到五分钟互动这种"薄切"经验——就能相当准地评判他人，而刻意琢磨不仅多余还会添乱。在一项研究她称之为"薄切"这一能力的实验里，已故心理学家 Nalini Ambady 让被试观看10秒无声教师视频，并给老师的整体教学效果打分。正确项与原文构成同义替换（We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions ↔ the reliability of first impressions；first impressions ↔ first impressions）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: In Ambady's study, rating accuracy dropped when participants____.
options: B) gave the rating in limited time
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 A）focused on specific details 定位句在第 2 段：关键的是，另一组被要求在打分前花一分钟写下自己评判的理由。准确率显著下降。Ambady 推测，这种刻意琢磨让被试盯住了一些醒目却具有误导性的线索，比如某些手势或言语，而没能让微妙信号之间复杂的交互形成一个整体印象。正确项与原文构成同义替换（focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances ↔ focused on specific details；focused them on ↔ focused on）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Judith Hall mentions driving to show that____.
options: C) social skills must be cultivated
D) deception is difficult to detect
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）reflection can be distracting 定位句在第 3 段：其他研究表明，靠直觉而不是反思，我们更善于从薄切信息中识破欺骗。"这就像你在开手动挡，"东北大学心理学家 Judith Hall 说，"如果你开始想得太多，反而会忘了自己在干什么。但如果你切到自动驾驶模式，反而开得很顺。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing ↔ reflection can be distracting；we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection ↔ reflection can be distracting）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: When you are making complex decisions, it is advisable to____.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 D）follow your feelings 定位句在第 4 段：而且，当被要求专注于感受而不是细节时，人们做出的购车决定既客观上更好、也主观上更让自己满意——但前提是这个决策是复杂的，也就是他们要处理大量信息时。正确项与原文构成同义替换（focus on their feelings ↔ follow your feelings；only if the decision was complex ↔ follow your feelings）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can we learn from the last paragraph?
options: A) Generating new products takes time.
B) Intuition may affect reflective tasks.
D) Objective thinking may boost intuitiveness.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是推断题，正确答案 B）Intuition may affect reflective tasks. 定位句在第 5 段：在一项研究中，被试完成了八项任务的组合，其中四项考反思（找规则、理解词汇），另四项考直觉和创造力（创造新产品或新比喻）。然后他们打分评估自己使用直觉的程度（"凭感觉""直觉""用心"）。使用直觉如预期那样损害了前四项任务的表现，却在后四项上帮了他们。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks ↔ Intuition may affect reflective tasks.；four that tapped reflective thinking ↔ reflective tasks；gut ↔ Intuition）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive. In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness. Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings. Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory. Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
paragraphs.zh: 我们相当擅长基于第一印象来判断他人，这种薄片体验范围从瞥见一张照片到五分钟的互动，而深思熟虑不仅可能是多余的，还可能是干扰性的。在一项关于她称之为"薄片切割"能力的研究中,已故心理学家Nalini Ambady要求参与者观看教授们的10秒无声视频片段,并对教师的整体有效性进行评分。他们的评分与学生的学期末评分高度相关。另一组参与者在观看视频片段时必须从1000倒数,每次减9,占用他们有意识的工作记忆。他们的评分同样准确,证明了社会处理过程的直觉性质。

paragraphs.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating. Accuracy dropped dramatically. Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression. She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
paragraphs.zh: 关键的是,另一组被要求在给出评分之前花一分钟写下他们判断的理由。准确性急剧下降。Ambady怀疑深思熟虑使他们专注于生动但具有误导性的线索,例如某些手势或话语,而不是让微妙信号的复杂相互作用形成整体印象。当参与者观看15秒的两人配对视频片段并判断他们是陌生人、朋友还是约会对象时,她发现了类似的干扰。

paragraphs.en: Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection. "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing. But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine. Much of our social life is like that."
paragraphs.zh: 其他研究表明,当我们依靠直觉而非反思时,我们更善于从薄片中检测欺骗。东北大学心理学家Judith Hall说:"这就像你在开手动挡车,如果你开始想得太多,你就记不住自己在做什么。但如果你进入自动驾驶模式,你就没问题。我们的社会生活很大程度上就是这样。"

paragraphs.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences. College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale. And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
paragraphs.zh: 思考过多也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。当大学生不被要求分析他们的理由时,他们对草莓酱和大学课程的评分与专家意见更一致。当人们被要求关注自己的感受而非细节时,他们做出的购车决策既在客观上更好,也在个人层面上更令人满意,但只有在决策复杂时才如此——当他们有大量信息需要处理时。

paragraphs.en: Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances. In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech). Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart"). Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest. Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
paragraphs.zh: 直觉的特殊力量只在特定情况下才会释放。在一项研究中,参与者完成了八项任务,其中四项利用反思性思维(辨别规则、理解词汇),四项利用直觉和创造力(生成新产品或修辞手法)。然后他们评估自己使用直觉的程度("直觉感受"、"预感"、"我的内心")。如预期的那样,使用直觉损害了他们在前四项任务上的表现,但帮助了他们完成其余任务。有时心灵比头脑更聪明。
