blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 B）profit。「生意做得不错却要更上一层」的小企业语境。其余三项：A）purchase 对象错——CEO 「做」的不是采购、C）connection 话题偏离——下文没接「人脉」、D）bet 感情色彩冲突，均可排除。
第 2 空正确答案 C）prioritize。全段在号召把增长放在第一位。其余三项：A）define 动作错位——不是「定义」是「去做」、B）predict 方向错——不是预测，是推动、D）appreciate 色彩与对象都不对，均可排除。
第 3 空正确答案 A）exclusively。团队的全部精力都给增长。其余三项：B）temporarily 时间限定与「专门组队」相悖、C）potentially 语气太虚——不是「可能」、D）initially 暗含「后来不再」与下文不符，均可排除。
第 4 空正确答案 D）example。下面是 BitTorrent 的故事而非实验或辩论。其余三项：A）experiment 下文不是实验设计、B）proposal 下文不是提议、C）debate 下文没有正反观点，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 D）traditional。「成立成长团队前」的常规架构。其余三项：A）identical 事实错——三个部门并不相同、B）marginal 色彩冲突——这些是核心部门、C）provisional 时态错——不是临时设置，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 D）problem。增长停滞 + 顾客不付费=问题。其余三项：A）rumor 事实非「未经证实」、B）secret 并非隐秘信息、C）myth 并非「广为流传的错误观念」，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 A）despite。「付费版有改进」却「升级的人少」是让步。其余三项：B）unlike 对比对象错位、C）through 方式与结果矛盾、D）besides 并列增量与反差结果不搭，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 B）however。上段是困境、本段是转机。其余三项：A）moreover 并非追加同向信息、C）therefore 并非因果直接推出、D）again 无重复语境，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 B）created。P2 公司还没有成长团队。其余三项：A）inspected 无可检查的既有团队、C）expanded 扩张需有原物、D）reformed 改革也要有原物，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 C）fresh。「创新经理」+「跨部门视角」=新视角。其余三项：A）cultural 话题外延偏离、B）objective 侧重「客观」与上下文不符、D）personal 色彩与团队属性矛盾，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 C）lack。上一段「很少人升级」 = 升级少。其余三项：A）end 事实错——升级并未终结、B）burden 色彩错——升级不是负担、D）decrease 走向错——文中没说在下降，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 D）insight。P3 末「发现真因」=洞察。其余三项：A）policy 上文未给出政策、B）suggestion 上文非「建议」、C）purpose 目的与上文事实错位，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 C）promoting。「提升认知」需要「推介/推广」型动作。其余三项：A）contributing 搭配错——contribute to 后才接名词、B）allocating 动作对象错、D）transferring 对象错——不是「转让」，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 A）As a result。上文「推广」=因，「升级暴涨」=果。其余三项：B）At any rate 语气与因果链不符、C）By the way 话题切换错——这里不是岔话、D）In a sense 限定语气不对，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 A）unite。「跨学科团队 + 让大家走在轨道上」=凝聚。其余三项：B）finance 话题错——leader 角色不是出钱、C）follow 主客倒置、D）choose 范围错——不是「挑选」，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 B）identify。「设定目标前」要先「确定目标区域」。其余三项：A）share 动作错位——不是「分享」目标区、C）divide 动作错——不是切分、D）broaden 方向错——不是扩大，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 D）accomplishment。目标是用来「完成」的。其余三项：A）announcement 动作错——不是宣布、B）assessment 对象错——评估不是目标的终点、C）adjustment 前提错——目标不是用来调整的，均可排除。
第 18 空正确答案 B）responsible。句中 keeping ... 是 leader 的具体职责。其余三项：A）famous 语义错位、C）available 状态错、D）respectable 属性错——不是评价，均可排除。
第 19 空正确答案 C）While。「吸引力 + 分心」一正一反 = 让步。其余三项：A）Before 时间关系不对、B）Once 条件结果错、D）Unless 否定条件错，均可排除。
第 20 空正确答案 A）serve。「服务于目标」才不该被搁置。其余三项：B）limit 方向错、C）summarize 对象错、D）alter 方向错，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice [1] , you need to find a way to take it to the next level. What you need to do is [2] growth by establishing a growth team. A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus [3] on finding ways to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是当今许多创业者面临的常见情景：你是一家小企业的首席执行官，虽然你盈利不错,但你需要找到一种方法将其提升到更高水平。你需要做的是通过建立增长团队来优先考虑增长。增长团队由来自公司内不同部门的成员组成，它利用协作的力量专注于寻找增长的方法。

paragraphs.en: Let's look at a real-world [4] . Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees working in the [5] departments of engineering, marketing and product development. This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued. The [6] was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product. And [7] improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.
paragraphs.zh: 让我们看一个真实案例。在组建增长团队之前，软件公司BitTorrent有50名员工在传统的工程、营销和产品开发部门工作。这为他们带来了良好的成果，直到2012年，他们的增长陷入停滞。问题在于太多客户使用的是基础免费版本的产品。尽管对高级付费版本进行了改进，但很少有人升级。

paragraphs.en: Things changed, [8] , when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard, [9] a growth team and sparked the kind of [10] perspective they needed. By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the [11] of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，当一位创新的项目营销经理加入、创建了增长团队并激发了他们所需的新视角时，情况发生了变化。通过从营销角度审视工程问题，很明显升级不足并非由于质量问题。大多数客户只是不了解高级版本及其提供的功能。

paragraphs.en: Armed with this [12] , the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently [13] the premium version to users of the free version. [14] , upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.
paragraphs.zh: 有了这一洞察，营销和工程团队联手通过向免费版本用户显著推广高级版本来提高知晓度。结果，升级量激增，收入增长了92%。

paragraphs.en: But in order for your growth team to succeed, it needs to have a strong leader. It needs someone who can [15] the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement. This leader will [16] the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the [17] of these goals.
paragraphs.zh: 但是为了让你的增长团队取得成功，它需要有一位强有力的领导者。它需要一个能够团结跨学科团队并使他们保持改进方向的人。这位领导者将确定目标领域、设定明确目标并为实现这些目标建立时间框架。

paragraphs.en: The growth leader is also [18] for keeping the team focused on moving forward and steering them clear of distractions. [19] attractive, new ideas can be distracting; the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't [20] the current goal and need to be put on the back burner.
paragraphs.zh: 增长领导者还负责让团队专注于前进并引导他们避开干扰。虽然具有吸引力，但新想法可能会分散注意力；团队领导者必须识别何时这些想法不服务于当前目标并需要暂时搁置。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things. The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel. Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia. Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material. As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes. The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was. The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper. According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails. Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails. It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense. I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world. The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper. Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.

questions.stem: The Romans buried the nails probably for the sake of______.
options: A) saving them for future use
C) letting them grow in value
D) hiding them from the locals
questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 D）hiding them from the locals 定位句在第 2 段：最可能的解释是，撤退仓促，他们不想让当地的凯尔多尼亚人拿到这 10 吨可作武器原料的铁。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron ↔ hiding them from the locals）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属无中生有、C 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: The example of early 17th-century Virginians is used to______.
options: A) highlight the thriftiness of early American colonists
B) illustrate the high status of blacksmiths in that period
C) contrast the attitudes of different civilisations towards nails
D) show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time
questions.explanation: 第 22 题是例证目的题，正确答案 D）show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time 定位句在第 3 段：「为了回收钉子竟然可能把整栋房子烧掉」这一想法，凸显出这项看似简单的技术当时是何等稀缺、昂贵、珍贵。正确项与原文构成同义替换（underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was ↔ show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: What played the major role in lowering the price of nails after the late 1700s?
options: B) Wider use of new energies.
D) Reduced cost of raw materials.
questions.explanation: 第 23 题是细节题，正确答案 A）Increased productivity. 定位句在第 4 段：根据 Sichel 的研究，虽然钉子价格下降部分得益于铁和能源变便宜，但主要功劳归于钉子制造商，他们找到了把钢转为钉子的更高效方法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails ↔ Increased productivity）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 5 that nails______.
options: A) have undergone many technological improvements
B) have remained basically the same since Roman times
C) are less studied than other everyday products
D) are one of the world's most significant inventions
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 B）have remained basically the same since Roman times 定位句在第 5 段：钉子本身这些年也有变化，但 Sichel 研究它们恰因为它们变化不大。罗马的灯具和马车与 LED 灯带和跑车截然不同，但罗马的钉子至今仍明显就是钉子。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Roman nails are still clearly nails ↔ have remained basically the same since Roman times；they haven't changed much ↔ have remained basically the same since Roman times）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属无中生有、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarises the last two paragraphs?
options: A) Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change.
B) Technological innovation is integral to economic success.
C) Technology defines people's understanding of the world.
D) Sophisticated technologies develop from small inventions.
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it's the cheap technologies that change the world ↔ Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change；Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system ↔ Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属答非所问、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things. The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
paragraphs.zh: 将近2000年前,当罗马人开始撤出苏格兰时,他们留下了一件奇特的宝藏:10吨钉子,将近一百万枚。这批钉子宝藏于1960年在一个四米深的坑中被发现,坑上覆盖着两米厚的砾石。

paragraphs.en: Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
paragraphs.zh: 罗马人为何要埋藏一百万枚钉子?最可能的解释是撤军过于仓促,他们不想让当地的喀里多尼亚人得到这10吨可用作武器的铁。罗马人把钉子埋得如此之深,以至于它们在近两千年后才被发现。

paragraphs.en: Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith's labour in a nail even more than the raw material. As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes. The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
paragraphs.zh: 后来的文明更加看重熟练铁匠在一枚钉子上付出的劳动,甚至超过原材料本身的价值。正如Roma Agrawal在她令人愉悦的新书《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的,17世纪早期的弗吉尼亚人如果打算搬迁,有时会烧毁自己的房屋。这是为了回收那些珍贵的钉子,它们可以在筛过灰烬后重新使用。为了回收钉子而烧毁整座房屋的做法,凸显了这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵和珍贵。

paragraphs.en: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper. According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
paragraphs.zh: 经济学家Daniel Sichel在一篇研究论文中指出,从18世纪末到20世纪中期,钉子的价格下降了90%。根据Sichel的研究,尽管钉子价格的下降部分是由更便宜的铁和更便宜的能源推动的,但大部分功劳应归于钉子制造商,他们只是找到了将钢铁变成钉子的更高效方法。

paragraphs.en: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails. It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
paragraphs.zh: 钉子本身多年来有所变化,但Sichel研究它们是因为它们变化不大。罗马灯具和罗马战车与LED灯带和跑车截然不同,但罗马钉子显然仍是钉子。试图追踪自1695年以来跑车价格的变化是荒谬的,但对钉子提出同样的问题则完全合理。

paragraphs.en: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world.
paragraphs.zh: 我对日常物品的一个特定特征着迷,对此我不作任何辩解:它们的价格。毕竟,我是一名经济学家。在撰写了两本关于发明史的书之后,我学到的一点是,尽管那些迷人而复杂的技术获得了所有的炒作,但改变世界的是廉价技术。

paragraphs.en: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper. Solar panels had a few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
paragraphs.zh: 古腾堡印刷机改变了文明,不是通过改变书写的本质,而是通过改变其成本——如果没有书写表面价格的同步暴跌,它不会取得多大成就,这要归功于一种常被忽视的技术,叫做纸张。太阳能电池板在变得廉价之前只有少数利基用途;现在它们正在改变全球能源系统。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested. The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults. Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and "baby-wearing", in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm. According to Dr. Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents. Dr. Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life. In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery. The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities. In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history. This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative", which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful. "Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote. By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care. One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour. Chaudhary said that parents now had less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing. An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three. While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents "might also enhance their own social development".

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, alloparenting refers to the practice of______.
options: A) sharing childcare among community members
B) assigning babies to specific adult caregivers
C) teaching parenting skills to older children
D) carrying infants around by their parents
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 A）sharing childcare among community members 定位句在第 1 段：这一观点基于对博茨瓦纳孔人等部落的研究——在这些部落里，每个孩子都由众多成年人共同照料。正确项与原文构成同义替换（each child is cared for by many adults ↔ sharing childcare among community members；Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones ↔ sharing childcare）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

questions.stem: The scheme in Germany is mentioned to illustrate______.
options: A) an attempt to facilitate intergenerational communication
B) an approach to integrating alloparenting into western society
C) the conventional parenting style in western culture
D) the differences between western and African ways of living
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是例证目的题，正确答案 B）an approach to integrating alloparenting into western society 定位句在第 3 段：儿童精神科医生 Annie Swanepoel 认为，有办法把这些做法融入西方生活。在德国，有一项方案把一所养老院和一所托儿所配对：老人帮忙照看孩子，这种安排类似 alloparenting。正确项与原文构成同义替换（there are ways to incorporate them into western life ↔ an approach to integrating alloparenting into western society；an arrangement akin to alloparenting ↔ alloparenting）。其余三项中，A 项属答非所问、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, the "intensive mothering narrative" ______.
options: C) results in the child-centred family
D) departs from the course of evolution
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 D）departs from the course of evolution 定位句在第 4 段：研究者在《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》上发表论文称，西方核家庭其实是一项「近期发明」，与人类演化史断裂。这种向「密集母职论调」的突变——即主张母亲应独自承担育儿——很可能是有害的。正确项与原文构成同义替换（broke with evolutionary history ↔ departs from the course of evolution；abrupt shift ↔ departs from）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the nurseries in the UK?
options: A) They tend to fall short of official requirements.
B) They have difficulty finding enough caregivers.
C) They ought to improve their carer-to-child ratio.
D) They should try to prevent parental depression.
questions.explanation: 第 29 题是推断题，正确答案 C）They ought to improve their carer-to-child ratio. 定位句在第 6 段：出生在狩猎采集社会的婴儿可能拥有十多位照护者——这与英国托儿所的规定形成鲜明对比，那里规定每名照护者要带 4 名 2–3 岁的孩子。正确项与原文构成同义替换（this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three ↔ ought to improve their carer-to-child ratio；introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing ↔ improve their carer-to-child ratio）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属过度推断、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?
options: A) Instructive teaching: a dilemma for anxious parents
B) For a happier family, learn from the hunter-gatherers
C) Mixed-age playgroup, a better choice for lonely children
D) Tracing the history of parenting: from Africa to Europe
questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 B）For a happier family, learn from the hunter-gatherers 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children ↔ For a happier family, learn from the hunter-gatherers；Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents "might also enhance their own social development" ↔ learn from the hunter-gatherers；there are ways to incorporate them into western life ↔ learn from the hunter-gatherers）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、C 项属以偏概全、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested. The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults. Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and "baby-wearing", in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,从非洲狩猎采集者那里获得的育儿建议可能是培养更快乐儿童的关键。这一观点基于对博茨瓦纳Kung人等群体的研究,在那里每个孩子都由许多成年人照顾。年仅四岁的Kung儿童就会帮助照看年幼的孩子,而"背婴",即用吊带背着婴儿,被认为是常态。

paragraphs.en: According to Dr. Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents.
paragraphs.zh: 剑桥大学进化人类学家Nikhil Chaudhary博士认为,这些被称为异亲抚育的做法可以减少儿童和父母的焦虑。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life. In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery. The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities.
paragraphs.zh: 儿童精神病学家Annie Swanepoel博士认为,有办法将这些做法融入西方生活。在德国,有一个项目将养老院与托儿所配对。养老院的老人帮助照看孩子,这种安排类似于异亲抚育。另一项措施可以是鼓励不同年级儿童之间的友谊,以模仿狩猎采集群体中无人监督的混龄游戏小组。

paragraphs.en: In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history. This abrupt shift to an "intensive mothering narrative", which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful. "Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences," they wrote.
paragraphs.zh: 在发表于《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》的一篇论文中,研究人员表示,西方核心家庭是一项与进化史决裂的近期发明。这种突然转向"密集型母职叙事"的做法很可能是有害的,这种叙事认为母亲应该独自承担育儿责任。他们写道:"这种叙事会导致母亲精疲力竭,并产生危险的后果。"

paragraphs.en: By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child's care. One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下,在狩猎采集社会中,父母以外的成年人可以提供儿童近一半的照料。此前一项研究考察了刚果民主共和国的Efé人。研究发现,婴儿在18周大时平均每天有14个异亲抚育者,每小时在照顾者之间传递八次。

paragraphs.en: Chaudhary said that parents now had less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans' evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to a child's wellbeing. An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
paragraphs.zh: Chaudhary表示,与人类进化史的大部分时期相比,父母现在从家庭和社会网络获得的育儿支持更少,但引入额外的照顾者可以减少压力和产妇抑郁,这可能对儿童的健康产生"连锁"效益。在狩猎采集社会中出生的婴儿可能有十多个照顾者——这与英国的托儿所环境形成鲜明对比,英国的规定要求一名照顾者对应四名两到三岁的儿童。

paragraphs.en: While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents "might also enhance their own social development".
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员表示,虽然狩猎采集者儿童通过在混龄游戏小组中的观察和模仿来学习,但西方的"指导式教学",即要求学生坐着不动,可能会导致注意力缺陷多动障碍等疾病。Chaudhary表示,英国应该探索这样一种可能性:年长的兄弟姐妹帮助父母"也可能促进他们自己的社会发展"。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: A Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes, Greg Rutkowski has made illustrations for games such as Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering. And he's become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation. His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion. The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts. For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski," and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style. But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists. As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright. And artists like Rutkowski have had enough. According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million Stable Diffusion images and prompts, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times. Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences. Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published. The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn't his. "It's been just a month. What about in a year? I probably won't be able to find my work out there because the Internet will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski said. "That's concerning." Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators—and some are now fighting back. Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion's data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright. Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes. But it's also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems. "There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz. The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation. One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water. The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges. All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways. Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a "continuous surface connection" to bodies of water. This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules. And it carries "significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States," as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed. In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections. But that's a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay. The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries. The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware. Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA? Perhaps some, but all? That seems unlikely. It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors. And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states. Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream. And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved. We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them, but teeming with aquatic life. It's worth the scenic drive.

paragraphs.en: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways. This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules. And it carries "significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States," as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.
paragraphs.zh: 上月底,美国最高法院在一起Idaho案件中作出裁决,大幅削减了美国环境保护署(EPA)监管湿地和水道的权限,这使得上述一切面临巨大风险。具体而言,5比4的多数意见裁定,EPA根据《清洁水法》权限保护的湿地必须与水体具有"连续的地表连接"。这一监管范围的缩小对建筑商、采矿运营商和其他经常与环境法规相冲突的商业利益来说是一场胜利。正如大法官Brett Kavanaugh所指出的,它"对全美的水质和洪水控制具有重大影响"。

paragraphs.en: In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections. But that's a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay. The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries. The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware. Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA? Perhaps some, but all? That seems unlikely.
paragraphs.zh: 在Maryland,好消息是该州有许多提供湿地保护的法律。但这是一种非常短视的看法,特别是涉及Chesapeake Bay时。现实是,水以及经常伴随而来的污染物并不尊重州界。Chesapeake的流域面积达64000平方英里,延伸至Virginia、Pennsylvania、New York、West Virginia、District of Columbia和Delaware。这些司法管辖区会提供Sackett诉EPA案中被否定的同等保护吗?也许有些会,但全部都会?这似乎不太可能。

paragraphs.en: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors. And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states. Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.
paragraphs.zh: 将此类法院裁决仅仅视为维护土地所有者权利是过于简单且具有误导性的,因为其后果对邻居可能是如此严重。这也提醒人们,EPA参与Chesapeake Bay项目长期以来一直至关重要,因为这是超越邻州财力雄厚的特殊利益集团影响的手段。举一个说明性例子,Pennsylvania的农民在决定是否在田地上施撒动物粪便时,并不会考虑Maryland明年的蓝蟹收成,然而流入附近溪流的径流会对下游产生巨大影响。

paragraphs.en: And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved. We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them, but teeming with aquatic life. It's worth the scenic drive.
paragraphs.zh: 因此,我们呼吁从Richmond到Albany的州议员考虑审查他们自己的湿地保护措施,亲自了解其中涉及的巨大利害关系。我们可以邀请他们访问Dorchester County的Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge,在那里白头鹰飞越浅到无法划船穿越的潮汐沼泽,但却充满水生生物。这趟风景优美的旅程是值得的。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. "Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past," she writes. "An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable." Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can't be expected to embrace the changes if they're not seeing the benefits—if they're just seeing good jobs being destroyed. In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech's inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. "We're talking about disruption," she says. "These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed." To make such "tremendous changes," she adds, you need social buy-in. Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities. According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings's Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States. The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow. Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants. A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don't simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country's reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK's wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world. Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don't go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. "Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood," said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. "For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall." The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent. The causes of the UK's current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels. It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects. While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall added: "While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero." "While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground. Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand."

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it's time to turn over the keys. "It's a complete life-changer" when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke. "The American Medical Association advises physicians that 'in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician's advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,'" Menke wrote. "Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality," she counseled. Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. "There's not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies," she said. "We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe" and what can help, said Dugan. One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two. Many older drivers don't see eye doctors or can't afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can't turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven't changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily. As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won't solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. "If we're going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably."

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone. While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections. Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties." Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained. Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is. As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.

questions.explanation: 第 37 题是推断题，正确答案 A）Its coverage needs to be extended. 定位句在第 2 段：现行的健康隐私法（例如《健康保险流通与责任法案》）主要管医院、诊所、保险公司在线保存病历的方式。而这些 app 和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备所收集的健康信息，通常得不到同等的法律保护。正确项与原文构成同义替换（is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online ↔ Its coverage；The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections ↔ needs to be extended）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有=换维度、C 项属无中生有=横插无关话题、D 项属张冠李戴=对象角色错位，均可排除。

questions.stem: Before sharing its users' health information, Flo Health is required to______.
options: A) seek the approval of the FTC
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 D）obtain their explicit permission 定位句在第 3 段：Flo Health 与 FTC 通过一份同意令了结此案：该同意令要求公司在分享用户健康信息之前必须获得用户明确肯定的同意，并要求其指示第三方删除已获取的数据。正确项与原文构成同义替换（get app users' express affirmative consent ↔ obtain their explicit permission）。其余三项中，A 项属张冠李戴=同意主体错位、B 项属无中生有=蹭关键词造新要求、C 项属答非所问=时点错位，均可排除。

questions.stem: What challenge is the FTC currently faced with?
options: A) The complexity of health information.
B) The rapid increase in new health apps.
C) The subtle deceptiveness of health apps.
D) The difficulty in assessing consumer harm.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是细节题，正确答案 B）The rapid increase in new health apps. 定位句在第 4 段：尽管 FTC 正在竭尽所能确保这些 app 兑现对消费者关于敏感健康信息处置的承诺，但这些健康 app 涌入市场的速度，显示出这一挑战何其巨大。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market ↔ The rapid increase in new health apps）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有=造新挑战维度、C 项属偷换概念=移位+加修饰、D 项属无中生有=蹭术语造新难点，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that health data protection______.
options: A) has been embraced by health app developers
B) has been a focus of federal policy-making
C) has encountered opposition in California
D) has gained legislative support in some states
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是推断题，正确答案 D）has gained legislative support in some states 定位句在第 5 段：至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为短期内全面的联邦隐私立法不太可能。各州已开始自行推出方案，加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加州凭借 2018 年《加州消费者隐私法案》一直走在州一级隐私保护的最前列。弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他也最近通过了州一级的消费者数据隐私立法。正确项与原文构成同义替换（States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data ↔ has gained legislative support in some states；California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 ↔ legislative support；Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation ↔ in some states）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有=换主语角色、B 项属与原文相反=方向颠倒、C 项属与原文相反=立场颠倒，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你查看手机上的应用程序,很可能至少有一个与健康相关的应用——而且可能有好几个。无论是心理健康应用、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是其他什么,我们中的许多人都在利用这项技术以某种形式更好地追踪自己的健康状况。健康与护理应用审查组织最近的研究发现,市场上有35万个健康应用程序,其中仅2020年就推出了9万个。

paragraphs.en: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors' offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然这些应用程序有很多好处,但我们输入的个人信息如何被收集、保护和在线共享并不总是清楚的。现有的健康隐私法律,如《健康保险携带和责任法案》,主要关注医院、诊所、门诊部和保险公司在线存储健康记录的方式。这些应用程序和健康数据追踪可穿戴设备收集的健康信息通常不会受到同样的法律保护。

paragraphs.en: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that "despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users' sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties." Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users' express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
paragraphs.zh: 在没有额外保护措施的情况下,公司可能会以消费者未授权或未预料到的方式共享(并可能将其货币化)个人健康信息。2021年,Flo Health面临联邦贸易委员会的调查。联邦贸易委员会在一项投诉中指控"尽管有明确的隐私声明,该公司还是控制了用户的敏感生育数据并将其与第三方共享"。Flo Health与联邦贸易委员会通过一项同意令解决了此事,要求该公司在共享用户健康信息之前获得应用程序用户的明确肯定同意,并指示第三方删除他们已获得的数据。

paragraphs.en: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company's privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
paragraphs.zh: 《联邦贸易委员会法》第5条授权联邦贸易委员会对不公平或欺骗性行为采取执法行动,这意味着联邦贸易委员会只能在公司的隐私做法具有误导性或造成不正当消费者损害之后采取行动。虽然联邦贸易委员会正在尽其所能确保应用程序信守对消费者关于处理其敏感健康信息的承诺,但这些健康应用程序进入市场的速度表明这是一个多么巨大的挑战。

paragraphs.en: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
paragraphs.zh: 至于联邦立法的前景,评论人士认为短期内似乎不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法。各州已开始实施自己的解决方案,以加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加利福尼亚州一直处于州隐私努力的前沿,制定了2018年《加利福尼亚州消费者隐私法》。弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州最近也通过了州消费者数据隐私立法。

paragraphs.en: Your social life is defined as "the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working". It's important to have a social life, but what's right for one person won't be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, [1] some of us may feel drained, even if it's doing something we enjoy.
paragraphs.zh: 你的社交生活被定义为"当你不工作时，为了娱乐而与他人一起做的活动"。拥有社交生活很重要,但适合一个人的方式不一定适合另一个人。我们中的一些人会因为与他人共度大量时间而感到精力充沛,而我们中的另一些人可能会感到疲惫,即使是在做自己喜欢的事情。

paragraphs.en: This is why finding a [2] in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not [3] others, can make you feel lonely and [4] . Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and [5] a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, [6] , you are working from home and you are [7] on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can [8] periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是为什么在社交生活中找到平衡是关键。独自度过太多时间,不与他人见面,会让你感到孤独和疏离。众所周知,孤独会影响你的心理健康并导致情绪低落。任何人在任何时候都可能感到孤独。例如,如果你在家工作,错过了办公室里通常发生的社交对话,这种情况可能尤其真实。其他生活变化也可能引发孤独时期,比如退休、换工作或成为父母。

paragraphs.en: It's important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to [9] a social life, but it can feel overwhelming [10] . It's a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet [11] people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to [12] a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and [13] ideas.
paragraphs.zh: 认识到这些孤独感很重要。有一些方法可以重建社交生活,但一开始可能会让人感到难以应对。从思考你喜欢的爱好开始是个好主意。然后你可以找到与这些爱好相关的群体和活动,在那里你将能够遇到志同道合的人。有针对新手父母的群体,针对想首次尝试新运动的人的群体,或者针对同一职业的人聚会和分享想法的社交活动。

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, it's [14] possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you're always doing something and there is never any [15] in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social [16] . We all have our own social limit and it's important to recognise when you're feeling like it's all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be [17] of poor social health. Make sure you [18] some time in your diary when you're [19] for socialising and use this time to relax, [20] and recover.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面,社交生活也可能过度。如果你觉得自己总是在做某事,日程表上永远没有任何休息时间,你可能会遭受社交倦怠或社交疲劳。我们每个人都有自己的社交极限,重要的是要认识到何时你感觉这一切太多了。情绪低落、精力不足、易怒和睡眠困难都可能是社交健康不良的迹象。确保在你的日程表中标出一些无法参加社交活动的时间,利用这段时间来放松、休息和恢复。

reading.passage: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out. A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy. "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said. The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils aged nine and ten—at 45 state primary schools that had not been "previously exposed to RSC pedagogy". They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage. The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words "classed as more sophisticated or rarer", and wrote at greater length. They also "appear to be more comfortable writing in role … while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion". The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions". O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful". She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes." The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said. But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
