paragraphs.en: There's fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness. A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they're all in headphones. People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes. A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and "talking on the brush handle".
paragraphs.zh: 人们享受纯粹新鲜感的见证充满趣味。一幅漫画嘲讽一群人无法交谈,因为他们都戴着耳机。有人报告说广播音乐让工人们哼起了新曲调。一位女士说自从无线电到来后街头斗殴减少了,但停下来"靠在扫帚把上聊天"的情况也少了。

paragraphs.en: By and large the wireless was welcome. I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered "a lot of variety…things I thought I'd never be interested in…ice hockey perhaps". True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task. In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: "I caught up with the news, learnt some 17th-century history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope."
paragraphs.zh: 总的来说,无线电是受欢迎的。我喜欢那位来自三十年代研究中的男士,他发现无线电突然提供了"很多种类……我以为自己永远不会感兴趣的东西……也许是冰球"。确实如此:在超过80年的前数字时代,线性语音广播带来了意外惊喜的礼物,为汽车旅程或枯燥的体力劳动随机注入活力。在我自己关于广播的书中,我记录了在一次驾驶中如何:"我了解了新闻,学习了一些17世纪的历史,并被一个关于听诊器历史的朴实节目令人惊讶地教育了一番。"

paragraphs.en: But radio's enriching serendipity is ebbing. With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when. And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
paragraphs.zh: 但广播丰富的意外惊喜正在消退。有了多个网络和无数播客,智能手机用户可以选择听什么和何时听。虽然戴着耳机散步听任何内容都很美好,但无限的选择鼓励我们缩进小众兴趣和投合的信念。

paragraphs.en: A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered? Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading. But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest. Whatever we do, innovation will happen. Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfie-vanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of "talking on the brush handle". It's enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.
paragraphs.zh: 在Marconi和Reith之后一百年,单纯倾听的艺术是否正处于危险之中?有人会说有声书的繁荣复兴了它,尽管我想你也可以担心阅读的衰落。但发明塑造了我们所有人,当技术社会习惯确实发生改变时,值得注意并询问是否要稍加控制或保护最年轻的一代。无论我们做什么,创新都会发生。今天我们为盯着智能手机和自拍虚荣的孤立文化而苦恼,但早在1939年就有那位女士遗憾地说,当她所在的街道都有了无线电后,就失去了"靠在扫帚把上聊天"的邻里习惯。这足以让人放下智能手机,拿着院子扫帚走到前面去。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to "put everything out," he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent. Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings. The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier. They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns. In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month. In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression. This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. "Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions." To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient. These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions. Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. "It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging," said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Swetnam was surprised by ____
options: A) the scarcity of tree-ring research in the U.S.
B) the firefighting measures in ancient Europe.
C) the forest management practices in the 1970s.
D) the number of wildfires in precolonial times.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 D）the number of wildfires in precolonial times. 定位句在第 1 段：但是当 Swetnam 进入亚利桑那大学树轮研究室读研时，他惊讶地发现一份记录显示，早在欧洲殖民者抵达这片大陆几百年前就已存在反复发生的火灾。正确项与原文构成同义替换（repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent ↔ the number of wildfires in precolonial times；Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings. ↔ the number of wildfires in precolonial times）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: Paragraph 2 mainly focuses on ____
options: A) the causes of previous burns.
B) the treatment of diseased trees.
C) the benefits of low-severity fires.
D) the importance of forest ecosystems.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）the benefits of low-severity fires. 定位句在第 2 段：相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁、低强度的火灾让许多生态系统更健康。正确项与原文构成同义替换（frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier ↔ the benefits of low-severity fires.；reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease ↔ the benefits of low-severity fires.）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属以偏概全、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: What did the study find about the wildfires over the past few decades?
options: A) Their intensity has vastly fluctuated.
B) Their frequency has markedly decreased.
C) Their threats have been underestimated.
D) Their records have been misinterpreted.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）Their frequency has markedly decreased. 定位句在第 3 段：在这项研究中，研究者把历史上的火灾节律与近几十年记录的野火相比较，发现了一个惊人的缺口：NAFSN 各站点经历的火灾数量不到原本（在没有灭火措施时）应当出现数量的四分之一。正确项与原文构成同义替换（less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected ↔ Their frequency has markedly decreased.；uncovered a striking shortfall ↔ Their frequency has markedly decreased.）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about modern firefighting?
options: A) Its workforce needs more training.
B) Its effectiveness is questioned by the public.
C) It may render traditional tactics useless.
D) It may make severe fires harder to put out.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是推断题，正确答案 D）It may make severe fires harder to put out. 定位句在第 4 段：然而，灭火措施与气候变化的共同后果已经削弱了人类压制火灾的能力——尤其是那些在最危险天气条件下被点燃的火。正确项与原文构成同义替换（eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires ↔ It may make severe fires harder to put out.；those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions ↔ It may make severe fires harder to put out.）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Both Martin and Prichard would agree that ____
options: A) it is challenging to predict large wildfires.
B) it is urgent to assess the use of planned fires.
C) it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.
D) it is rewarding to double fire detection efforts.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是态度题，正确答案 C）it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient ↔ it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.；we need this work even more ↔ it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to "put everything out," he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent. Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
paragraphs.zh: 当Tom Swetnam在20世纪70年代加入美国林务局时,他回忆说,自己的任务是"扑灭一切火灾"。但当Swetnam进入亚利桑那大学树木年轮研究实验室攻读研究生时,他惊讶地发现,在欧洲殖民者到达这片大陆之前的数百年间,有反复发生火灾的记录。他分析的一些树木的年轮中有超过20处火灾疤痕。

paragraphs.en: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier. They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
paragraphs.zh: 火灾如此频繁发生的事实意味着它们不可能严重到足以杀死大多数树木。相反,越来越多的研究表明,频繁的低强度火灾使许多生态系统更加健康。它们清除了森林中死亡和患病的树木,减少了竞争并抑制了疾病的传播。由于易燃物质无法在地表堆积,火势往往移动缓慢,并在到达先前燃烧过的区域时逐渐熄灭。

paragraphs.en: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month. In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
paragraphs.zh: 2022年,Swetnam和其他科学家合作编制了一个来自整个大陆的火灾疤痕树木数据库。他们的北美树木年轮火灾疤痕网络(NAFSN)为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。在该研究中,研究人员将历史火灾频率与过去几十年记录的野火进行了比较,发现了显著的短缺。NAFSN站点经历的火灾数量不到没有火灾抑制情况下预期数量的四分之一。

paragraphs.en: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. "Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions."
paragraphs.zh: 国际荒地火灾协会前主席Kelly Martin说,这一缺口证明了现代消防的有效性。"然而,抑制和气候变化的综合后果削弱了人类抑制火灾的能力,特别是那些在最危险天气条件下点燃的火灾。"

paragraphs.en: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient. These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
paragraphs.zh: Martin说,为了防止整个生态系统化为灰烬,人们必须将健康的火灾带回需要它的地方。在Yosemite国家公园,Martin监督使用所谓的计划性燃烧来使景观更具韧性。这些火灾是经过精心规划的,并在天气条件使火势易于控制的时期有意点燃,有助于消除在公园重要设施周围积累的部分燃料。研究表明,这些计划性燃烧使随后的野火强度降低,即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下。

paragraphs.en: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. "It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging," said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
paragraphs.zh: 专家说,然而,尽管科学家和公职人员越来越一致认为我们的森林需要更多火灾,但气候变化正在使这一策略更具挑战性。华盛顿大学火灾生态学家Susan Prichard说:"这是一把双刃剑,因为在气候变化下野火变得更加严重和更大,我们更需要这项工作,但这项工作也变得更具挑战性。"

paragraphs.en: While AI offers exciting possibilities, it also raises ethical [13] . There is a risk of deepening societal beauty [14] and perpetuating unattainable beauty standards. [15] , AI-powered beauty filters and editing tools can lead to distorted self-perception and [16] body dissatisfaction. As summarized in a recent post on "The Hidden Dangers of Online Beauty Filters", [17] on this technology for social presentation can cause harm [18] body image issues, lower self-esteem, and social anxiety.

paragraphs.en: It's important to note that while AI can enhance our [19] of beauty, it should not [20] the genuine human experience and the emotional connections we derive from seeing the beauty in each other.

reading.passage: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now? And anyway — aren't they all closing? The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday. As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald's. Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity. While books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support. There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs. Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP's surgery. There are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free. In return for all of this, you'll be asked for precisely nothing. There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself; you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not. There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same. Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated. There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure. The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed. An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England. It is, of course, 230 libraries too many. So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do. The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children. If we don't use them, we will end up losing them. And for those who haven't been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.

options: A) the crisis faced by libraries.
D) the flaws existing in libraries.
questions.explanation: 第 24 题是细节题，正确答案 A）the crisis faced by libraries. 定位句在第 6 段：公共财务与会计学会的年度调查显示，全英范围内（关闭数）接近 800 间；艺术委员会持有的官方统计则记录英格兰为 230 间。当然，230 间也算关得太多了。正确项与原文构成同义替换（230 libraries too many ↔ the crisis faced by libraries；struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure ↔ the crisis faced by libraries）。其余三项中，B 项属与原文相反、C 项属张冠李戴、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following is suggested for libraries in the last paragraph?
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是细节题，正确答案 C）Improving user convenience. 定位句在第 7 段：该审查建议：开展全国品牌宣传以增强图书馆的实体存在感；重启允许会员在全国任一图书馆使用借阅证的方案；为儿童自动开通会员资格。正确项与原文构成同义替换（enable members to use their card in any library in the country ↔ Improving user convenience；automatic memberships for children ↔ Improving user convenience）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属过度推断，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now? And anyway — aren't they all closing?
paragraphs.zh: 问人们关于公共图书馆的看法,某种印象便会浮现在脑海中:尘封的、过时的,那种你小时候喜欢的地方,但就像英国的海滨小镇一样,你现在还会去那里吗?而且不管怎样——它们不是都在关闭吗?

paragraphs.en: The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday. As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald's.
paragraphs.zh: 现实情况截然不同,正如我在文化部委托我对英格兰公共图书馆进行独立审查时所发现的那样,该审查于昨日发布。当我走访全国各地的图书馆时,我惊讶地了解到图书馆的数量(2892家)是麦当劳分店数量的两倍多。

paragraphs.en: Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity. While books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.
paragraphs.zh: 走进其中任何一家,你都会发现一片繁忙的景象。虽然书籍现在是、而且应该永远是任何图书馆的核心,但图书馆还提供众多其他服务:就业咨询、语言课程或数字访问和支持。

paragraphs.en: There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs. Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP's surgery. There are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.
paragraphs.zh: 有些图书馆设有商业和知识产权中心,可以帮助企业主和创业者。许多图书馆有护士现场进行基本的健康检查,并与全科医生诊所建立联系。有些图书馆年轻人可以免费借用符合国际足联标准的足球。

paragraphs.en: In return for all of this, you'll be asked for precisely nothing. There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself; you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not. There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same. Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated. There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 作为这一切的回报,你不会被要求付出任何东西。不会有任何收费,你也永远不会被要求证明或解释自己;你只会受到欢迎,需要帮助时会得到帮助,不需要时也不会被打扰。没有其他机构,无论是公共的还是私人的,能做出同样的承诺。然而我们的图书馆仍然常常被忽视和低估。访问量总体下降,许多图书馆由于地方当局持续面临财政压力而陷入困境。

paragraphs.en: The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed. An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England. It is, of course, 230 libraries too many. So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.
paragraphs.zh: 自2010年以来关闭的图书馆数量存在争议。英国特许公共财政与会计协会的年度调查显示全英国有近800家;艺术委员会保存的官方统计数据记录英格兰有230家。当然,这230家图书馆已经太多了。因此,如果我们要为子孙后代保护图书馆,就必须提高人们对图书馆及其工作的认识。

paragraphs.en: The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children. If we don't use them, we will end up losing them. And for those who haven't been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.
paragraphs.zh: 该审查报告建议开展一项全国性的品牌宣传活动,以增强图书馆的实体存在感,重新推行一项计划使会员能够在全国任何图书馆使用其借书证,以及为儿童提供自动会员资格。如果我们不使用它们,最终就会失去它们。对于那些有一段时间没去过图书馆的人来说,他们可能会对所发现的情况感到惊讶。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems. Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated. But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential information, even though over a third of people don't realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secrets…secret. For businesses, the implications are worrying. Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example. It gains Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user — rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties. This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world. Employers are taking note and taking action. According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations. But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules. They have their reasons — around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues. The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure. Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage. There's also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed — 40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI. By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, businesses can positively shift the AI landscape. With AI's potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience, it's up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy. There's no need to back away from progress, as long as we're equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend. And this is where the challenge lies. There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it's easy to fall victim. But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our businesses, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, workers' engagement with AI can ____
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 B）give them emotional support. 定位句在第 1 段：我们的数据显示，像这样与 AI 互动可以让我们感到被倾听、不那么孤独。正确项与原文构成同义替换（feeling heard and less isolated ↔ give them emotional support）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Microsoft Copilot is cited to show that the use of AI may ____
options: A) pose a threat to businesses.
questions.explanation: 第 27 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）pose a threat to businesses. 定位句在第 2 段：这就意味着任何敏感的商业信息都有可能被暴露给整个世界。正确项与原文构成同义替换（any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world ↔ pose a threat to businesses）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Some employees choose to break the rules on AI due to ____

B) the desire to stay well-informed.

questions.stem: To positively shift the AI landscape, businesses should ____

B) prioritise the quality of AI-produced content.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, we may easily fall victim to AI as we ____

C) tend to overemphasise its power.

questions.explanation: 第 30 题是细节题，正确答案 A）have a limited understanding of it. 定位句在第 4 段：外面有那么多产品，用巨额广告和营销预算去推广，以至于人们很容易上当受害。正确项与原文构成同义替换（as long as we're equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend ↔ have a limited understanding of it；so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets ↔ have a limited understanding of it）。其余三项中，B 项属张冠李戴、C 项属无中生有、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems. Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated. But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential information, even though over a third of people don't realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secrets…secret.
paragraphs.zh: 根据我们的研究，英国约有五分之一的员工像朋友一样与AI交谈，在个人和职业问题上寻求指导。我们的数据显示，以这种方式与AI互动可以让我们感到被倾听，减少孤独感。但是，随着这种新建立的联系，我们中的许多人分享了敏感的、有时是高度机密的信息，尽管超过三分之一的人没有意识到AI平台可能并不擅长保守我们的秘密……秘密。

paragraphs.en: For businesses, the implications are worrying. Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example. It gains Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user — rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties. This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world. Employers are taking note and taking action. According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations. But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules. They have their reasons — around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues.
paragraphs.zh: 对企业而言，这种影响令人担忧。以Microsoft Copilot为例，它使Microsoft获得对任何用户输入或输出数据的广泛权利——以其认为合适的任何方式使用这些数据的权利；它甚至可以与第三方分享这些数据。这意味着任何敏感的商业信息都可能暴露给全世界。雇主们注意到了这一点并采取了行动。根据我们的研究，25%的雇主决定完全禁止AI或规范其在组织内的使用。但即使有这些政策，一些员工仍选择违反规定。他们有自己的理由——约63%的员工报告称使用AI提高了他们的生产力，有些人甚至觉得AI比他们的人类同事提供更多帮助。

paragraphs.en: The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure. Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage. There's also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed — 40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI. By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, businesses can positively shift the AI landscape.
paragraphs.zh: 这种情况需要在利用AI提高生产力和冒机密数据泄露风险之间保持微妙的平衡。雇主需要像管理任何其他形式的数据共享或存储一样谨慎地管理AI工具。还有一个知识差距需要解决——受访者中有40%不确定谁保留AI生成内容的所有权。通过灌输AI使用的最佳实践并制定随技术发展而演变的政策，企业可以积极改变AI格局。

paragraphs.en: With AI's potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience, it's up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy. There's no need to back away from progress, as long as we're equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend. And this is where the challenge lies. There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it's easy to fall victim. But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our businesses, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.
paragraphs.zh: 鉴于AI简化我们职业生活、处理行政事务并提升工作体验的潜力，我们有责任谨慎使用它，使其在不损害我们隐私的情况下为我们提供支持。没有必要退避进步，只要我们具备确保AI保持友好的知识和工具。而这正是挑战所在。市场上有如此多的产品，用巨额的广告和营销预算进行推广，很容易成为受害者。但通过在我们的企业中建立数字责任文化，我们可以创造一个AI能够在不泄露秘密的情况下帮助我们的未来。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike. Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours. The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin. In many cases, it is the best option — in terms of travel time and cost — for both leisure and business travellers. This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP. Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage. Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023. The huge improvements in Italy's obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie. RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026. Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years. But lack of capacity is another problem. Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable. "We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there's a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex," he said. A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities. If there's congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected. One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links. Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts. It will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the high-speed rail network in Italy ____
options: A) is seen by tourists as outdated.
B) is a popular option for travelling.
C) is inadequately utilised by locals.
D) is an example of good maintenance.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 B）is a popular option for travelling. 定位句在第 1 段：自 2008 年罗马—米兰高铁网开通以来，火车已经成为意大利本地人和游客同样首选的出行方式。正确项与原文构成同义替换（trains have become the preferred means of travel ↔ is a popular option for travelling）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: Ferrovie is quoted in Paragraph 3 to show ____
options: A) the common occurrence of train delays.
B) the value of the Italian train network.
C) the wide media coverage of trains.
D) the high efficiency of Trenitalia.
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）the common occurrence of train delays. 定位句在第 3 段：中断越来越频繁，火车延误如今已成意大利媒体报道的常客。意大利国铁集团——掌控运营商 Trenitalia 和国家铁路网 RFI 的公共控股集团——表示，2023 年其运营的所有高铁中有 23% 出现晚点。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Disruptions have become increasingly frequent ↔ the common occurrence of train delays；23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023 ↔ the common occurrence of train delays）。其余三项中，B 项属答非所问、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Which of the following is one cause of the disruptions in the network?
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 C）Its limited capacity. 定位句在第 5 段：但容量不足是另一个问题。交通经济学家安德烈亚·朱里钦表示，已规划的投资将带来改善，但在此期间中断不可避免。"我们是一个混合系统，没有冗余容量，线路上一旦出点小问题，局面就会变得非常复杂。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（lack of capacity ↔ Its limited capacity；there is no spare capacity ↔ Its limited capacity）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: It can be learned that the mixed system ____
options: A) provides a wide choice of routes.
C) increases the level of travel comfort.
D) puts the high-speed network in trouble.
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是推断题，正确答案 D）puts the high-speed network in trouble. 定位句在第 5 段：所谓混合系统，是指高铁在某些路段或穿越大城市时必须借用普通线路。一旦发生拥堵，或譬如某列普通列车抛锚，整张高铁网都会受影响。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the entire high-speed network is affected ↔ puts the high-speed network in trouble；If there's congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected. ↔ puts the high-speed network in trouble）。其余三项中，A 项属与原文相反、B 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: Improvements to the Italian train network will include ____
options: A) reconstructing the regular train lines.
C) building more stations in urban centres.
D) enhancing the safety of high-speed trains.
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是细节题，正确答案 B）shortening high-speed train intervals. 定位句在第 7 段：专家表示，改进也将来自 RFI 多年来一直投资的高密度技术和卫星信号系统。它将使同一线路上同时运行的高铁列车之间的距离得以缩短，按朱里钦的说法，这应当意味着运力和通行流畅度的显著提升。正确项与原文构成同义替换（a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line ↔ shortening high-speed train intervals）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike. Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours. The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin. In many cases, it is the best option — in terms of travel time and cost — for both leisure and business travellers.
paragraphs.zh: 自2008年罗马与米兰之间的高速铁路网络开通以来,火车已成为意大利本地人和游客在全国各地出行的首选方式。快速列车可以在三小时内完成两座城市之间500公里的行程。该铁路网还连接那不勒斯、博洛尼亚、佛罗伦萨和都灵。在许多情况下,无论对休闲旅客还是商务旅客而言,它都是在旅行时间和成本方面的最佳选择。

paragraphs.en: This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是为什么最近由大量维护工程造成的严重延误使铁路行业在大多数人外出度假的时期陷入混乱,这对一个旅游业占GDP百分之十的国家的商业活动至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage. Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.
paragraphs.zh: 中断变得越来越频繁,列车延误现在已成为意大利媒体报道的固定内容。Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane是一家公共控股集团,拥有列车运营商Trenitalia和国家铁路网络RFI,该集团表示其运营的所有高速列车中有百分之二十三在2023年出现晚点。

paragraphs.en: The huge improvements in Italy's obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie. RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026. Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.
paragraphs.zh: Ferrovie表示,意大利陈旧基础设施的巨大改善在一定程度上解释了中断的原因。网络运营商RFI是欧洲复苏基金的最大单一受益方,计划到2026年投资240亿欧元。Ferrovie将在未来10年内对基础设施投资总计1240亿欧元。

paragraphs.en: But lack of capacity is another problem. Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable. "We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there's a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex," he said. A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities. If there's congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.
paragraphs.zh: 但运力不足是另一个问题。交通经济学家Andrea Giuricin表示,计划中的投资将带来改善,但期间的中断是不可避免的。他说:"我们有一个混合系统,没有备用运力,一旦线路上出现小问题,情况就会变得高度复杂。"混合系统意味着高速列车在某些路线上或通过大城市时必须在普通轨道上行驶。如果出现拥堵或者例如一辆地方列车发生故障,整个高速铁路网都会受到影响。

paragraphs.en: One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links.
paragraphs.zh: 升级将带来的最重要变化之一是通过建设地下铁路连接线,在某些城市中心将高速线路与普通线路分离。

paragraphs.en: Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts. It will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.
paragraphs.zh: 专家表示,改善还将来自RFI多年来一直在投资的高密度技术和卫星信号系统。Giuricin认为,这将使在任何给定时间在同一线路上行驶的高速列车之间的距离得以缩短,这应该意味着运力和交通流畅性的显著提升。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals. The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024. What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down. Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now. The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed. Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive. At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically. Chicago's summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they're in and the city of Chicago as a whole. Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special. We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city's largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations. The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs. Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago's most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection. In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance. Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history. This year, we've been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest. We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park's unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect. This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you'll remember that they exist because of community support. A thriving summer festival season doesn't happen by accident; it happens when we all chip in.

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the Silver Room Block Party ____
options: A) has been replaced by other festivals.
B) has gained great international fame.
C) was held in various neighborhoods.
D) was an appealing cultural gathering.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 D）was an appealing cultural gathering. 定位句在第 1 段：（这场活动）最初只是一场小型邻里聚会，后来发展成一项大型文化盛事，近二十年间每年吸引数万人参与，直到突然停办。正确项与原文构成同义替换（massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year ↔ an appealing cultural gathering；one of its most beloved street festivals ↔ appealing）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属过度推断、C 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: One reality street festival organizers face is that ____
options: A) they are unable to use the donations wisely.
B) they are unable to get sufficient facilities.
C) they have to tackle financial difficulties.
D) they have to step up security measures.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是细节题，正确答案 C）they have to tackle financial difficulties. 定位句在第 2 段：Williams 把制作成本上涨和参与者捐款下滑列为 Silver Room Block Party 无法继续的主要原因，并指出这是所有街道节日组织者眼下都要面对的现实。正确项与原文构成同义替换（rising production costs and declining attendee donations ↔ tackle financial difficulties；The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed ↔ financial difficulties；donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically ↔ financial difficulties）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 3 and 4, Chicago's street festivals ____
options: B) are funded by the government.
C) contribute to the local economy.
D) are famous for their music shows.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 C）contribute to the local economy. 定位句在第 3 段：芝加哥的夏日节日远不止是娱乐——它们是经济引擎，直接惠及所在的社区以及整个芝加哥市。正确项与原文构成同义替换（economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they're in and the city of Chicago as a whole ↔ contribute to the local economy；Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses ↔ contribute to the local economy）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: It is implied that the organizers of Wicker Park Fest have to ____
options: A) count on amateur artists' participation.
B) reduce the number of performances.
C) give up its most prominent feature.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是推断题，正确答案 B）reduce the number of performances. 定位句在第 5 段：今年，我们被迫缩减节日的规模——撤掉一个舞台、减少演出阵容、再做其他削减以压缩成本，同时努力让节日保持一贯的活力，继续支持本地艺术家与商家，延续 Wicker Park 独有的精神与名声。正确项与原文构成同义替换（eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers ↔ reduce the number of performances；booking fewer performers ↔ reduce the number of performances）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author holds that the future of street festivals depends on ____
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是主旨题，正确答案 B）the generosity of attendants. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（they exist because of community support ↔ the generosity of attendants；it happens when we all chip in ↔ the generosity of attendants；gate donations reached their lowest point in our history ↔ the generosity of attendants）。其余三项中，A 项属以偏概全、C 项属答非所问、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals. The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024. What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down.
paragraphs.zh: 2023年,芝加哥失去了最受欢迎的街头节日之一。由Hyde Park社区领袖Eric Williams举办的Silver Room街区派对宣布不会在2024年回归。这个节日最初只是一个小型社区聚会,后来发展成为一项大规模文化活动,在近二十年间每年迎接数万人,然后突然停办。

paragraphs.en: Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now. The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed. Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive. At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically.
paragraphs.zh: Williams指出,不断上涨的制作成本和不断下降的参与者捐款是Silver Room街区派对无法继续举办的主要原因,这凸显了所有街头节日组织者目前面临的现实。在芝加哥举办街头节日的成本已经飙升。安保、娱乐、便携式卫生间、保险甚至围栏和人员配备等基本费用都变得显著昂贵。与此同时,节日入口处的捐款却大幅下降。

paragraphs.en: Chicago's summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they're in and the city of Chicago as a whole. Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special.
paragraphs.zh: 芝加哥的夏季节日不仅仅是娱乐活动,它们是经济引擎,直接惠及所在社区和整个芝加哥市。街头节日为本地商业带来客流量,培育使我们城市与众不同的文化活力。

paragraphs.en: We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city's largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations. The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs.
paragraphs.zh: 我们经常听到人们问为什么我们在入口处请求捐款,尤其是当芝加哥爵士音乐节等该市最大型节日不要求捐款时。事实是,与那些由市政府制作的大型音乐节不同,你们社区的街头节日没有得到市政拨款,依靠赞助、摊位费和入口捐款的组合来支付成本。

paragraphs.en: Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago's most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection. In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance. Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history. This year, we've been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest. We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park's unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect.
paragraphs.zh: Wicker Park音乐节长期以来一直是芝加哥最受期待的夏季节日之一,在整个周末吸引超过7万名参与者,呈现现场独立音乐、本地艺术、小型商业摊位,以及最重要的社区联结。2024年,Wicker Park音乐节的参与人数创下纪录。尽管参与人数众多,入口捐款却降至我们历史上的最低点。今年,我们被迫缩小节日的规模。我们取消了一个舞台,预订了更少的表演者,并进行了额外削减以降低成本,同时努力保持节日一如既往的活力,一如既往地支持本地艺术家和商业,并一如既往地忠于参与者所期待的Wicker Park独特精神和声誉。

paragraphs.en: This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you'll remember that they exist because of community support. A thriving summer festival season doesn't happen by accident; it happens when we all chip in.
paragraphs.zh: 今年夏天,当你享受你最喜爱的社区街头节日时,我希望你会记得它们的存在源于社区支持。一个繁荣的夏季节日季不会偶然发生,它的实现需要我们所有人共同出力。

cloze.passage: Most of us strive for self-respect — to see ourselves in a positive light, to be [1] of who we are. Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only [2] to want to avoid them. But the thing is, [3] your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective. Much of it comes down to your [4] of what someone said or did. When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person. Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a [5] member of staff. Or, two of your friends cancel your [6] get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you. Psychologists have a [7] for this way of thinking: personalisation. But the [8] is that your boss might view you very highly. It's just you made some [9] in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time. [10] , in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just [11] their minds. In both [12] — and others that we all experience — there's another [13] at work that psychologists call mind reading. This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you, when you can't really know without [14] them directly. One simple way to avoid [15] personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's [16] . When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you — especially in the sense of saying anything deep or [17] about you. When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes. The fact your boss took the time to give you [18] at all means they care enough to want to help you [19] . When it comes to your friends — maybe it's because your friendship is so [20] that they felt able to cancel at late notice.

blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 C）proud。self-respect 与正面光下。其余三项：A）afraid 色彩相反、B）critical 态度偏负、D）tolerant 强度不足且跑偏，均可排除。
第 2 空正确答案 B）natural。only 暗示理所应当。其余三项：A）risky 评价偏负、C）admirable 褒义过头、D）foolish 贬义且与 only 冲突，均可排除。
第 3 空正确答案 A）whether。主观与否而非地点原因。其余三项：B）where 无地点缺口、C）why 主观针对真假非原因、D）how 方式与判断错配，均可排除。
第 4 空正确答案 C）perception。subjective 锁定主观解读。其余三项：A）citation 意为引用偏离、B）imitation 模仿对象错位、D）introduction 搭配语义不通，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 A）poor。picks holes 锁定负评。其余三项：B）loyal 色彩相反、C）creative 褒义不符、D）shy 维度跑偏，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 D）planned。cancel 暗示已有约定。其余三项：A）sponsored 赞助维度跑偏、B）crowded 形容场地非聚会、C）disputed 争议含义不符，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 B）term。冒号后 personalisation 是术语。其余三项：A）method 方法非名称、C）design 设计与命名无关、D）goal 目标偏离，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 D）reality。But 引出与前文相反的真相。其余三项：A）evidence 证据需有出处、B）theory 理论与可能错位、C）condition 条件与真相无关，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 C）mistakes。point these out 反推 mistakes。其余三项：A）complaints 抱怨方向反、B）choices 中性不触发指正、D）suggestions 建议来源错位，均可排除。
第 10 空正确答案 A）Similarly。老板事例与朋友事例平行。其余三项：B）Relatively 相对偏离、C）Accordingly 因果不成立、D）Contrarily 对立关系反方向，均可排除。
第 11 空正确答案 B）changed。cancel 与 change one's mind。其余三项：A）opened 搭配不解释取消、C）trained 训练大脑跑偏、D）cleared 清空思绪偏离，均可排除。
第 12 空正确答案 D）examples。老板与朋友是两个例子。其余三项：A）quotations 引文性质不符、B）experiments 实验语境错配、C）questions 问题层级跑偏，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 A）process。personalisation 是 process 的并列。其余三项：B）objective 目标性质不符、C）outcome 结果偏离过程、D）background 背景性质错位，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 D）asking。知道别人想法靠直接问。其余三项：A）blaming 指责非获知途径、B）warning 警告与求知无关、C）teaching 教导而非询问，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 C）engaging in。personalisation 是心理活动。其余三项：A）arguing about 争论方向跑偏、B）accounting for 解释非陷入、D）interfering with 干扰对象不符，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 A）happened。negative assumptions 的对象。其余三项：B）continued 持续性偏题、C）returned 回归与情境无关、D）disappeared 消失方向不符，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 D）fundamental。deep 锁定根本性。其余三项：A）casual 随意与深刻相反、B）obvious 明显非深刻、C）familiar 熟悉与深刻错位，均可排除。
第 18 空正确答案 B）feedback。picks holes + point out 即 feedback。其余三项：A）reward 奖赏方向错、C）trust 信任范畴跑偏、D）proof 证据维度错位，均可排除。
第 19 空正确答案 C）improve。feedback + do better 锁 improve。其余三项：A）innovate 创新过窄、B）concentrate 专注偏题、D）relax 放松方向反，均可排除。
第 20 空正确答案 B）strong。敢临时取消因关系牢固。其余三项：A）strange 古怪不合逻辑、C）vulnerable 脆弱与取消因果反、D）valuable 宝贵不直接导致敢取消，均可排除。

paragraphs.en: Most of us strive for self-respect — to see ourselves in a positive light, to be [1] of who we are. Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only [2] to want to avoid them. But the thing is, [3] your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective. Much of it comes down to your [4] of what someone said or did.
paragraphs.zh: 我们大多数人都追求自尊——以积极的眼光看待自己,为自己感到自豪。任何削弱这些自我价值感的评论或经历都会让人不舒服,想要避免它们是很自然的。但问题在于,你的自我价值是否真的受到了削弱,在很大程度上是主观的。这在很大程度上取决于你对某人所说或所做之事的理解。

paragraphs.en: When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person. Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a [5] member of staff. Or, two of your friends cancel your [6] get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you. Psychologists have a [7] for this way of thinking: personalisation.
paragraphs.zh: 当你把事情往心里去时,你是在将这些情况理解为关于你这个人的某种重要且负面的东西。比如你的老板在你的销售报告中挑毛病,你离开时感觉这意味着她认为你是个糟糕的员工。或者,你的两个朋友取消了你们计划好的酒吧聚会,你将此理解为他们对你感到厌倦了。心理学家对这种思维方式有一个术语:个人化。

paragraphs.en: But the [8] is that your boss might view you very highly. It's just you made some [9] in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time. [10] , in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just [11] their minds.
paragraphs.zh: 但现实是,你的老板可能对你评价很高。只是你在报告中犯了一些错误,她想指出这些错误,以便你下次做得更好。同样,在你朋友取消聚会的情况下,也许他们俩那个周末都感觉不舒服,或者他们只是改变了主意。

paragraphs.en: In both [12] — and others that we all experience — there's another [13] at work that psychologists call mind reading. This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you, when you can't really know without [14] them directly.
paragraphs.zh: 在这两个例子中——以及我们都会经历的其他例子中——还有另一个心理学家称之为读心术的过程在起作用。这是指你假设自己知道别人对你的想法,而实际上如果不直接询问他们,你是无法真正知道的。

paragraphs.en: One simple way to avoid [15] personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's [16] . When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you — especially in the sense of saying anything deep or [17] about you.
paragraphs.zh: 避免陷入个人化和读心术的一个简单方法是质疑你对所发生事情的负面假设。当你发现自己把某个情况往心里去时,试着想想其他不那么关注你的解释——尤其是在说关于你任何深层或根本性东西的意义上。

paragraphs.en: When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes. The fact your boss took the time to give you [18] at all means they care enough to want to help you [19] . When it comes to your friends — maybe it's because your friendship is so [20] that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
paragraphs.zh: 当你这样做时,试着设身处地为他人着想可能会有所帮助。你的老板花时间给你反馈这一事实本身就意味着他们足够在意,想要帮助你进步。至于你的朋友——也许正是因为你们的友谊如此牢固,他们才觉得可以在最后时刻取消。
